Eager construction errors for source-file -n remain under mux.chain-parse-abort, and empty or multi-command alias execution remains under aliases.command-bodies. No protocol change was needed.

closed.title: Prepare Control commands against live aliases
closed.resolution: Protocol v74 appends request-correlated PrepareCommandList and PreparedCommandList messages and a prepared bit on CommandRequest. The daemon prepares each complete input vector under one mux lock, expanding exactly one live alias layer, preserving source and caller arguments, returning canonical identity plus alias-match and typed error state, and performing no execution, target or format resolution, hook emission, message publication, or authorization. Control prepares the initial argv unit before its flags-0 result and every complete LF line before any flags-1 frame, preserves bare initial unknown errors, whole-line parse-error framing, numbering, ignored lines, queued stdin, and interleaved notifications, then executes the immutable prepared invocations without a second alias lookup. Each request carries a nonzero request id, stale replies are ignored, every ClientKind handles the RPC, and a prepared line keeps the alias snapshot even when an earlier command mutates command-alias. The prepared bit is an internal freeze marker rather than an authority token: a forged prepared request bypasses alias lookup by design but still passes the ordinary read-only authorization gate, and a destructive forged request from a read-only client is rejected without mutation. Local ordinary CLI preprocessing is closed under aliases.client-preflight; remote preprocessing remains under aliases.remote-client-preflight, and actual empty and multi-command alias bodies remain under aliases.command-bodies.

closed.title: Refuse unsupported matched alias bodies
closed.resolution: MuxEngine::resolve_command_alias now returns Miss, Expanded, or MatchedUnsupported with empty, multiple-command, and unparsable reasons. Every mux and daemon construction entry point converts a matched unsupported body to `unknown command: <typed name>` instead of falling through to a shadowed canonical name or catalog alias. Direct execution, daemon routing, terminal-qualified replay, bind-key and set-hook storage, option-command normalization, and read-only preflight share that result. Stored bind-key and set-hook command lists execute the commands constructed for storage without another user-alias lookup; read-only clients authorize the same frozen list as one all-or-nothing chain before effects. Typed `if-shell`, `run-shell`, and `confirm-before` callbacks are likewise frozen after lexical construction. Typed `if-shell` and `run-shell` callbacks preserve physical groups: a failed group stops its remaining commands while later physical lines continue; string callbacks remain one group. Typed `command-prompt` templates retain their structured constructed command list through submission without another user-alias lookup. String templates substitute raw source before a fresh parse and complete construction pass against the then-current alias table. Both prompt paths replace the first `%%` and every `%1`, with trailing-percent quoting; typed substitution preserves leaf-argument boundaries and physical groups, while string templates and free input form one group. `set-hook` and command-valued native set-option intentionally apply their documented second construction stage. A selected typed `display-menu` action drops its structural wrapper before its fresh construction stage, while a quoted brace string remains literal. Alias-resolution failures use the same command-output and key-command-failed path as other per-command failures. Focused regressions prove `kill-server=`, multi-command `list-windows` and `lsw` shadows, and an unparsable `kill-session` shadow cannot shut down, list, kill a session, replace a binding, install a hook, or change an option command. Each construction path admits one user-alias layer, and a malformed shadow refuses before read-only authorization. `aliases.command-bodies` remains open for actual empty and multi-command execution; local CLI preprocessing is closed under aliases.client-preflight, while remote preprocessing remains under aliases.remote-client-preflight.

closed.title: Route buffer files through client path context
closed.resolution: load-buffer and save-buffer now route their file through the client that invoked them, the way file_read and file_write do. The daemon expands the path exactly once in its own format context, a leading ~/ against the server's own home and anything else relative against server_client_get_cwd(c, NULL) — the config client during startup, an unattached client's own working directory, then that client's attached session cwd, then home. An unattached command client then does the bounded read, or the create-truncate or -a append, on its own host over the protocol v89 ClientFileRequest/ClientFileResponse pair, correlated by request id and released when the connection ends; an attached Interactive or Control client keeps daemon-side IO, as the pin keeps server-side IO for an attached client. Failures read `strerror: path` the way cmd-load-buffer.c and cmd-save-buffer.c print them, and a client-side read that fails after the open reports Input/output error, which is what the pin's bufferevent path reports. The client reports its working directory the way find_cwd does, preferring PWD when it resolves to the same place as getcwd. Eleven focused CLI tests drive a daemon whose directory and home are deliberately not the client's; the two three-step differentials run seven and nine checks per engine over relative, nested, tilde, absolute, append, truncate, and failure paths.

closed.title: Honor buffer clipboard writes
closed.resolution: load-buffer -w and set-buffer -w now write the stored buffer to the selected client's clipboard. The target follows the pin's CMD_CLIENT_TFLAG plus CMD_CLIENT_CANFAIL rule: -t picks an attached client, no -t picks the current one, and an unresolvable -t is quiet and still stores the buffer. As in cmd-set-buffer.c and cmd-load-buffer.c the write goes straight to that one client and never through the set-clipboard gate that guards the application OSC 52 path, so it fires with set-clipboard off and raises no pane-set-clipboard hook; -a writes the joined buffer the way the pin writes bufdata. A client that advertises no clipboard terminal feature is the pin's Ms-less client: the command succeeds, stores the buffer, and writes nothing. That mapping is wider than the pin's: zz's client_term_features reports clipboard for any colour-capable client, so in zz only a Control client is the Ms-less case, and a pty client whose terminal lacks the pin's Ms capability (a TERM=vt100 client gets no OSC 52 from the pin) would still receive the write from zz. The scenario attaches a real pty client beside a control client on both binaries and compares the decoded OSC 52 payload stream, which matched on all ten checks. zz still encodes the selection field as `c` where the pin sends the empty field, and a non-UTF-8 buffer is not written because the wire clipboard payload is a String.

closed.title: Read and write buffer standard streams
closed.resolution: Closed semantic:buffer-standard-streams, relocated from protocol.binary-streams. Pinned d77c9dc6 cmd-load-buffer.c and cmd-save-buffer.c plus smoke/buffer-standard-streams prove binary stdin/stdout (61 00 62 ff), named -b loads, save-buffer -a - without byte modification, file append, empty-input preservation, built-in aliases and compact options. Literal load-buffer - on the command CLI reads at most 1,048,576 bytes through read_stdin_payload and transports one RawText payload after the validated path arguments; oversized stdin is refused, while the pin is unbounded. save-buffer stdout skips the CLI line terminator; file append keeps its existing path. No wire type changes. Config/Control load-buffer - without a command client's payload and paths that only expand to '-' still refuse rather than reading the daemon's stdin; binary stdin through a multi-command alias body remains outside this bounded literal-CLI proof.

closed.title: Complete chooser command controls
closed.resolution: Measured against the pin on 2026-09-01 through clients attached on real ptys, because a chooser only answers a client that is attached to it. -F is expanded once per visible row in that row's own context and becomes the text the row draws: window_tree_build_session, _window and _pane pass the product to mode_tree_add as the row text, window_buffer_build does the same in each paste-buffer's context, and the row keeps its shortcut, its order and its target. The board recipe claimed #{line} is part of that context; it is not. format_add(ft, "line") is only in window_tree_get_key and window_buffer_get_key, so #{line} belongs to -K and expands empty inside -F; measured with choose-tree -F '<L#{line}|P#{pane_id}>' on an attached 80x24 client, which drew '<L|P%0>'. zz now expands -F the same way and carries the product as ChooseTreeItem.text and ChooseBufferItem.text on protocol v93, empty when the command had no -F; the raw TUI draws it in place of the label/detail and name/size/preview row it composes otherwise, and the GPUI chooser substitutes it for the row's primary text and drops the secondary columns. -h drops the invoking pane's own row: window_tree_build_window counts the filtered panes first and skips the source only afterwards, so a window whose only match is the source keeps its row with no pane children, the session row is untouched, and a selection that would have landed on the hidden row falls to the first row while a single-pane source window keeps the window row it already started on. -k is stored on the mode entry and read by window_pane_reset_mode, which kills the pane the chooser was entered on after the mode is freed, on cancel, on Enter, on a row shortcut, and when the buffer chooser closes because its last buffer was deleted; the chosen template still runs, and it runs after the kill: window_tree_key and window_buffer_key append the template with mode_tree_run_command and then call window_pane_reset_mode, whose server_kill_pane is synchronous, so a two-pane window whose -k chooser runs `run-shell 'echo #{window_panes}'` on Enter writes 1 on the pin. zz ran the template first and wrote 2 until the cycle-6 gate reordered it; the scenario now measures that count, and a buffer paste whose source pane died falls to the client's current pane the way the pin's queued paste-buffer resolves against it. choose-buffer parses -y and never reads it, since window_buffer_init copies only -F, -K and the template and buffer-mode deletes without a prompt, so the flag is accepted and inert alone, clustered and repeated. Two divergences stay recorded rather than copied. zz's chooser is a per-client overlay and not a pane-mode stack, so a client that detaches drops the chooser instead of leaving it and the -k pane survives, which is what the pin does too because the mode outlives the detach; but raising another overlay retires zz's chooser outright where the pin keeps the mode underneath and kills the pane only when it is finally left, so a -k chooser replaced by an overlay never kills its pane in zz. While probing that, display-menu -c on a client that already has a chooser open was measured to leave the client's keys with the chooser in zz: the menu item never ran and 'q' cancelled the chooser instead, where the pin's menu takes the key and leaves the mode alone. flag:choose-tree:-y stays open: its only consumer on the pin is the PROMPT_ACCEPT that auto-answers the 'Kill session/window/pane?' prompt raised by x and X, and zz's choose-tree table delivers neither key, so accepting the flag would claim a semantic zz has no place to spend. semantic:chooser-key-vocabulary stays open with the same measurement: the pin's mode_tree_key also answers t, T, C-t, K, J, S-Up, S-Down, O, r, F1, C-h, M-- and M-+, and window_tree_key adds m, x, X and ':', none of which zz's choose-tree or choose-buffer tables name. Sized again on 2026-09-02 without being closed, and the sizing is the useful part. zz's chooser keys are not a switch in the daemon: choose_tree_key_action and choose_buffer_key_action in crates/zz-daemon/src/keys.rs resolve the pressed key through the shared `choose-tree` and `choose-buffer` key tables and then map the resolved `send-keys -X <name>` to a ChooseTreeAction or ChooseBufferAction. So the pin's vocabulary lands in three places at once: the key tables in crates/zz-protocol/src/key.rs would gain rows for t, T, C-t, K, J, S-Up, S-Down, O, r, F1, C-h, M-- and M-+ from mode_tree_key plus m, x, X and ':' from window_tree_key; ChooseTreeAction and ChooseBufferAction would gain the matching variants and take a protocol bump; and the daemon chooser session would gain tagging, swap, sort order, reverse, the help overlay, collapse-all and expand-all, the mark toggle, and the two kill keys with the confirm prompt they raise. flag:choose-tree:-y is the PROMPT_ACCEPT on that prompt and cannot be accepted before x and X exist. mode_tree_key's own shape matters for whoever picks this up: the row shortcut table is consulted before the switch, so a row whose shortcut is one of these letters wins the key; 't' untags every parent and child of the current row before tagging it and only advances the cursor for a mouse press; C-t tags every row whose parent is absent or itself untaggable and untags every other; K and S-Up call mode_tree_swap(-1) and J and S-Down mode_tree_swap(1); O steps the sort order and r flips its direction, both followed by a rebuild; F1 and C-h open the help screen, which the next key of any kind closes; and M-- and M-+ collapse or expand every top-level item rather than the current one. Read against the pin again on 2026-09-02 and left open after its budget, with four corrections to the sizing above and the real blocker named. The blocker is the prompt. Both remaining keys that matter, x and X, and ':' too, raise a prompt through mode_tree_set_prompt, and that prompt belongs to the MODE - mtd->prompt, drawn inside the mode's own screen and answered by mode_tree_key before anything else - not to the client. zz has no prompt that belongs to an overlay: command_prompts is a per-client slot and popup_other_overlay_present already counts choose_trees, so a command prompt cannot be raised while a chooser is open. The shape that fixes it is the one display-popup's context menu just took: an overlay that owns its own nested overlay, inserted by the overlay rather than through the command, with the client's existing route drawing it on top. The command gate itself is right and must not be relaxed - cmd_display_menu_exec returns immediately when tc->overlay_draw is set - but a chooser is a pane mode on the pin and not an overlay, which is why display-menu over a chooser draws there and is refused over a popup. Corrections. The kill prompts carry their target: 'Kill session %s? ' with the session name, 'Kill window %u? ' with the winlink index and 'Kill pane %u? ' with the pane index from window_tree_key's x arm, and 'Kill %u tagged? ' from X, which does nothing at all when mode_tree_count_tagged is zero. ':' raises '(%u tagged) ' when anything is tagged and '(current) ' otherwise. -y is PROMPT_ACCEPT and mode_tree_set_prompt only queues mode_tree_prompt_accept when PROMPT_SINGLE is set alongside it, which x and X pass and ':' does not, so -y auto-answers the two kill prompts and never the command prompt. O steps a per-mode sequence rather than one list: window_tree_order_seq is index, name, activity, z and window_buffer_order_seq is creation, name, size, and sort_next_order wraps from the end and also from an order that is not in the sequence at all. And the vocabulary is wider than the enumeration above on the buffer side: window_buffer_key adds 'e' (edit the buffer in an editor), 'd' (delete the current buffer), 'D' (delete every tagged buffer) and 'P' (paste every tagged buffer) on top of mode_tree_key, so tagging is load-bearing there too. flag:choose-tree:-y closed on 2026-09-03 with the prompt it needed. The shape is the one the popup context menu took: the prompt belongs to the overlay, not to the client. `ChooseTreeSession` gained a `prompt` slot beside its `tagged` set, `input_choose_tree` answers that slot before it resolves the pressed key through the `choose-tree` table, and the prompt dies with the chooser because it lives on the chooser. `command_prompts` was not touched, so the gate `cmd_display_menu_exec` keeps is unchanged and no command prompt can still be raised over a chooser. The vocabulary that landed with it is t, T, C-t, x and X, on protocol v97: `ChooseTreeAction` gained `Tag`, `TagNone`, `TagAll`, `KillCurrent` and `KillTagged` after `Key`, `ChooseTreeState` gained `prompt` after `filter_no_matches`, and `ChooseTreeItem.flags` gained `TAGGED = 1 << 3`; the raw TUI draws the prompt above the rows and a `*` on a tagged row, and the GPUI chooser draws the same prompt as a band under its header and a TAGGED chip on a tagged row. Both clients must draw it: every key still goes to the daemon while the prompt stands, so a client that renders neither answers a kill its viewer never saw. `-y` moved from `unsupported_flag` to a real flag in catalog.rs, one step on the (supported, unsupported) counters, which the cycle-11 integration left at (471, 32) once the formats lane's `display-message -v` took its own step, and puts `y` into zz's own usage string; the pinned usage is unchanged, because `cmd_choose_tree_entry` carries `y` in its args string `F:f:GhK:kNO:rst:wyZ` and never in its usage text, so choose-tree keeps its PINNED_TMUX_USAGE_OVERRIDES row and the override count stays 20. The five new key rows are zz-only default bindings the way every other chooser row is, because the pin hard-codes the mode-tree keys in mode-tree.c instead of binding them, so they were registered as native-key:choose-tree:t, :T, :C-t, :x and :X in keys.native-defaults and the manifest's zz and native binding counts moved from 268 and 58 to 273 and 63. Measured on both binaries on 2026-09-03 with one client attached on a real pty to a five-window session, driving keys through chooser-drive.py and reading back either the `%%` target the template wrote or the window list: `x` on a window row raises the prompt and the Enter that follows is eaten by it, so nothing is activated and nothing is killed; `n` closes the prompt and leaves the chooser there, so the next Enter activates the row; `y` kills the row and leaves the mode open on the same line, which is the next row's target after the kill; `t` then `X` raises the tagged prompt, which eats Enter the same way; `X` with nothing tagged is inert, so Enter activates; `T` puts it back to inert; `C-t` tags the session row, the only row whose parent is absent in a tree filtered to one session, so `X` prompts without a `t`; and with `-y` both `x` and `X` kill with no answer key at all. Those 15 answers are compat/scenarios/smoke/chooser-kill-keys.txt. Two corrections to the sizing this record carried. The first: `t` advances the cursor on a keyboard press, not only on a mouse press. `mode_tree_key`'s `t` arm guards the `mode_tree_down` on `m != NULL`, and `server_client_handle_key` hands `window_pane_key` the client's own `mouse_event` for every key, so the pointer is never null and the row moves down after every tag; measured as the pin answering the row below the tagged one where this record predicted the tagged one. zz advances the same way. The second: `mtd->current` is a line index, so a row a kill emptied keeps its place; zz's chooser remembered the selected target instead and fell back to the source pane's row when it vanished, and it now carries the row index across a kill's rebuild. The prompt strings themselves - 'Kill session %s? ', 'Kill window %u? ', 'Kill pane %u? ' and 'Kill %u tagged? ' - are built from window_tree_key's own arms but are not differentially provable, because they are drawn inside the mode's screen and the raw TUI's chooser is not cell-comparable with the pin's; the probe proves the prompt's existence and its answer rule instead. semantic:chooser-key-vocabulary stays open with the rest of the vocabulary sized and unbuilt: K, J, S-Up and S-Down (mode_tree_swap), O and r (the per-mode order sequence window_tree_order_seq index/name/activity/z and window_buffer_order_seq creation/name/size, with sort_next_order wrapping from an order outside the sequence too), F1 and C-h (the help screen the next key of any kind closes), M-- and M-+ (collapse or expand every top-level item), m and M (the mark), ':' (the command prompt, which carries '(%u tagged) ' or '(current) ' and which -y never answers because it does not pass PROMPT_SINGLE), and window_buffer_key's e, d, D and P on top of mode_tree_key, where D and P need the same tagging the tree chooser now has. Decided 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator under fabrico's instruction to close the campaign; reversible. semantic:chooser-key-vocabulary closed on 2026-09-04 with the rest of the vocabulary built and measured on both binaries through clients attached on real ptys, in compat/scenarios/smoke/chooser-tree-vocabulary.txt (21 checks) and compat/scenarios/smoke/chooser-buffer-vocabulary.txt (14 checks). Protocol v98 carries it: ChooseTreeAction gained SwapUp, SwapDown, SortNext, SortReverse, Help, CollapseAll, ExpandAll, Mark, MarkClear and CommandPrompt after KillTagged; ChooseBufferAction gained Tag, TagNone, TagAll, SortNext, SortReverse, Help, CollapseAll, ExpandAll, DeleteTagged and PasteTagged after Key; ChooseTreeState and ChooseBufferState each gained help: bool and ChooseBufferItem gained tagged: bool. The 22 new key rows are zz-only default bindings the way every other chooser row is, so they are recorded in keys.native-defaults and the manifest's zz and native binding counts moved from 273 and 63 to 295 and 85. What the pin answered, measured. K and J are mode_tree_swap over window_tree_swap: two window rows of one session trade slots, and unlike cmd_swap_window_exec the mode moves curw so the same window stays current, which is why zz needed MuxState::swap_windows_keeping_current beside swap_windows rather than the swap-window command; a window row with only the session row above it, and the last row, both refuse, and so does any pair the sort order would reorder (sort_would_window_tree_swap allows an index order outright and otherwise only a pair that compares equal). O steps window_tree_order_seq index, name, activity, z and wraps at the end and from an order outside the sequence, r flips the reversal, and both rebuild. M-- and M-+ collapse or expand every top-level item rather than the current one, so M-- over a single-session tree leaves that session's own row alone in it and Enter answers '=SESSION:'. F1 and C-h raise mode_tree_display_help, and the next key of any kind closes it and does nothing else: 'q' after F1 does not cancel the chooser, and the Enter after that still activates the row. m is server_set_marked on the pane window_tree_pull_item resolves - a window row's active pane - which is a plain set and not select-pane -m's toggle, and M is server_clear_marked; measured through #{pane_marked}. ':' raises the mode's own command prompt, an edited line rather than a single key, and window_tree_command_each runs it once per tagged row and only falls back to the current row when nothing is tagged: with the rows for windows 1 and 2 tagged and the cursor on window 3, 'set-environment -g CHOOSER_ROW %%' answered =SESSION:2. on both binaries. -y does not answer it, because mode_tree_set_prompt queues PROMPT_ACCEPT only alongside PROMPT_SINGLE and the ':' arm passes neither that nor data->prompt_flags: under -y an 'x' typed after ':' is text in the line and kills nothing. On the buffer side window_buffer_key's D and P are mode_tree_each_tagged with no fallback to the current row, so D deletes nothing when nothing is tagged while P still closes the mode having pasted nothing; t, T and C-t tag the flat rows they walk, and window_buffer_order_seq is creation, name, size with creation newest first. Four divergences and one correction, all measured. The correction first, because it contradicts what this record said in cycle 11: mtd->current is not simply a line index across a rebuild. mode_tree_build saves the current row's tag and restores the cursor onto that item, so after O reorders the tree the pin's Enter still answers the row the cursor was on, not the row that moved under it; the buffer scenario reads an order from the first row after a 'g' for exactly that reason. The cycle-11 pending_row behaviour after a kill is unaffected, because there the item is gone. First divergence: S-Up and S-Down cannot be delivered by zz at all. input_key_name folds shift into a name only for a character key (it uppercases an ascii letter), so a shift+Up press names 'Up' and does cursor-up, where the pin's tty_keys names it S-Up and runs mode_tree_swap. K and J carry the swap on both binaries and are what the scenario measures. Emitting 'S-' for every special key is a change to the shared key contract that every table and every client would feel, not a chooser change, so it is recorded rather than built: decided 2026-09-04 by the orchestrator under fabrico's instruction to close the campaign; reversible. Second: window_buffer_key's 'e' is window_buffer_start_edit, which spawns $EDITOR on the buffer in a job and writes what comes back into it. zz has no editor-job path for a paste buffer, so 'e' is unbound in the choose-buffer table and inert; decided 2026-09-04 by the orchestrator under fabrico's instruction to close the campaign; reversible. Third: mode_tree_start passes no swapcb for the buffer mode, so K, J, S-Up and S-Down are inert on the pin's buffer chooser; zz binds none of them there, which matches. window_buffer_key also has no 'm', 'M' or ':' arm and mode_tree_key has none either, so those three stay tree-only in zz too. Fourth, on the desktop client, which the cycle-11 reviewer was right to ask about: the GPUI chooser still forwards every key to the daemon with no local filtering, so every key added here reaches it. ':' and the line typed into it ride ChooseTreeState.prompt, which ChooserModal already draws as a band under its header, so the command prompt is visible before it runs; the help screen is a new band on the same modal, so the key it swallows is not swallowed silently; a tagged buffer row now draws the TAGGED chip its tree counterpart already had; K, J, O, r and m rebuild rows the viewer can see, and D removes rows in place. The one key the desktop client cannot deliver is M-+: gpui names the unshifted physical key, so alt+shift+= arrives as 'M-=' on a US layout and resolves to nothing, while the raw TUI's ESC '+' names 'M-+' and works. M-- works on both. That is a client-side fold gap with no destructive edge, recorded here rather than fixed. Two defects the cycle-12 reviewer found on this branch were fixed at the gate before it merged, each proved by reverting the fix and watching the new fixture rows go red on zz alone while the pin stayed clean. ':' ran its line against the client's ExecutionContext, so only the %% substitution carried the row and a target-less command acted on the client's own window: with the cursor on window 1 and 'rename-window colonrow' typed at the prompt, the pin renamed window 1 and zz renamed window 0. window_tree_command_each hands mode_tree_run_command the row's own cmd_find_state (window_tree_get_target calls cmd_find_from_winlink_pane, and a session row resolves to that session's current window and its active pane, a window row to the window's active pane), so choose_tree_target_context now resolves each row and the daemon retargets the execution context per run, restoring the client's own target afterwards. And swap_windows_keeping_current restored active_window over swap_windows' slot remap but left last_window pointing at the window that is current, a state the pin never has: window_tree_swap moves curw through session_set_current, which drops the destination slot off the last stack and pushes the slot the current window vacated, so the session's last window is the other member of the swapped pair. Measured on the pin with windows 1:w0 2:w1 3:w2, active w0 and last w1, and 'C-o g j j K': #{?window_active,*,}#{?window_last_flag,-,} reads '1:w1- 2:w0* 3:w2' where zz answered '1:w1 2:w0*-', so select-window -l after a chooser swap was a no-op on the current window. Both are pinned differentially by three new rows in smoke/chooser-tree-vocabulary, which reads clean:24 on both binaries, and the swap half also by crates/zz-mux/src/command.rs chooser_swap_leaves_the_other_window_of_the_pair_as_last. On 2026-09-05 keys.shift-modifier superseded the old delivery limitation "S-Up and S-Down cannot be delivered by zz at all": both clients now deliver these names, proven by smoke/keys-shift-attached. This changes input naming, not the chooser default rows; K and J remain the previously proven swap bindings.

closed.title: Keep native chooser input client-scoped
closed.resolution: Choose-tree and choose-buffer now account each writable native action or raw key exactly once against the source session, advance that client as the latest geometry owner, and preserve pane bells. A raw key routes through chooser bindings only when that same client owns the chooser; another client's key follows its own ordinary input path. Read-only raw keys bypass the retained chooser into normal root-table resolution, while read-only dedicated chooser actions and rejected terminal-view input update activity and latest geometry before rejection without clearing the bell. Read-only-safe local view actions also bypass the retained chooser, reach the pane, and account exactly once. Activating a different session records the source-session input first and then the target-session attach, preserving the pin's two legitimate activity boundaries. Pane Focus and ClearLinkHover remain outside chooser activity accounting.

closed.title: Align chooser result feedback
closed.resolution: Protocol v72 appends a durable filter_no_matches bit to both chooser states. A full daemon rebuild sets it only when an explicit static -f filter produced no rows and the chooser restored its unfiltered rows; a matching filter or no filter clears it, while incremental search and selection deltas preserve it. TUI and GUI render the native status `filter: no matches` without replacing the selectable fallback rows. The GUI reserves its 46px shortcut cell for every rendered row only when at least one rendered row has a nonempty key, and removes the cell for a fully keyless list, matching the TUI's list-level gutter decision. The real attached-client fixture requires the status independently on the current tree and buffer chooser screens for both zz and pinned tmux. Native layout differences remain under choosers.native-presentation, while key vocabulary remains under choosers.command-flags.

closed.title: Seed and refresh client environments
closed.resolution: Protocol v82 appends a bounded environment snapshot to ClientHello for local and SSH-forwarded clients. The client sorts and deduplicates up to 4,096 valid UTF-8 NAME=VALUE entries within a 4 MiB aggregate limit; the codec enforces the same count, entry, syntax, and aggregate bounds, and debug output reports only the entry count. The daemon retains one immutable snapshot per connection and removes it on unregister. Fresh new-session copies names selected by the effective update-environment array from the invoking client unless -E, writes unset markers for selected missing names, expands wildcard patterns, preserves empty values, replaces selected hidden entries as ordinary values, then applies repeated -e overlays. Existing new-session -A follows attach behavior, honors -E, and ignores -e. attach-session refreshes only after target and terminal preflight, while the native attach path and Control clients use the same update. The exact native attach parser accepts separate or bundled -E and routes the initial attachment through the daemon command path, preserving the session environment; its automatic reconnect behavior remains unchanged. switch-client refreshes from the selected target client's snapshot rather than an external command caller; -T exits before refresh and -E preserves the session environment. Existing processes keep their startup environment, future panes consume the refreshed session map, and the session values survive client disconnect. Focused protocol, mux, and daemon tests plus the full attached-client differential pass against pinned tmux d77c9dc6, including exact, missing, empty, wildcard, hidden, Control, PTY, -A, -E, targeted-switch, and disconnect cases. A native PTY integration test independently proves -E preservation followed by ordinary attach refresh. Non-UTF-8 Unix environment entries remain visible under clients.path-encoding rather than being substituted.

closed.title: Retain requested client flags across attachment
closed.resolution: attach-session -f and attaching new-session -f now retain the final comma-separated client-flag mutation string in typed daemon state. Common flags are read-only, ignore-size, active-pane, and no-detach-on-destroy; Control clients also apply no-output, wait-exit, and pause-after with the pin's unsigned numeric-prefix and wrapping behavior. Unknown and empty names are ignored, ! clears except that read-only cannot clear itself, repeated -f keeps the last argument, missing targets do not mutate, terminal-open failure retains an existing-target mutation, detached creation ignores flags, and successful -A follows the attach path. State survives session switches and detach, clears on client unregister or replacement, and exact native and TUI reconnect paths replay only the mutation actually applied by a successful attaching command. Protocol v81 and the wire schema are unchanged. The fresh debug attached-client differential passes against the pinned tmux binary, including the accepted zz divergence that -r adds only read-only rather than tmux's coupled ignore-size. Flag retention and ignore-size consumption closed in this slice; the later clients.no-detach-on-destroy closure consumes the destruction fallback, while active-pane behavior remains under clients.active-pane.

closed.title: Retain session cwd across attachment
closed.resolution: Each session now retains one daemon-local working directory, seeded in precedence order from explicit new-session -c, the attached source session, then the caller cwd. attach-session -c resolves the exact target first, selects a compound target's window and pane, expands in that pane context, and stores the result before terminal validation; a missing target does not mutate state, while terminal-open failure does not roll the mutation back. Exact native attach-session -c enters the existing Interactive attach path, and the full debug attached-client differential separates command cwd from session cwd with decoys before passing for zz and pinned tmux. A focused daemon test adds a third source-file -t target cwd decoy. Attached source-file and reload-config now prefer the invoking client's attached session cwd while -t remains only the format and replay target; nested replay keeps that selected base. Focused mux, daemon, catalog, and native CLI tests pass. This uses internal mux and daemon state without a protocol, snapshot-schema, or format-vocabulary change. Requested attach flags and retained-client sizing later closed under clients.attach-flags and clients.attach-sizing; session_path later closed under formats.session-path.

closed.title: Aggregate retained attached-client sizes
closed.resolution: resize-window -A and -a now perform one-shot component-wise largest and smallest aggregation over eligible retained client geometry, with full target and numeric validation before sizing and -A winning when both flags are present. Interactive clients use retained outer terminal size minus their effective status rows, GUI clients fall back to projected full-window pane geometry, and Control clients count only after refresh-client -C; a per-window Control size overrides its global size and hard-clamps each aggregate dimension. Detached, unrelated-session, and Command clients do not count. Explicit ignore-size follows tmux's global fallback rule: ignored clients are excluded while any attached unignored client exists anywhere, then become eligible when every attached client is ignored. The same rule and Control ceilings now apply to automatic latest, largest, and smallest modes. No eligible target client uses the target session's effective default-size. Final dimensions clamp to 1 through 10000, and the command stores an immediate durable manual extent that later client changes cannot overwrite. The multi-client attached differential uses crossed rectangles to prove component-wise extrema, unrelated exclusion, numeric override, -A precedence, manual freeze, mixed and all-global ignore-size behavior, and default-size fallback against pinned tmux. Focused daemon tests cover Control ceilings, status subtraction, GUI projection, automatic modes, and size limits. The fixture also exposed and closed a pre-existing refresh-client -f seam so targeted Interactive clients now mutate common retained flags. The implementation uses one internal mux effect with no protocol, wire, client, or snapshot-schema change.

closed.title: Carry the client's bytes past the wire
closed.resolution: All three consumers carry the client's bytes now. Format expansion runs on RawText from the environment tail through lookup and expand to every sink that prints an expansion to a client, and the trim, pad and width modifiers were rewritten onto one walk that reproduces format-draw.c's: a byte that opens no complete UTF-8 sequence and is not printable ASCII takes no column, format_trim_left drops it even when the value fits, format_trim_right keeps it in that case, n: is strlen and w: is format_width. The client-encoding sanitizer exists for the first time: the client raises tmux's CLIENT_UTF8 for itself out of $TMUX and the first of LC_ALL, LC_CTYPE and LANG that is set, declares it on the hello as a capability string so no wire type moved, and the daemon spends one underscore per column a complete sequence would have drawn over output bound for a command or control client that raised nothing. The gate is the pin's SINK, not the client's kind alone: only a response whose pin twin is cmdq_print or cmdq_print_data is sanitized, so capture-pane -p (file_print_buffer for a command client, control_write for a control one) and save-buffer (file_write for a real path and for -) keep their bytes for every client shape, and show-buffer is sanitized for a control client but not for a session-less command client, which is the only shape zz's Command kind has. A byte-only path argument opens the path it names: MuxEffect::SourceFile and the daemon's SourceFileRequest carry RawText, and -F expands through expand_pane_format_bytes, so source-file runs a config file whose name a UTF-8 string cannot spell. Proved by smoke/environment-bytes at clean:18, the new smoke/client-utf8-sanitizer at clean:11, whose last row pins capture-pane -p answering 78 e6 bc a2 79 0a to a C-locale client on both binaries and the new smoke/source-file-byte-name at clean:4, all on both binaries, plus four pin-derived unit tests. What is left is listed here, and in the divergences page this record names: the s/// modifier, the #{Ve:} loop, cmdq_error's twin of the sanitizer, a newline inside one message, the missing-path diagnostic, load-buffer and save-buffer, and the passwd half of the tilde, the last three of which need ClientFileRequest.path or ClientMessage.text to become byte-capable and so need a protocol bump. The seven measurements that did not close are written up under 'What the byte-clean consumers still lose (2026-09-04)' in knowledge/tmux/divergences.md.

closed.title: Preserve command-client output bytes
closed.resolution: Retrospective finding 15 had no slug. Pinned d77c9dc6 cmd-display-message.c calls cmdq_print, which writes a line even when empty, while cmd-save-buffer.c uses file_write for a command client's show-buffer. The old CLI returned immediately on empty output and appended a newline to every nonempty result. The new stance adopts exact printed-line and buffer stdout boundaries; decided 2026-09-05 by the orchestrator under fabrico's instruction to continue the campaign past the frozen scope; reversible. The existing copy-mode-mode-keys-tail fixture explicitly routed through save-buffer to avoid show-buffer's extra LF; the client-loop fixture's command substitution hid the empty result's missing LF. show-buffer's non-UTF-8 refusal remains in protocol.binary-streams. Closed semantic:cli-output-byte-fidelity: the differential fixture asserts empty display is 0a, existing message LF receives an additional terminator, literal display remains literal, show-buffer emits exactly five stored bytes and preserves a stored LF, and three sourced print commands emit 0a 6c 69 6e 65 0a 0a. The final mixed-queue measurement asserts the known per-side difference and belongs solely to the new open clients.cli-output-mixed-queue group; it is not a claimed parity proof. Both attached fixtures now observe direct bytes instead of the previous workaround or command substitution.

closed.title: Back client format facts
closed.resolution: Protocol v83 appends the originating process id to ClientHello and retains it with existing per-connection tty, environment, geometry, colour scheme, requested flags, focus, attachment, activity, and creation state. The daemon derives the pin's 26 client format facts plus session_last_attached from that retained state, the active key table, Control geometry, terminal cell metrics, and reliable-mailbox byte counters. Interactive clients expose tty, size, cell, colour, terminal-feature, theme, UTF-8, identity, and session values. client_flags reports attached, the current focused state, requested flags, Control mode state, and UTF-8 in pinned order. Piped Control clients keep tmux's defined empty height, cell, colour, feature, type, theme, and tty fields while explicit refresh-client -C supplies width; terminal-backed Control can expose a retained tty. Unavailable terminal type remains empty, missing TERM becomes unknown, zero counters remain numeric, and clientless contexts retain only session facts. One shared client-fact selection path serves list-clients, ordinary commands, foreground inserted commands, status rendering, and display-message, including the highest-activity target-session client with oldest-created tie precedence when -c is absent. The real attached-client differential passes against pinned tmux d77c9dc6 for list, explicit and implicit display, an attached key binding through run-shell -C, status, Interactive empties, Control empties, and session_last_attached. The CLI suite checks flags by membership so pinned focused and UTF-8 additions do not become false regressions.

closed.title: Carry the caller working directory
closed.resolution: Protocol v72 carries a bounded cwd only for local endpoints; top-level command-client source-file resolves after -F and before globbing. Exact attached session-cwd selection later closed under clients.attach-session-cwd.

closed.title: Execute a command after detaching a client
closed.resolution: detach-client -E now takes a shell command and reaches the presentation process as the protocol v91 ClientExitAction::Exec carried on the Detached event. Victim selection is unchanged, so bare, -t, -a, and -s pick exactly the clients ordinary detach picks; each pty victim is replaced instead of detached, while a Control victim is left attached and running, matching the pin, where MSG_EXEC only acts in the pty client's attached dispatch. The shell is the victim session's default-shell with the pin's _PATH_BSHELL fallback for an unusable value, and the raw-terminal client restores the terminal, then execs `shell -c command` with argv0 from the shell's basename and SHELL exported, printing no detach notice and hanging up no parent, the way client.c runs MSG_EXEC before the exit message. An empty -E is server_client_exec's early return: the victim is neither replaced nor detached. -E wins over -P. The differential attaches a real pty client to both binaries and compares the return code, the exit notice shape, whether the parent saw SIGHUP, the client process's wait status, and the surviving client count for every case; all six observations matched, including exec statuses 7 and 5. The GUI client has no process to replace and reports the command instead.

closed.title: Target and classify client detach
closed.resolution: The catalog accepts detach-client -t, and one no-wire daemon resolver now serves detach-client and switch-client. Explicit targets resolve exact attached client names, native device names, full tty paths, tty paths without /dev/, and one trailing-colon variant before any -s lookup. Without a selector, an attached Interactive or Control client selects itself; a Command client selects the best client on its origin pane's session, then falls back to the best client on the most recently active attached session. detach-client -s wins over -a and quietly does nothing when its source session is missing; -a detaches every attached peer except the resolved target, while bare detach selects only that client. A read-only client may detach only itself. Requested detach publishes the existing Requested reason without a by-client, while attach-session -d eviction retains Evicted; unregister cleanup remains unchanged. Local terminal surfaces always publish a discovered tty, so switch-client and detach-client retain their full-tty and /dev/-stripped aliases even outside nested tmux; remote clients still omit the host tty. The separate client-nested-v1 hello capability is emitted only when TMUX is nonempty and gates nested refusal together with an exact pane-tty match. Focused mux and daemon tests cover parsing, selector and source precedence, origin and fallback selection, aliases, read-only authorization, reasons, victim sets, and nested-marker lifecycle. The attached-client fixture obtains each real outer PTY, targets the client by that tty, and requires the attached client count to reach zero. For nested refusal it removes whitespace from the complete pane history and fixed pin text, snapshots the count of exact normalized substrings before each attempt, requires that count to increase afterward, and holds the attached count at one through a settle for both attach-session and new-session -A. It then proves env -u TMUX admits both paths and uses the retained root tty to detach only the forced nested client. The later clients.tty-basename-targeting closure aligned every supported client-selector caller and removed the display-panes basename widening. The later clients.local-control-terminal-facts closure extended only tty identity and nested intent to a local Control client whose stdin is a terminal. detach-client -E and parent-HUP exit actions remain separate open gaps.

closed.title: Produce client lifecycle hooks
closed.resolution: The daemon now retains the latest attached client for each window and produces client-active, client-focus-in, client-focus-out, client-resized, client-light-theme, and client-dark-theme at their retained report boundaries. client-active fires only when the window's latest client changes; repeated focus, theme, and positive Interactive size reports each fire, even when the retained value is unchanged. Focus-in precedes a resulting active event, resize follows a resulting active event, focus-out never changes the latest client, and loss of the latest client promotes the remaining client with greatest activity before client-detached. Control clients do not originate focus, theme, resize, or input-driven active events, but an attached Control client can win loss promotion. Hooks remain clientless: hook_client identifies the reporter, client notifications expose no hook-specific session variables, copied session, window, and shared active-pane state supplies ordinary target formats, and ordinary client facts keep their independent selection rules. Per-client active-pane behavior remains under clients.active-pane. Focused daemon tests cover all six names, duplicate reports, ordering, suppression, Control exclusions, and loss promotion; the real two-client fixture proves the TUI-drivable active, focus, and resize sequence against pinned tmux without a protocol change. Post-geometry format timing for changed resize reports remains under clients.event-resize-context.

closed.title: Defer client-resized until geometry settles
closed.resolution: Both re-scoped clauses are proved by compat/scenarios/smoke/client-resized-context.txt on both binaries, and the group closes without deferring anything. The report clause holds as measured: one changed Interactive outer resize raises client-resized exactly once with `#{client_width}` current and `#{window_width}x#{window_height}` equal to the geometry the resize replaced, an unchanged report of the same size raises nothing at all, and two Control `refresh-client -C 120,40` connections resize the window to 120x40 while raising neither client-resized nor client-active. The client clause needed the fix the cycle-6 revert asked for. `notify_insert_one_hook` appends a hook body with client NULL, so `cmdq_fire_command` resolves it through `cmd_find_client(item, NULL, 1)` -> `cmd_find_current_client` -> `cmd_find_best_client`, a pure activity_time comparison the MSG_RESIZE arm of server-client.c never updates; the reporting client reaches the body only as `#{hook_client}`. zz now resolves a hook body's format client the same way, through the most recently active session's activity winner rather than through the invoking client, in `format_hook_facts_for_client`. With two pty clients attached and both hooks logging `h:#{hook_client} t:#{client_tty}`, resizing the older client A logs `active h:A t:B` then `resized h:A t:B c:80x24`, and after one key in A, resizing B logs `active h:B t:A` then `resized h:B t:A c:100x30`: the body reads the other client's tty and size while hook_client names the reporter, and the client-active the resize provokes precedes the client-resized, on both binaries. Two identity facts the fixture had to work around are recorded here rather than claimed: zz names a pty client by its tty exactly as the pin does, so client_tty and hook_client are comparable (`#{session_attached_list}` answered the device name in zz when this fixture was written and joins the tty like the pin's loop->name since the display-message.format-listing close in the same batch), and the window geometry a zz hook body sees is smaller than the pin's for the same pty because the raw client reserves chrome, so the fixture compares the lag rather than the measurement. The hook body still carries no format client SESSION: `#{session_active}` stays empty in a zz hook body where the pin answers 1, because `ExecutionContext::has_no_client` forces FormatClient::NoClient; that is a separate producer question and belongs to formats.context-producer-fidelity.

closed.title: Publish local Control terminal facts
closed.resolution: A local Control connection now publishes its bounded working directory plus client-tty-v1 only when stdin has a discoverable tty and client-nested-v1 only when TMUX is nonempty. It does not inspect terminal size, publish client-size-v1, send ClientTerminalSize, infer geometry, retain TERM or terminal-name facts, or expose its tty through ClientFormatFacts. Control geometry remains explicit refresh-client -C state. The established attach-session, new-session -A, and new-session -Ad refusal paths require both the nested marker and a tty that exactly matches a daemon pane when they would attach an existing session. A fresh new-session and a new-session -A miss still create and attach, while duplicate and validation errors keep their existing precedence. Piped Control stdin has no tty identity and is not nested-refused merely because TMUX is set. The change reuses the existing additive hello capability tokens and unregister cleanup, with no field, tag, or protocol-version change. The sequential daemon suite passed 600/600, the focused Control CLI suite passed 30/30, and debug build, strict clippy, and fmt passed. The complete attached-client differential passed for zz and pinned tmux, including terminal-backed Control refusal, fresh-session attachment, and piped-stdin non-refusal. Independent review found the fresh-marker harness sound. This closure makes no canonical-suite claim. Attach sizing later closed under clients.attach-sizing. The protocol v83 clients.context-formats closure exposes retained Control facts and keeps piped-client tty and terminal-only values empty.

closed.title: Separate nested intent from client tty identity
closed.resolution: The additive client-nested-v1 hello capability records whether an eligible local Command or terminal-surface process inherited a nonempty TMUX value; the existing client-tty-v1 value remains unconditional when that process has a discoverable local terminal. The daemon retains both facts independently and refuses attach-session or an attaching new-session -A only when the nested marker is present and the tty exactly matches one of its panes. Unsetting TMUX therefore forces either attach path without deleting the tty needed by ordinary client targeting. Remote endpoints publish neither host tty nor nested marker. Unregister removes both retained facts. This adds no field, tag, or protocol-version change. Focused client and daemon tests cover marker emission, retention, refusal, forced attach, tty targeting, and cleanup. The attached-client fixture removes whitespace from the complete pane history and fixed refusal literal, snapshots the count of exact normalized substrings before each attempt, requires that count to increase afterward, and holds the attached count at one through a settle. The typed commands contain no refusal text, so neither command echo nor the earlier attach-session refusal can satisfy the new-session -A proof, while terminal-query prefixes and physical-line wrapping remain tolerated. The later clients.local-control-terminal-facts closure applies the same two independent facts to local Control only when stdin supplies the tty identity.

closed.title: Honor no-detach-on-destroy per client
closed.resolution: Session destruction now preserves tmux's two-tier survivor choice per client. The configured primary applies to every client. When `on` has no primary, or `no-detached` finds no detached primary, only a client retaining `no-detach-on-destroy` falls back to the newest remaining session; an unflagged peer receives SessionDestroyed, and no remaining session still exits every peer. Focused daemon tests cover mixed clients, detached-primary and attached-fallback cases, no remaining sessions, externally observable attach and detach messages, and unaffected `off`, `previous`, and `next` selection. The real attached-client fixture proves the mixed-client destruction contract against pinned tmux. No protocol or snapshot change was needed.

closed.title: Signal client parents after forced detach
closed.resolution: detach-client -P, attach-session -x, and an attaching new-session -X now evict with the protocol v91 ClientExitAction::ParentHangup instead of an ordinary detach. -x and -X select exactly the peers -d and -D select and only change the action, so the eviction, hooks, and snapshot paths are unchanged. A raw-terminal victim restores its terminal, prints `[detached and SIGHUP (from session NAME)]` where the ordinary notice would have gone, and then sends SIGHUP to its own parent when that parent is not init, matching client.c's kill(getppid(), SIGHUP) after the exit message. Requested and stolen detach notices without the flag are untouched. The differential attaches real pty clients to both binaries and compares the notice shape, whether the fixture process received SIGHUP, the client's wait status, and the surviving client count across nine cases; all nine matched, including detach-client -P, a stealing attach-session -d that stays on the plain notice, attach-session -x, and new-session -A -X.

closed.title: Preserve non-UTF-8 client facts
closed.resolution: The cwd half closed on 2026-09-01. Protocol v92 replaces the UTF-8-only cwd on ClientHello with ClientPath, a bounded byte string that is the client's own OsStr bytes on Unix and UTF-8 everywhere else, and registration rebuilds the exact absolute PathBuf from it. Measured before the change against a client launched in /tmp/cwd-<0xff>-dir: the pin resolved `source-file rel.conf` and zz answered `No such file or directory: rel.conf`, because the client filtered any path whose to_str() was None out of its hello. Both binaries now resolve the direct and nested relative paths, keep a quiet miss at status 0 with empty channels, and keep a loud miss at status 1 on stderr, differentially clean in smoke/client-non-utf8-cwd. Omission is unchanged where it was already correct: a relative cwd is still dropped at registration and a cwd past MAX_CLIENT_WORKING_DIRECTORY_BYTES is still omitted by the client rather than failing the connection, which the encode and decode guards still reject if one is constructed directly. Protocol v82's UTF-8 NAME=VALUE client environment is untouched and still substitutes or drops unrepresentable entries; that half needs its own byte-preserving entry shape plus the pin's update-environment byte behavior. The environment half was measured on ATTACH on 2026-09-02, which is what the earlier `new-session -d` probe could not settle. With `update-environment` naming ZZBYTES and a real pty client launched with ZZBYTES=a<0xff>b, the pin's `show-environment -t <session> ZZBYTES` answers the bytes 5a 5a 42 59 54 45 53 3d 61 ff 62 0a, that is `ZZBYTES=a\xffb` verbatim, and a plain neighbouring variable answers normally; zz answers `-ZZBYTES`, the unset form, because the client filters any entry whose value is not UTF-8 out of its hello before the daemon ever sees it. Not attempted on 2026-09-02, and the reason is scope rather than difficulty: the byte-preserving hello entry is the small half and would follow ClientPath exactly (a bounded byte string with a NAME=VALUE guard, plus protocol 94 -> 95), but the pin's answer above is `show-environment` printing bytes it stored, and zz's session environment is `BTreeMap<String, EnvironmentEntry>` with a `String` value in crates/zz-mux/src/command.rs. Making the second acceptance clause true therefore means making that map byte-clean end to end, through `set-environment`, `environment_line`'s show-environment output, format expansion and the pty spawn environment, which is a command.rs change and not a hello-shape change. Closing the hello half alone would leave the clause unproved, so the item stays open with the measurement recorded here. Re-measured on 2026-09-02 and NOT implemented, and the measurement moves the blocker: the second clause is not a command.rs change and the earlier reading of it was wrong. On a throwaway pin server with no client involved at all, `set-environment -g ZZBYTES $(printf 'a\377b')` then `show-environment -g ZZBYTES` answers 5a 5a 42 59 54 45 53 3d 61 ff 62 0a, the `-s` form answers `ZZBYTES="a\xffb"; export ZZBYTES;` with the byte raw inside the quotes, `display-message -p '#{ZZBYTES}'` answers 61 ff 62 0a, a non-UTF-8 NAME is accepted and printed back raw (`N\xff=plain` in `show-environment -g`), a session store behaves the same, and a pane spawned afterwards inherits 61 ff 62 in its own environment. zz loses the byte before the daemon ever sees it: the same `set-environment` stores `a\u{fffd}b`, `show-environment -g` prints 61 ef bf bd 62 and a spawned pane inherits the same three replacement bytes, because the CLI turns argv into `String`. So the byte has to survive four channels, not one, and three of them are shared wire types every client surface reads: `CommandInvocation { name: String, args: Vec<String> }` for the argv, the session store in crates/zz-mux/src/command.rs, the format value the expander returns, and `Execution::output: String` -> `CommandResponse::Success { output: String }` for what `show-environment` and `display-message -p` print. A `String` cannot hold 0xff, so no lossy display and no command.rs edit reaches the pin's answer; closing this clause needs a byte-capable command output and argv, which is a wire and client-surface change, not a mux one. The hello half is still the small half and still follows ClientPath exactly (a bounded byte string with a NAME=VALUE guard plus protocol 94 -> 95), but landing it alone would spend a protocol version and leave every observable channel unchanged, so it was deliberately left undone rather than half-landed. One divergence found beside this and belonging to the formats groups rather than here: zz has no environment fallback in format expansion at all. Measured on both binaries on 2026-09-02, `set-environment -g PLAIN hello` then `#{PLAIN}` answers `hello` on the pin and empty on zz, `#{HOME}` answers the client's home on the pin and empty on zz, and a session-scoped `set-environment -t <session> SESSPLAIN sv` then `#{SESSPLAIN}` answers `sv` on the pin and empty on zz. That is `format_find`'s `environ_find` tail, and it is also what formats.modifier-fidelity's `#{I:HOME}` fallback clause rests on. 2026-09-02, third look, still NOT implemented, and this entry now carries the measured cost of each of the four channels so the next attempt can be scheduled rather than discovered. (i) The hello entry is small and unchanged in shape: ClientHello.environment becomes a bounded byte string with a NAME=VALUE guard, exactly ClientPath's shape (crates/zz-protocol/src/message.rs), plus the CLI forwarding OsString bytes in crates/zz/src/lib.rs. It costs no protocol version of its own on a branch that already bumps one. (ii) CommandInvocation.args is Vec<String> and crates/zz-mux/src/command.rs alone reads it as &str in 99 places behind 65 `args: &[String]` signatures, all funnelled through one parse_command_options entry point; a byte type cannot Deref to str, so every one of those reads needs a lossy conversion and every command implementation is touched. (iii) The store is BTreeMap<String, EnvironmentEntry> with a String value (command.rs:1672), four construction sites and environment_line as the single printer, which is the cheapest of the four. (iv) Execution.output is a String that becomes CommandResponse::Success { output: String }, mentioned 193 times in crates/zz-daemon, 25 in crates/zz, 5 in crates/zz-tui and 2 in crates/zz-protocol, most of them test constructions that a struct-literal field type change breaks. The order that matters is (i)+(iii) alone change nothing observable -- the byte still dies in argv on the way in and in the output on the way out -- so the same decision as 2026-09-01 holds: it stays open rather than half-landed. The cycle-10 daemon lane spent its budget on the per-connection command worker (control-mode.disconnect-cancels-command-queue) and split-window -W, which is why this was not started; the probes in this reason are the acceptance test and are unchanged. CLOSED 2026-09-04. The three-times-priced four-channel change landed as one branch, and every probe this entry recorded as the acceptance now answers identically on both binaries in smoke/environment-bytes, whose fixture reduces seven byte comparisons to one differential row reading clean:7 on the pin and on zz. Protocol v98 adds RawText to crates/zz-protocol/src/message.rs: a byte string on the wire, serialized and deserialized exactly like ClientPath, that derefs to a lossy &str so the 99 read sites this entry counted needed no rewrite. (i) ClientHello.environment is Vec<RawText> with the NAME=VALUE guard and the entry, per-entry and total ceilings now measured on bytes, and crates/zz-daemon/src/client.rs client_environment_with reads std::env::vars_os as OsStr bytes instead of dropping any entry whose into_string failed. (ii) CommandInvocation.args is Vec<RawText>, so the byte survives the CLI (crates/zz/src/diagnostics/mod.rs application_args_from now forwards OsString bytes instead of to_string_lossy), split_command_words' `;` grammar, and parse_tmux_options' flag grammar. (iii) The store in crates/zz-mux/src/command.rs is BTreeMap<RawText, EnvironmentEntry> with a RawText value, environment_line builds its two spellings byte by byte and shell_environment_escape works on bytes, and the spawn environment is byte-clean end to end: job_environment -> environment_for_session -> terminal_environment_for_session -> TerminalSpawn.env, which is now Vec<(OsString, Option<OsString>)> in crates/zz-terminal/src/session.rs, and configure_shell_job_environment in crates/zz-daemon/src/lib.rs passes OsString to Command::env. (iv) CommandResponse::Success.output and CommandResponse::Error.output are RawText, Execution.output and DaemonError's three output fields follow, and print_command_output in crates/zz/src/lib.rs writes the bytes to stdout unchanged. TWO DIVERGENCES FOUND BESIDE THIS AND NOT CLOSED HERE. First, format expansion is still lossy and that is deliberate: FormatEnvironRow keeps String and format_environment_rows converts with to_string, because crates/zz-mux/src/formats.rs is String end to end. Measured at this tip on both binaries: set-environment -g ZZBYTES with a<0xff>b then display-message -p '#{ZZBYTES}' answers 61 ff 62 0a on the pin and 61 ef bf bd 62 0a on zz. The environment fallback itself is no longer missing (the 2026-09-02 note above is stale: #{PLAIN} answers hello on both now), so the remaining gap is a byte-clean format expander, which belongs to the formats groups and not here; this entry's own acceptance clause names the client's environment and update-environment, both of which the scenario proves. Second, the pin sanitizes byte output to a client it does not consider UTF-8: server_client_print calls utf8_sanitize when ~c->flags & CLIENT_UTF8, and tmux.c sets that flag from $TMUX or from LC_ALL/LC_CTYPE/LANG containing UTF-8. Measured on 2026-09-04 with LC_ALL=C and no $TMUX, the pin's show-environment -g ZZBYTES answers 61 5f 62, that is a_b, while zz answers the raw bytes in either locale. That is a client-encoding gap of its own and is not registered anywhere yet; smoke/environment-bytes pins LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 so the byte probes measure the store rather than that sanitizer. Three follow-ups from the cycle-12 reviewer were applied at the gate. The control client and the raw TUI still substituted U+FFFD for the bytes the plain CLI printed, because both output sinks took &str and swallowed a RawText through Deref; ControlWriter::payload and zz-tui's print_command_output now take the byte view with the same trailing-newline rule. Measured on both binaries with ZZBYTES=a<0xff>b: `<bin> -C show-environment -g ZZBYTES` answered 5a5a42595445533d61efbfbd620a on zz against 5a5a42595445533d61ff620a on the pin, and answers 5a5a42595445533d61ff620a on both now. smoke/environment-bytes gained that probe as its eighth check, so the fixture reads clean:8 on both binaries and drops to broken on zz alone when the lossy sink is put back, which was verified by reverting it. crates/zz/src/control_mode.rs a_command_block_carries_the_output_bytes_it_was_given and crates/zz-tui/src/lib.rs command_output_reaches_the_terminal_as_bytes carry the same measurement in-repo. The two divergences this record had only described in prose now have a registry home: the lossy format expander and the pin's CLIENT_UTF8 output sanitizer are items of clients.byte-clean-consumers, opened 2026-09-04, alongside semantic:config-tilde-home-non-utf8, which came back out of protocol.binary-streams because the byte-capable command argument its blocker named now exists. knowledge/tmux/divergences.md's Client environment refresh and Session environment updates rows were rewritten to the v98 behaviour and no longer point at this group.

closed.title: Allow read-only local copy and scroll navigation
closed.resolution: Read-only clients can use direct local scroll, copy-mode entry, movement, history, line, word, paragraph, prompt, bracket, goto-line, set-mark, jump-to-mark, and cancel actions. One typed copy-action classifier also authorizes `send-keys -X`; selection, copying, search, rectangle, jump capture, paste, clear-history, raw mouse, mixed wheel, and application pane-focus effects remain blocked. Non-`-X` `send-keys`, including an otherwise unsupported `-M` request, is rejected as read-only before repeat or full option parsing. Pin-recognized but zz-unimplemented unsafe copy actions reject; genuinely unknown and empty `-X` actions retain the pin's later no-op or no-mode path. Direct command requests and an entire stored binding chain are preflighted before any effect, including one-layer aliases, and rejected paths report `client is read-only` without terminal or browser input. Safe actions bypass retained chooser and display-panes surfaces, reach the pane, and update activity and latest geometry exactly once without clearing bells or dismissing the modal. Rejected non-focus actions, including mouse input, preserve the same bell and accounting behavior. Pane Focus is rejected without activity because v73 ClientFocus owns client-window accounting. A read-only command cannot fan a local view effect into a pane outside its attachment. The accepted uncoupled ignore-size and same-uid differences remain under `clients.read-only-and-focus`; committed-text accounting is closed separately.

closed.title: Align supported client TTY selectors
closed.resolution: Every implemented tmux command flag that selects an attached client now shares exact registered-name, exact displayed client_name, full-tty, and exactly one leading-/dev/-prefix removal, with exactly one optional trailing colon. The displayed-name path covers tmux's tty, registered-name, client-PID, and device-N fallback ladder, so a nameless Control client can be targeted by the same client-PID value returned from list-clients. The shared device-N alias remains, while popup, menu, confirm, refresh, and lock keep their documented numeric and client-N native aliases. A final pathname basename is not a selector: /dev/pts/3 accepts pts/3 but rejects 3 unless 3 is the exact client name. When aliases collide across sessions, the globally oldest attached client by creation id wins; switching sessions does not reorder it. This covers detach-client -t, switch-client -c, display-message -c, display-panes -t, display-popup -c, display-menu -c, confirm-before -t, refresh-client -t, lock-client -t, and load-buffer -t format context. Unsupported command-prompt -t, show-messages -t, send-keys -c, and suspend-client -t remain with prompt.command-fidelity, messages.tty-model, terminal.key-control, and commands.native-client-tools. set-buffer -t remains accepted but inert and is not part of this selector closure. Focused daemon coverage pins PID fallback and all earlier selectors. The complete 102-test CLI binary suite proves Control menu targeting and nonself detach through the published name while retaining queued-return behavior.

closed.title: Route TUI command-output navigation
closed.resolution: zz-tui now sends every command-output press and repeat through the daemon's pane-targeted Key path. Release events remain inert, and the output surface owns mouse and paste input instead of leaking either to the hidden workspace. The daemon resolves the target window's effective copy-mode or copy-mode-vi table, including live custom bindings and mode-keys changes, then applies supported movement, history, word, prompt, selection, rectangle, search, and copy actions to the PTY-free retained output terminal. Stock emacs Escape and q cancel. Stock vi q cancels while Escape clears an active selection and leaves the view open. A live custom q or Escape binding wins. TerminalUiCommand::BeginSearch now opens the TUI's local search editor. Text entry, bounded and control-filtered paste, backspace, submit, cancel, next, and previous actions drive the command-output viewport, and the renderer uses display-cell width for the prompt and retained output. Search submission or cancellation closes only that local editor; the TUI consumes the matching repeat and release so the same physical key cannot also run an action in the retained output table. Protocol v79 adds output_id to the existing EventPayload::CommandOutput tag 11. The daemon assigns each real output actor a nonzero daemon-lifetime-global monotonic ID and keeps it on live frames, resync frames, and closes. ClientCore retains an ID watermark, ignores stale frames and closes, and prevents a closed actor from reappearing after mailbox coalescing or a resync race. The watermark resets when the client adopts a new handshake because a restarted daemon begins a new ID lifetime. The attached differential opens 96 rows of output and passes against zz and pinned tmux for line and page movement, editable search, next and previous matches, selection and paste-buffer copy, a live q override, vi Escape behavior, and a live switch to the emacs table. Unsupported window-copy actions remain under copy-mode.action-fidelity. Reopened in part on 2026-09-05 as clients.command-output-pane-prompt: the historical claim "Search submission or cancellation closes only that local editor" does not hold for the current stock / binding, which now uses command-prompt -P. The attached probe measures zz discarding output when that prompt opens while pinned tmux preserves it. The unchanged search-editor assertions now explicitly name the native copy-mode-search-prompt route; stock prompt lifecycle remains open.

closed.title: Render and consume confirm-before in zz-tui
closed.resolution: zz-tui now caches ConfirmState from ClientCore on construction, reconnect, and every ConfirmChanged notification, clears it on attachment replacement, and paints the daemon prompt once in the configured message row, the status-off virtual row, or the sidebar status area with the pane cursor hidden. Its confirm route runs before detach, sidebar, prompt, chooser, browser, terminal, paste, and mouse handling. Printable ASCII replies compare exact case; Control-transformed characters reject, while Alt and extended modifier bit 8 do not change that comparison. Enter follows default_yes with any decoded modifier; named navigation and function input plus key releases are consumed without closing. Raw-TUI paste and pointer input are swallowed under zz's stricter overlay safety rule, while focus, size, and terminal capability traffic continues. Pinned tmux routes bracketed paste to the pane before prompt dispatch, so focused unit tests cover that intentional difference rather than the attached differential. After a reply, a pending gate retains input ownership until the daemon publishes None, and the reply key's repeat and release cannot escape after close. The attached fixture opens seven targeted prompts on zz and pinned tmux for ordinary y, Meta-y, n, custom uppercase accept and lowercase reject, and Enter with and without -y. Accepted commands mutate unique options, rejected options stay empty for a one-second settle, prompt open and close are visible, and one blocking byte sentinel proves no tested reply key reached the pane before a final z releases it. Unit coverage proves state seeding and reconnect reset, single main or sidebar rendering, hidden-status placement, modifier and key rules, pending reply ownership, paste, pointer, and key lifecycle. No protocol or daemon change was needed. GPUI confirmation shares the pinned Meta and Enter rules while retaining its native platform, function, and named nontext handling.

closed.title: Render and consume display-menu in zz-tui
closed.resolution: Raw zz-tui now retains MenuState from ClientCore at construction, update, close, attachment replacement, and reconnect. The renderer layers the menu after workspace, chooser, or command-output bases, centres descriptor coordinates in the published client grid, clamps them to the outer terminal, draws the title, borders, item names, shortcuts, selected row, and disabled rows from one descriptor, suspends Kitty images, and hides the base cursor. The shared zz-client resolver gives GPUI and raw TUI one keyboard contract: shortcuts win before cancel, step keys wrap while retaining the pin's raw boundary rows when no usable item exists, Home and End select edges, page keys retain raw-row behavior, Enter handles enabled and unusable rows with stay-open support, the cancel set closes, Press and decoded Repeat share behavior, and Release is consumed. The TUI owns menu input before confirmation, shortcuts, and pane delivery. It keeps selection in client state until an action, swallows paste and pointer events, holds input while an action waits for the daemon to clear the descriptor, and consumes decoded action-key Repeat and Release events across close. Legacy terminals report every repeated byte as a fresh Press, so that indistinguishable event follows ordinary post-close input just as it does in tmux. The attached fixture shows a titled short menu on zz and pinned tmux; proves q shortcut precedence through a unique option mutation; proves Down skips a separator and disabled row before Enter; proves Escape cancels without mutation; proves -O plus PageUp lands on an unusable row and Enter keeps the menu open before navigation selects a valid row; and proves a nonactivating paste leaves the menu open. Focused resolver coverage pins the exact raw-row-zero landing and all-disabled boundary behavior. A one-byte pane sentinel proves those test inputs do not reach the pane. This closure covers raw-TUI consumption of the daemon-published descriptor without a protocol or daemon change. display-menu.behavior-fidelity keeps selected-action context and errors, mouse policy, paste-close ordering, command-queue ordering, rendered width, resize lifecycle, shortcut display and grammar, and style refresh open. At this checkpoint popup consumption remained open; slice 10p later closed it as clients.tui-display-popup-overlay and registered the broader residue as display-popup.behavior-fidelity.

closed.title: Render and consume display-popup in zz-tui
closed.resolution: Raw zz-tui now seeds, updates, reconnects, replaces, closes, and resets PopupState from ClientCore while retaining the current synthetic terminal viewport only for the descriptor that owns it. One shared floating-layout resolver centres the published client grid, clamps it to the attached terminal, gives borderless popups their full frame, and insets every bordered family by one cell. The renderer paints workspace, popup, then higher menu or confirmation state; applies popup and border styles; draws title, terminal cells, all published border families, and the popup cursor; suspends Kitty images; preserves incremental popup damage; and fully restores the overlay after unrelated base repaints. Descriptor close, pane replacement, attachment replacement, reconnect, and late-frame races remove pending frames plus terminal, damage, browser, and Kitty caches before the latest underlay is repainted. Menu and confirmation input retain priority, then the popup owns key presses and decoded repeats, paste, and tracked content-relative pointer and wheel input before chrome, chooser, browser, or pane routes. External FocusOut and FocusIn still update retained client state.
