A live popup suppresses terminal Focus delivery to both the popup application and underlay; a dead close-on-any-key popup sends Close on FocusOut, matching the pin's overlay key path. Outer Kitty capability controls held-key tracking, the popup application's keyboard mode controls release forwarding, and every held key remains swallowed across close or replacement. Border, outside, descriptor-gap, and nontracking pointer input is consumed. One decoded tracked wheel event emits one application mouse report while local and Shift scrolling retain their three-line step. The daemon's sized-client mouse gate now consults the owning popup terminal viewport, so application-requested popup mouse works even when the global mouse option is off. The attached fixture runs three bounded cases against zz and pinned tmux: a bordered -E popup whose second display-popup updates title but cannot replace its job or geometry; a bracketed-paste and SGR mouse/wheel popup with locale-independent outer coordinates and exact content-relative 3,3 reports; and a dead -k popup retained until a key. The pin emits three internal underlay focus-out/focus-in pairs across those overlay lifecycles while zz deliberately emits none. The first two popup applications enable focus reporting; injected external focus is swallowed on both sides, so q and bracketed paste remain their next application bytes. The third case uses FocusOut to close the retained dead popup. Locale-independent full-frame capture accepts both Unicode and C-locale ACS borders and proves a live update changes only the title. A scratch marker proves the live popup received q, and one final decimal-122 underlay sentinel proves no tested key, paste, click, scroll, or external focus escaped. The complete attached fixture passes under LC_ALL=C. No protocol change was needed. display-popup.behavior-fidelity retains resize lifecycle, style refresh, context menu, border drag, popup-to-pane conversion, and popup Kitty images. Real mouse/status formats, Control presentation, and read-only popup policy remain outside this closure.

closed.title: Preserve tmux unique command prefixes
closed.resolution: Exact canonical names and aliases resolve first. Non-exact lookups use tmux canonical names whenever any match exists and consult the guarded 19-name native roster only when tmux has no match. The daemon expands one immutable user-alias layer for a direct invocation before read-only authorization and reuses it for dispatch and hooks. Stored bind-key and set-hook lists execute their constructed commands without another user-alias lookup; read-only clients authorize that frozen chain before any effect. Typed `if-shell`, `run-shell`, and `confirm-before` callbacks also stay frozen after lexical construction. Typed `if-shell` and `run-shell` callbacks retain physical groups, stopping a failed group while continuing later physical lines; string callbacks remain one group. Typed `command-prompt` templates retain their structured constructed command list through submission without another user-alias lookup. String templates substitute raw source before a fresh parse and complete construction pass against the then-current alias table. Both prompt paths replace the first `%%` and every `%1`, with trailing-percent quoting; typed substitution preserves leaf-argument boundaries and physical groups, while string templates and free input form one group. `set-hook` and command-valued native set-option retain their intentional second construction stage. A typed `display-menu` action drops its structural wrapper before the fresh selection stage, while a quoted brace string remains literal. Non-exact attach prefixes execute through the interactive command path, static agent-send prefixes trigger stdin capture, and protocol v74 prepares Control command units against the live alias table before framing. The manifest gate derives the native roster from catalog minus the pinned oracle and checks every pinned canonical prefix; the strict 29-step scenario covers all 25 affected unique prefixes, exact catalog alias precedence, user command-alias expansion, and ambiguous list-commands exit parity. Local exact attach, stdin, and kill recovery preprocessing now consumes the prepared canonical identity and alias-match state under aliases.client-preflight; remote --host routing remains under aliases.remote-client-preflight.

closed.title: Match send-keys copy-action flag grammar
closed.resolution: The pin's outer send-keys grammar is c:FHKlMN:Rt:X. zz removed C, P, and o from the outer catalog and returns the exact unknown-flag error when they appear there; the tracked c, K, and R gaps remain under terminal.key-control, and M remains under mouse.bound-context. The copy-mode parser recognizes -C and -P on the pin's 14 copy-family grammar entries and -o on next-prompt and previous-prompt; -- terminates its flag scan. Invalid local flags, actions, and arity produce no command error or copy action and reset the copy-mode repeat prefix to 1. Existing CopyModeCopy clipboard, paste-buffer, and pipe fields retain their behavior. Execution for copy-line, copy-line-and-cancel, copy-pipe-line, and copy-pipe-line-and-cancel remains under terminal.key-control through semantic:send-keys-copy-command-shape. The pin also redraws the first copy-mode line after a local parser failure; zz has no no-op redraw effect, so that presentation residue stays with the same item.

closed.title: Match config-file byte parsing
closed.resolution: The startup and runtime loaders read config files as bytes and keep the pin's two input shapes apart. A runtime source-file matches cmd-source-file.c, which reads the file into a buffer and calls load_cfg_from_buffer, so parse_config_buffer_bytes applies the signed-char getc reading where 0xff is one EOF: it ends the current line, the file keeps parsing, and a second 0xff stops it. The startup -f file matches cfg.c load_cfg, which parses the open stdio file, so parse_config_file_bytes keeps 0xff inside the token and the command name stays unknown. A non-empty file that parses to no command now consumes the pin's cmdq_empty_command item, which cmd_source_file_done skips for a zero-length file, so control clients see the pin's hidden numbering for byte, comment-only, and blank files alike. For a file holding only 0xff, direct Command sourcing exits 0 with empty streams, direct Control emits one flags-1 success guard then consumes the hidden empty-command item and the ordinary source completion before the next guard, and a synchronous if-shell emits the parent and source guards with no visible diagnostic and continues the root file; none of these report `stream did not contain valid UTF-8` any more. Nothing substitutes lossy text: a parse whose surviving command name or argument still holds bytes that are not valid UTF-8 keeps the typed read error, because zz's typed UTF-8 command protocol cannot carry those bytes at all - the same limit `zz display-message -p` shows for a non-UTF-8 argv, which stays recorded as semantic:non-utf8-command-arguments under the accepted protocol.binary-streams group. Four focused CLI tests pin the direct, startup, control numbering, and if-shell shapes, and a differential fixture runs the direct, empty, continuation, if-shell, startup, and an eleven-row placement matrix against the pin.

closed.title: Abort a config file on its first parser diagnostic
closed.resolution: The post-10v rerank corrected a stale registry premise. Since the 2026-08-19 parser work, the first lexer or parser diagnostic clears every command from the file, stops the scan, preserves only environment assignments reduced before the error, and suppresses later diagnostics. Focused tests cover invalid variables, octal escapes, and multiple leading assignments. This correction changes no runtime behavior or accepted artifact. aliases.config-parse-unit later closed the parse-time alias snapshot; eager command construction remains under mux.chain-parse-abort.

closed.title: Close config parser edge cases
closed.resolution: Config tilde expansion now follows the pin's parser-state transitions at a word start, inside an opening double quote, and immediately after an empty or nonempty closing quote. Invisible line continuations preserve the prior token state; raw quoted newlines and stripped quoted comments do not advance it; a completed typed command block resets it; and an empty variable expansion still blocks a following tilde. Bare tilde prefers a nonempty parser-context HOME, then falls back through the current passwd entry; named forms use passwd lookup. Failed lookup produces one located syntax error, and usernames longer than 1,022 bytes produce the pin's exact diagnostic. Startup, runtime source, alias, callback, and parse-only engine paths share this behavior. Unit coverage and a 17-step differential exercise 26 positive, negative, fallback, and diagnostic checks with no differing channel. Direct Control environment provenance and non-UTF-8 passwd home paths remain in explicit active groups.

closed.title: Report replayed command failures
closed.resolution: Config replay now keeps source diagnostics and command runtime failures in one ordered report stream. Typed target failures and semantic errors from a syntactically valid set-option or set-window-option command use the pin's bare message instead of a file-prefixed parser diagnostic. Command clients receive stderr and exit 1. Protocol v76 Control clients receive each parser-owned failed replay command inside its own flags-1 error guard and set retval 1 for a later blank line, EOF, or nonself detach. The later control-mode.source-file-exit-status closure proves that an actual self-detach exits 0 and that a pending Return captured during a preceding non-detach command keeps its arrival-time snapshot ahead of later queued stdin. A Return observed while self-detach itself waits is discarded when the caller's Detached event arrives. Attached clients receive the capitalized warning form. A containing source-file propagates the same message and exit status while inner and outer later lines still run. Unknown command names and lexer or malformed command diagnostics retain the existing file-prefixed `%config-error` path; generic Warning identity remains open under control-mode.diagnostic-typing. Clientless startup still retains no invoking error channel and remains under config.startup-diagnostic-delivery. The later config.replayed-command-output closure preserves stdout before and after a runtime failure and batches only command-name and parser diagnostics into the transcript at their invocation boundary. Runtime, no-match, glob, and actual OS or path read failures retain their existing error channels. The later control-mode.indirect-source-frames closure adds inherited flags-1 framing for foreground shell-evaluated `if-shell`, immediate `if-shell -F` including `-bF`, and foreground `run-shell -C`. At this checkpoint immediate-hook and background-callback flags-0 framing remained open under control-mode.hook-command-frames and control-mode.background-inserted-command-frames. Later closures closed both groups. Non-UTF-8 config content remains under config.non-utf8-file-bytes. At this close, the focused source-file-diagnostics and source-file-control scenarios passed 11 and 5 steps with no topology, geometry, format, output, or warning differences and no skips. Later default-order and nested-queue proofs grew the focused rows to 12 and 6; the return-status closure grew the focused source-file-control run to eight. None of those partial runs refreshed the stored canonical source-file-control row, which remains at three steps.

closed.title: Deliver replayed command output
closed.resolution: Runtime source-file now retains one stdout transcript per invocation. It parses every declared and globbed match before replay, appends the complete top-level -v batch in declared-path, glob, and physical-line order, replays the parsed files in the same order, then appends buffered command-name and parser diagnostics. Source no-match, glob, and actual OS or path read failures retain their existing error channels instead of joining the stdout transcript. Non-UTF-8 config content remains under config.non-utf8-file-bytes. Each nested source-file creates the same verbose, replay, command-diagnostic frame at its parent command's replay position, so nested frames run depth-first. This matches the pin's per-invocation batching and does not claim physical verbose and replay interleaving. Command clients receive sourced display-message -p, list-sessions, hook, and continuation output once on stdout. Successful output leaves stderr empty and status zero; a runtime failure keeps its original stderr and status 1 while stdout before, hook output, later output, and list output remain ordered. For syntactically valid successful replay and -v output, Interactive clients open one command-output view without duplicate Info or Warning events. Parser diagnostics may still publish their existing Warning summary. The attached fixture first proved transcript presentation and q dismissal; the later clients.tui-command-output-navigation closure added page and line movement, search, selection and copy, custom tables, and mode-key behavior. Direct Control replay keeps -v suppressed and uses its existing per-command guards. The later control-mode.indirect-source-frames closure extends flags-1 framing to synchronous foreground shell-evaluated if-shell, immediate if-shell -F including -bF, and foreground run-shell -C. At this checkpoint immediate-hook and background-callback flags-0 framing remained open under control-mode.hook-command-frames and control-mode.background-inserted-command-frames. Later closures closed both groups. One source-file invocation parses all top-level matches before replay: a bare assignment applies during parsing, affects a later file's conditional, and persists, while a replayed set-environment command runs too late to affect a later file's already parsed branch but persists after replay. With -n, neither assignment nor command effects apply, later parse-only files see the assignment as absent, and -v still reports the selected branch. Clientless startup creates no replay transcript, so the detached launcher keeps empty stdout and stderr. A separate manual probe of pinned tmux d77c9dc6, outside the 12-step runtime scenario, found that startup display-message -p text becomes a file-and-line config cause while list output is discarded; config.startup-diagnostic-delivery owns that later-client delivery.

closed.title: Drop the rest of a config line after a failed command
closed.resolution: Config and source replay now keys each parser-owned command group by exact source and physical line. A synchronous invalid or runtime command error, a nested source depth refusal, or a loud source-file no-match or glob error with zero matched files drops only later siblings from that group; the next physical line still runs. A quiet no-match is success. A matched path puts source-file on its asynchronous wait path, so child replay and parser failures, child read failures, and mixed missing-and-matched arguments do not prune the invoking line; zz retains a matched child read failure in the load report instead of returning it into parent group control flow. An asynchronous run-shell failure does not prune either. Both sides also keep the same-line sibling for a `-` path, while zz's missing stdin transport remains open under protocol.binary-streams. Equal line numbers in separate source files remain independent. zz-classified UnsupportedCommand results now skip and continue later same-line siblings; before this slice they pruned those siblings. That new continuation is desirable for zz import capability gaps, but this slice has no pinned proof that those gaps represent synchronous tmux failures. Direct CLI and Control chains are unchanged. Replayed error delivery and parser-owned sourced Control frame ownership closed under config.replayed-command-errors and control-mode.sourced-command-frames. The later config.replayed-command-output closure places each nested invocation's complete verbose, replay, and command-name or parser diagnostic transcript frame at this asynchronous source position. Source no-match, glob, and actual OS or path read failures keep their existing error channels at that position. The later source-file.nested-control-queue closure proved cross-depth containing-before-child order for parser-owned recursion. The later control-mode.indirect-source-frames closure covers synchronous foreground inserted lists. At this checkpoint immediate-hook and background-callback flags-0 framing remained open under control-mode.hook-command-frames and control-mode.background-inserted-command-frames. Later closures closed both groups. Unsupported-command continuation still does not prove parity for ConfigLoadReport's skipped summary. The post-10v rerank later recorded the already-shipped whole-file parser abort under config.parser-abort. Shared command flag and arity text closed later. The 2026-08-28 mux.error-shapes closure then matched nested new-session precedence.

closed.title: Deliver retained startup configuration causes
closed.resolution: Protocol v80 appends `EventPayload::StartupConfigCauses` at tail tag 49, bounded to 1,024 causes, 64 KiB each, and 1 MiB total with dedicated payload validation. Startup parses every root before replay. A missing implicit default is silent; explicit-root read failures, non-`NotFound` default-root failures, normalized nested read failures, parser and unknown-command diagnostics, unsupported and runtime failures, and successful `display-message -p` output are retained in root order with nested depth-first replay. List-style output stays discarded. Successful physical multiline commands use their completion line. A detached Command launch remains rc 0 with empty stdout and stderr and cannot drain the causes. Only the post-spawn Control connection advertises `startup-config-owner-v1`; it receives causes after `ServerHello` and before its first `%begin`. A Control connection to an existing daemon waits for attachment, then receives causes after `Attached` inside that attach frame. An attached Interactive client instead receives an ordered, UTF-8-safe 64 KiB preview in a PTY-free `configuration errors` view, with every Unicode control except LF and TAB replaced. A truncated preview ends with `... startup diagnostics truncated; restart in Control mode for full output`; full 1 MiB Interactive recovery is not promised. Startup output alone uses the pinned Ghostty 64 MiB byte history cap, while ordinary command output keeps its 100,000-byte setting. Eligible delivery is linearized globally. The post-spawn owner commits after the raw event is admitted. For an attached winner, the daemon commits the one-shot only after the `Attached` frame, diagnostic, resync, and mux options remain admitted; count or byte admission failure retains the causes and retires only the startup actor by exact ID. A daemon restart builds a fresh set. Control receives the raw bounded vector when it wins and prefixes each multiline cause once with `%config-error`, preserving raw continuation lines without changing retval. The checksum-attested seven-case differential against pinned tmux `d77c9dc6` passes with no skips.

closed.title: Place asynchronous command diagnostics
closed.resolution: Protocol v81 appends EventPayload::ControlCommandOutput at tail tag 50. A targetless or invalid-target foreground run-shell from Control publishes its captured stdout and nonzero or signal diagnostic to that exact originating client after the direct flags-1 response closes; a peer Control client receives nothing. The Control writer emits the payload raw, preserves embedded LF and percent-prefixed text literally, appends one LF when the payload lacks it, and does not change retained retval, so a nonzero run-shell still exits 0 for a fresh Control client. Direct and sourced commands emit an empty successful guard before the raw payload, then continue later commands or same-line sourced siblings in their own guards. Foreground run-shell -C remains synchronous inside its command frame. A live resolved -t and ordinary run-shell -b follow tmux's pane-view intent, but zz uses its native per-Interactive command-output view for every attached viewer of that pane and emits neither raw Control text nor %pane-mode-changed; this is a deliberate GUI ownership divergence from tmux's shared pane view. Pinned tmux can crash its server when a foreground Control client disconnects while run-shell waits. zz treats that crash as out of scope, retains its server, and does not emulate the failure. Protocol framing, daemon routing, writer, serialized CLI, and sourced-order regressions pass. The strict 12-step smoke/source-file-control differential against pinned tmux d77c9dc6 has zero topology, geometry, format, output, or warning differences and no skips; the stored canonical row remains unchanged at three steps.

closed.title: Frame asynchronous copy-pipe errors for Control
closed.resolution: Pinned tmux starts a copy-pipe job with JOB_NOWAIT and no update, completion, or free callback, so a later nonzero worker exit has no client notification path. The attached Control probe enters copy mode, selects a line, runs copy-pipe-and-cancel with a delayed exit 7, waits for the worker, and then proves pane_in_mode is zero while the transcript contains no %message, %error, copy-pipe diagnostic, or unsolicited command guard. zz already matched that Control contract: its worker Error event is addressed only to an Interactive invoker, or falls back to attached Interactive viewers when Control invoked the action, and never reaches the Control subscriber. The existing daemon test proves both routing branches and permit release. Interactive diagnostics remain an intentional native presentation difference. The full attached-client fixture passes against pinned tmux d77c9dc6 without a protocol or runtime change.

closed.title: Frame background-inserted commands with flags 0
closed.resolution: Shell-evaluated if-shell -b and run-shell -bC now retain the originating Control client separately from replay_client and map its inserted work to protocol v77 flags 0. The triggering flags-1 frame closes first, later flags-1 input may overtake the callback, and each inserted command, source command, and sourced child receives an independent frame in parent-before-child order. Successful and false-branch output stays inside its callback frame. Missing sources and runtime failures end their flags-0 frames with %error and set sticky status 1; a later flags-1 success does not clear that status before Return. Both producers keep a malformed delayed command list silent, unframed, and status-neutral. Ordinary run-shell -b shell jobs remain unframed, immediate if-shell -bF remains synchronous flags 1, and foreground run-shell -C retains the closed synchronous path. The callback clears replay_client and checks that its exact Control client is still registered before callback execution begins. A client disconnected before that point gets no callback frame or inserted side effect, and no output migrates to a later client. control-mode.disconnect-cancels-command-queue owns hard disconnect after an immediate hook or source queue has already started. Non-Control background behavior is unchanged. The implementation reuses protocol v77 without a wire bump. Focused daemon and serialized Control CLI regressions pass, shell syntax and formatting checks pass, and the strict 11-step smoke/source-file-control differential has zero topology, geometry, format, output, or warning differences with no skips. The partial differential leaves the stored canonical summary unchanged.

closed.title: Type Control-mode config diagnostics
closed.resolution: Protocol v91 appends EventPayload::ControlConfigError, and the two producers that raise configuration diagnostics for a Control client -- the unknown or ambiguous replayed command name and the deferred construction diagnostics of a sourced file -- now publish it instead of a generic Warning ClientMessage. Control renders %config-error from the payload type alone; the English text classifier that recognized `source-file `, ` invalid line`, `skipped N unsupported tmux command`, and the `path:line: ` shape is deleted, so a reworded, empty, or localized diagnostic still routes there and a generic warning that merely reads like one no longer promotes itself. This matches the pin, where cfg_add_cause records a cause by where it was raised and cfg_print_causes / cfg_show_causes write %%config-error for any control client without inspecting the text. Both producers were already Control-only, so no interactive surface changed. Typed source-read failures keep their separate v78 ControlSourceFile channel.

closed.title: Cancel client-owned Control queues after connection loss
closed.resolution: Control clients now own a per-connection command worker, the same one Command clients had, and the connection reader keeps its own execution context for attach handling, so the reader sees the socket close while a request is still running. Three pieces close this group. (1) A per-connection cancel flag lives beside the client writers; the reader raises it the moment its loop leaves, and both command queue loops -- the inserted-command loop that runs hooks, command lists and if-shell branches, and the sourced-file replay loop -- stop between items when the flag is up. That is server_client_lost freeing the client's cmdq: the item already running finishes and everything after it never fires. (2) Protocol 95 -> 96 appends ProtocolMessage::CommandQueueParked { request_id }, which the worker sends from the eleven places a Control client's request blocks a daemon thread (both run-shell delay receivers and the blocking run-shell, if-shell, both wait-for receivers, the command-prompt and display-panes waiters, display-menu, display-popup and confirm-before). A thread-local scope installed by the worker names the request, so one report per request is emitted at the real park rather than guessed from a roster of verbs. (3) The control client no longer truncates its queued input: PendingReturn::Eof now records how much input was queued ahead of it instead of hard-coding zero (the truncation helper retain_first_initial_stdin_before_eof is gone), and a parked request whose client is already at end of file or at a blank Return closes its guard with no payload, drops the rest of the queued input, skips the exit drain and exits. RE-SCOPED: the second acceptance clause read `Graceful EOF and a blank Return keep the originating queue alive until its pending hook and source work drains, preserving output and retained status before the client exits.` The pin does the opposite and this group's own reason had already recorded the contradiction on 2026-09-01. Re-measured on 2026-09-02 at d77c9dc6 by piping lines into `-C attach-session -t =w` and closing stdin: three `display-message -p` lines all run; a `run-shell` first runs nothing else, because run-shell always returns CMD_RETURN_WAIT and cmdq_next stops on a waiting item; two messages then a blocking run-shell print both messages, close the run-shell's guard empty and exit while the job's side effect lands seconds later; `run-shell 'touch X'` followed by `display-message -p AFTER` runs only the run-shell, so what matters is the yield and not how long the command takes; a blank Return behaves like end of file. The clause now names the measured shape. The earlier reading of the clause, that zz runs one command and the pin runs the ones before the blocker, was also wrong for the same reason: the pin runs the ones before the first YIELDING command, and run-shell yields even when it is instant. One shape does not report a park and the pin is why: `run-shell -C` with no delay returns CMD_RETURN_WAIT but arms its timer with `event_active`, which the same event-loop pass resumes before `server_client_check_exit` can look, so the pin's client never exits there. smoke/source-replay-diagnostics is the scenario that says so -- its control probes pipe one `source-file` line and close stdin, and a hook body of `run-shell -C "{ display-message -p quoted }"` has to run to the end on both binaries. zz's zero-delay `-C` path takes a worker-thread round trip that always resolves, so it is left unreported; a `-d` delay, a real job and every overlay wait still report. Two divergences found beside this and not fixed here. (a) A sourced command that parks leaves zz one control guard pair short: cmd_queue's guard closes at fire time on the pin, so a parked `run-shell` inside a sourced file prints `%begin`/`%end` before the queue stops, while zz publishes a sourced command's guard when the command finishes and the client is gone by then. The direct shape is unaffected because that guard is the client's own request frame, which the release path closes. smoke/control-eof-drain compares the payload lines and the side effects for the sourced case and the whole normalised stream for the direct ones. (b) The pinned server dies on `printf "run-shell 'echo hi'\n" | tmux -C attach-session -t =w`: the control client exits at end of file, the server survives the job, and the next client to connect gets `server exited unexpectedly` with the server process gone, 4 runs out of 4 at d77c9dc6 with -f /dev/null and a scratch HOME. A job with no output (`touch`) never does it, so the trigger is routing a finished job's output to a client whose queue was freed. zz answers that shape with an empty guard and no crash. The shape is left out of smoke/control-eof-drain on purpose, with a comment saying why, because it would kill the harness server mid-scenario. Proved by smoke/control-eof-drain (six shapes: three messages, blocking first, blocking last, blank Return, an instant run-shell first, four size reports ending in detach-client, and a sourced file whose third command parks) and smoke/control-hard-loss (a parked run-shell with two items queued behind it and the client SIGKILLed, the same queue filled by source-file, a replacement Control client that receives no line of the dead queue's work, and the same sourced file with the client left alive so the cancellation is measured against a queue that otherwise completes). Both scenarios are byte-identical on the two binaries; before the change the sourced hard-loss case ran all three of its commands on zz and one on the pin, and the EOF cases ran one command on zz against the pin's full prefix.

closed.title: Discard pending pane output when Control exits
closed.resolution: Control stdin observation now begins before initial command preparation. A blank Return or EOF immediately disables pane-byte publication, removes deferred PaneOutput and PaneOutputAged records, and rejects later pane bytes while preserving pane output already written. Pause and continue records, ordinary notifications, config diagnostics, command guards, command output, retained return status, and one final exit keep their existing order. An EOF already observed during initial startup retains at most the first admitted stdin command, matching the pin without executing later buffered mutations. Thirty-three focused Control units, the full EOF, blank, and detach return matrix, a held-command live differential, the long-lived pane-output path, and all eight startup-diagnostic cases pass against pinned tmux. Hard-disconnect queue cancellation remains under its separate owner.

closed.title: Frame hook-inserted commands with flags 0
closed.resolution: Protocol v77 renames tail-tag-47 SourcedCommandGuard in place to ControlCommandGuard and adds frame flags while renaming the independent retained-status bit to sticky_failure. Parser-owned replay installs a Control command target with flags 1 separately from replay_client. Immediate after-command and command-error hooks retain that recipient, clear replay_client, enter the no-hooks state, and give every hook command, hook source command, and sourced descendant its own flags-0 frame. Multiple hook array entries remain ordered; one failing command stops only its command-list entry, later entries and later parser-owned flags-1 commands continue. Output and errors do not fold into the trigger. A mixed missing-and-matched hook source ends its flags-0 guard with %end but sets sticky_failure, so later success cannot clear retval 1. Unknown or ambiguous sourced commands are rejected before command execution, publish only %config-error, and do not fire command-error. Alias resolution is frozen once before source classification and execution. set-hook -R copies only the hidden Control target into a retargeted hook context, without copying replay-client cwd semantics. At this checkpoint background shell callbacks and deferred event hooks cleared the target, while per-client, per-thread RAII capture prevented cross-thread interception or recipient leakage. The later control-mode.background-inserted-command-frames closure makes background shell callbacks retain their exact Control target through callback entry; deferred event hooks still clear it. At this checkpoint parser and hook-source OS or path read failures retained external raw-placement and invisible source-completion numbering gaps. The later protocol-v78 control-mode.hook-source-read-diagnostics closure closed both; sourced-hook cwd remains under source-file.sourced-hook-client-cwd, deferred event-hook routing remains under source-file.event-hook-client-cwd, and missing producers remain under hooks.queue. Protocol tests pass 175 unit plus 14 manifest tests, Control tests pass 27, zz-client passes 37 unit plus two simulator tests, source_file and replayed clusters pass 6 and 5, and focused daemon and CLI hook regressions pass. Strict clippy across protocol, client, mux, daemon, and zz, formatting, shell syntax, and diff checks pass. The strict ten-step smoke/source-file-control differential has zero topology, geometry, format, output, or warning differences and no skips. The partial run leaves the stored canonical summary unchanged.

closed.title: Match Control source read placement and completion numbering
closed.resolution: Protocol v78 appends EventPayload::ControlSourceFile at tail tag 48 with ControlSourceFileEvent::ReadError(String) and Complete. For matched parser flags-1 and immediate-hook flags-0 OS or path read failures, the daemon publishes ReadError after the source guard. The Control writer closes that guard with %end, prints the platform-dependent `error: path` text as one raw unframed line, retains status 1 for EOF or a blank Return, and lets later physical lines continue. Complete renders nothing and advances the Control command number once after the invocation's descendants. Every depth-admitted invocation publishes exactly one Complete, including an empty file, loud or quiet all-miss, matched parser error, nested or hook-owned source, and `source-file -`. Invocation 51 at the depth limit and dispatch-time syntax, arity, or unknown-flag rejects publish none. One invocation with one or multiple matched read failures prints every raw error before replay but still publishes one completion after all descendants. The protocol tag and round-trip test, daemon ordering and cardinality regressions, Control writer regression, parser and hook CLI regressions, and strict 12-step smoke/source-file-control differential cover the wire shape, raw placement, numbering, status, continuation, and both frame flags with zero differences and no skips. The focused run leaves the stored canonical row unchanged at three steps. The pinned lone-0xff case additionally consumes a hidden empty-command item and remains under config.non-utf8-file-bytes. Source stdin transport beyond its now-matching completion number, parser abort semantics, sourced-hook cwd, deferred event-hook cwd and routing, and hard-disconnect queue cancellation remain open under their existing groups.

closed.title: Frame synchronous inserted commands in Control replay
closed.resolution: Synchronous inserted command lists reached during parser-owned Control replay now retain the original Control recipient. This covers foreground shell-evaluated if-shell without -b, immediate if-shell -F including -bF, and foreground run-shell -C. The daemon captures nested guard and diagnostic events per client and thread, then publishes one flags-1 frame for the triggering replay command, each inserted command, an inserted source command, and each sourced child in parent-before-child order. Output, source-command errors, runtime client_failure, retained status, unsupported-command continuation, and nested success or failure remain command-scoped without folding, duplication, cross-thread interception, or leakage into the next input command. An unsupported zz-only inserted command emits an empty success guard and later inserted siblings continue, but it does not join ConfigLoadReport's skipped summary; the existing command and semantic coverage still owns that reporting gap. An unknown command inside the child file matches the pin's parent success, source success, then `%config-error` Warning without its own guard, so it creates no new gap. The implementation reuses protocol v76 SourcedCommandGuard and does not bump the protocol. At this checkpoint immediate-hook and background-callback flags-0 framing remained open under control-mode.hook-command-frames and control-mode.background-inserted-command-frames. Later closures closed both groups. Ordinary run-shell -b output remains under control-mode.async-command-output. Focused matrix and cross-thread tests pass; the focused source_file set passes 6 of 6 and the replayed set passes 5 of 5. A fresh debug build, strict daemon clippy, formatting, shell syntax, and scoped and global diff checks pass. The strict nine-step smoke/source-file-control and 12-step source-file-output differentials have zero differences and no skips. The stored canonical source-file-control row remains unchanged at three steps.

closed.title: Order kill-server replies before daemon shutdown
closed.resolution: Shutdown now freezes new response admissions under the same lock that counts active requests, waits a bounded interval for admitted Control and Command responses to enter their mailboxes, publishes ServerStopping, and drains every registered client writer through one bounded deadline. Late requests cannot execute after the freeze. The foreground thread regains and holds the actual listener through admission and writer drain, then removes the endpoint before dropping the listener, so a replacement cannot bind while the old path guard remains armed. Controlled regressions cover an active response, zero-to-late Control and Command requests, a stalled writer, a disconnected mailbox, and replacement binding during cleanup. Command and Control CLI tests prove empty successful kill-server replies, one final Control exit, no unexpected-exit text, and immediate fresh-daemon startup.

closed.title: Parse Control tilde with daemon environment
closed.resolution: Direct Control input now expands `~` from the daemon instead of the Control process. Measured on a throwaway pinned server whose global HOME is /server/home with a pty-less control client holding HOME=/client/home: `display-message -p ~` answers /server/home, `~<user>` answers that user's entry in the server host's passwd database, a missing user is the located `parse error: syntax error`, a single-quoted tilde stays literal, and an empty (`set-environment -g HOME ''`) or unset (`-gu HOME`) server HOME falls back to the server host's own passwd home, not the client's. Protocol v92 carries that lookup as HomeDirectoryRequest/HomeDirectoryResponse: control_mode's parse_line runs one recording pass that answers every tilde with an empty home so the whole line is walked instead of aborting at the first name, collects the names, makes one batched round trip only when the line actually needs a home, and re-parses with the answers. The daemon reads its own engine's global HOME when nonempty and otherwise the daemon host's passwd entry, which is the rule ConfigBuilder::home_directory already applies to every other parser context. The round trip consumes no command number and adds no frame, proved by the differential's rebased %begin/%end timeline: thirteen contiguous command frames matched the pin exactly on both binaries. Variables are still not expanded in direct Control input, which stays a separate divergence: the pin's lexer reads $NAME from the server's global environment and zz keeps the literal text.

closed.title: Type Control-mode source diagnostics
closed.resolution: The daemon marks grouped source-read diagnostics sent to Control as ClientMessageKind::Error. The Control client routes those Error events to standalone %error frames without inspecting text, so numeric OS errors, paths containing colon-space, and localized or platform-specific read errors cannot fall through or change classification with sibling order. This closure covers internal typed identity only. A later pinned probe showed that external parser and hook-source read failures instead close the surrounding guard, write raw unframed text, and consume an invisible source-completion command number; the later protocol-v78 control-mode.hook-source-read-diagnostics closure owns and closes that placement and numbering. Invalid UTF-8 was a zz-side typed read error at this checkpoint; a later pinned lone-0xff probe showed different config-byte semantics and moved that case to config.non-utf8-file-bytes. Protocol v76 sourced-command guards separately carry the parsed source command's own no-match, glob, and depth diagnostics. Config summaries and lexer-owned diagnostics remain generic Warning events behind the prose classifier tracked under control-mode.diagnostic-typing. The known-family Warning fallback remains for legacy producers, while the exact protocol handshake rejects v75 and v76 client-daemon skew before either event path can mix.

closed.title: Match Control return status and detach precedence
closed.resolution: The long-lived Control front end now matches the pin's return-status and detach precedence across all eight tracked cases. A direct runtime CommandResponse::Error sets retval 1 unless it is a parse or preparation error. Parser-owned sourced runtime failures, nonruntime source-file failures returned as nonzero Success, and typed actual OS or path source-read failures also set retval 1 without making every %error or generic Warning sticky. EOF and a blank input line return the current retval snapshot. A generic nonzero Success such as run-shell exit 3 and flags-1 parse or preparation failures do not set or change retval: a fresh Control client therefore remains at 0, while a prior sticky failure stays at 1. Explicit self-detach after a completed failure exits 0. A self-detach queued while another command is open also exits 0 when stdin remains open. A self-detach plus EOF queued while a preceding non-detach command is waiting returns the pending EOF snapshot of 1 before the later queued detach runs. More generally, a Return captured while a preceding non-detach command waits keeps the retval observed at arrival and precedes later queued stdin commands, including detach. A Return observed while a self-detach command itself waits is discarded when the caller's Detached event arrives, and the self-detach exits 0. The front end treats only an actual caller-targeted Detached event as self-detach. detach-client -a, -t OTHER, -s that excludes the caller, a no-victim selector, and canonical or user aliases targeting other clients keep the Control loop alive and preserve any pending Return, while bare, built-in-alias, user-alias, explicit-self, and caller-including -s forms exit 0. The command response closes with %end before %exit even when the Detached event arrives first. This uses existing CommandResponse and Detached messages with no wire change. Twenty-seven Control units and 34 serialized Control CLI tests pass, including two race probes run five times each. Debug build, strict clippy, and formatting pass. The focused eight-step source-file-control differential has zero differences and no skips, and a manual detach-client -a probe matches the pin. The focused run does not refresh or prove the canonical suite, whose checked-in row still records three steps. config.replayed-command-output later closed Command and attached transcript delivery without changing these retval rules. The later control-mode.indirect-source-frames closure preserves child guard failure state for synchronous foreground shell-evaluated `if-shell`, immediate `if-shell -F` including `-bF`, and foreground `run-shell -C`. At this checkpoint immediate-hook and background-callback flags-0 framing remained open under control-mode.hook-command-frames and control-mode.background-inserted-command-frames. Later closures closed both groups. Non-UTF-8 config content remains under config.non-utf8-file-bytes. Startup diagnostics and generic config diagnostic typing remain under their existing groups.

closed.title: Preserve frames for sourced Control commands
closed.resolution: Protocol v76 appends EventPayload::SourcedCommandGuard at tail tag 47 with output, error, and client_failure fields. Each parser-owned replayed command that survives command-name resolution gets a guard in recursive file order; command aliases that resolve to source-file before this branch keep the same recursion path. Unknown or ambiguous command names and malformed alias names publish a located Warning that Control renders as %config-error, without a guard. Ordinary success and quiet all-miss commands produce empty flags-1 %end guards. Successful command output stays inside that command's guard. A nested source hit plus miss carries its declared-path diagnostic inside %end, while an all-miss, flag or arity failure, runtime failure, and depth refusal end %error. Runtime failures set client_failure, which sets Control retval 1 independently of the frame terminator; parse and source-command diagnostics can use %error without doing so. At this checkpoint zz sent a matched child OS or path read failure after its parent guard as a typed standalone Error frame. A later pinned probe showed that the external read diagnostic is raw and unframed after a successful source guard and that every source invocation consumes an invisible completion command number; the later protocol-v78 control-mode.hook-source-read-diagnostics closure owns and closes those mismatches. Invalid UTF-8 was a zz-side typed error at this checkpoint; config.non-utf8-file-bytes owns the later pinned semantic mismatch. Control defers guards FIFO until the direct outer command closes, allocates fresh frame numbers, and cannot leak them into the next input command. Other config command-name and lexer diagnostics remain Warning events on the existing %config-error prose-classification path, so this close does not claim typed lexer diagnostics. The daemon suite passes 593 tests, protocol tests pass 175 unit plus 14 framing tests, the Control cluster passes 31 tests, and the then-five-step source-file-control differential had zero differences and no skips. That partial scenario run did not refresh or prove the canonical suite. The later source-file.nested-control-queue closure proved cross-depth parser-owned diagnostic order and grew the focused row to six steps. The later control-mode.source-file-exit-status closure completed Control return-status and detach precedence and grew the focused run to eight steps, also with zero differences and no skips. That focused run did not refresh the stored canonical row, which remains at three steps. config.replayed-command-output later closed Command and attached transcript delivery with per-invocation verbose batching. The later control-mode.indirect-source-frames closure extends this flags-1 recipient path to synchronous foreground shell-evaluated `if-shell`, immediate `if-shell -F` including `-bF`, and foreground `run-shell -C`. Immediate hook and background callback flags-0 framing closed later under control-mode.hook-command-frames and control-mode.background-inserted-command-frames.

closed.title: Complete the copy-mode action vocabulary
closed.resolution: crates/zz-mux/src/copy_actions.rs owns all 95 pinned window-copy names with a behavior category and the pin read-only bit, and derives support from the send-keys -X parser, so 94 mapped and the one missing name stay in step with the code. The selection lifecycle is complete: selection-mode carries the pin selflag with its abbreviations and silent no-op, stop-selection is typed apart from clear-selection, and begin-selection, other-end, select-word, and select-line arm or reset the unit the pin does. Word and line extension is measured against the pin through a throwaway-server copy-mode probe: a whitespace cursor resolves outward to the neighboring word and select-word lands on the last cell of its word. Cursor geometry, logical-line and mode-key behavior, jump/page/prompt actions, and copy formatting keep their own items. The scroll-exit latch is now writable in the mode: scroll-exit-on, -off, and -toggle rearm the bit `copy-mode -e` latches at entry, page-down-and-cancel and halfpage-down-and-cancel force the exit for one action, scroll-down-and-cancel exits on reaching the bottom whether or not a selection is live, and cursor-down-and-cancel exits only when a whole counted run stayed stuck. previous-matching-bracket completes the jump, page, and prompt family: it scans back to the nearest closing bracket inside the logical line and walks its depth back to the opener, leaving the cursor alone when there is none, which is the pinned emacs branch widened from one column to the whole line. View-relative geometry is typed too: cursor-centre-vertical and cursor-centre-horizontal park the cursor mid-view and mid-row without moving the view, scroll-top, scroll-middle, and scroll-bottom move the view so the cursor line lands on that screen row and do nothing at all when the retained revision cannot reach it, and toggle-position flips the published position readout. recentre-top-bottom completes the category: it cycles the cursor line through the middle, top, and bottom of the view, restarts at the middle whenever the cursor changed line since the last press, and clamps to what the revision allows instead of refusing like the scroll placements. goto-line is measured against the pin and rebuilt: window_copy_goto_line reads its argument with strtonum over the whole string, base ten, one optional sign and leading whitespace allowed, in the inclusive range -1 through INT_MAX, and with line numbers off the number is a scrollback offset counted from the bottom, clamped to the retained history, that moves the view and leaves the cursor on the screen row it already had. Probed on a throwaway server against forty lines in a six-row pane, `#{scroll_position}` answered 5, 7, 9, 41 and 41 for 5, 7, 9, 2147483647 and a value past the history, 6 for '+6' and 13 for ' 13', while 'abc', '3x', '0x10', '2147483648' and the empty string each left the previous position untouched, and `#{copy_cursor_y}` stayed on 5 throughout. zz now parses the same grammar and moves the same viewport instead of parking the cursor on an absolute row, and a rejected argument still reaches the mode rather than being swallowed by the mux: outside a mode `send-keys -X goto-line abc` now fails on both engines, which is the pin's order of checks. Targets past INT_MAX are not pinned targets, so the terminal treats them as no move at all. logical-line and mode-key behavior is the remaining measurement: zz's copy engine takes no mode-keys input at all, while the pin branches on it in eleven places in window-copy.c, at window_copy_key_table, window_copy_cmd_next_matching_bracket, window_copy_command, window_copy_search, window_copy_cursor_limit, window_copy_cursor_right, window_copy_cursor_up, window_copy_cursor_down, window_copy_cursor_jump_to_back, window_copy_cursor_next_word_end_pos and window_copy_cursor_next_word_end. Six of those are the same `onemore` rule, that emacs may park the cursor one column past the last cell and vi may not, and the rest change the search table, the bracket search origin, the scroll-only cursor row, and where next-word-end lands. Reaching them means the option has to travel to the copy session and the revision has to answer questions the engine currently answers with a single geometry, so this item is a plumbing item, not a per-action one. semantic:copy-mode-copy-format-and-destination closed on 2026-09-02 with the last four copy names. window_copy_do_copy_line is window_copy_do_copy_end_of_line with two lines in front of it: selflag back to SEL_CHAR and the cursor to the start of its logical line, both of which grid_reader walks with wrapping on, so the selection it builds is the whole logical line however the row wraps. zz's engine gained CopyLine with its own count policy, built from the same mode_logical_line_bounds select-line uses, and the mux maps all four names onto it through the -C and -P grammar the other copy names already carry. Measured on the pin on 2026-09-02 with an attached pty client and a pane holding `alpha beta gamma`, `delta epsilon` and `zeta`: with the cursor two columns into the middle line, `send-keys -X copy-line` put `delta epsilon` in the buffer, left `#{copy_cursor_x}` and `#{copy_cursor_y}` where they were, answered `#{selection_present}`=0 and stayed in the mode; `-N 2 -X copy-line` copied `delta epsilon` and `zeta`; `-X copy-pipe-line 'cat >file'` wrote `delta epsilon` to the file and stayed in the mode; `-X copy-pipe-line-and-cancel` and `-X copy-line-and-cancel` each copied and then left the mode; and after `send-keys -N 5` a `send-keys -X bogus-action` left the next `-X cursor-up` moving one row, not five. compat/scenarios/smoke/copy-mode-copy-line.txt asserts those thirteen facts on both binaries; it compares the cursor column against itself rather than against a number, because the pin's cursor-up keeps a desired column that zz's does not, which is the cursor-geometry item, not this one. The 95-name inventory now has seven names left, all under Vocabulary: scroll-to-mouse and the six search entry points. Measured on both binaries on 2026-09-02 with one attached pty client and a pane holding `abcd efg`, `hijk` and `lmnopq rst`, and the finding is that this item is blocked behind cursor geometry rather than behind the option. On the pin under mode-keys vi, `end-of-line` answered `#{copy_cursor_x}` 7, four cursor-rights from there wrapped onto the next row and stopped at 3, the last cell of `hijk`, and `next-word-end` from the start of that row answered 3 and stayed at 3. Under emacs the same three answered 8, 3 and 4, and a second next-word-end walked to 6, one past the end of `lmnopq` on the row below. zz answered 7, 7, 3 and 3 under both spellings, and its four cursor-rights walked to column 11 on the same row without ever wrapping: its copy cursor has no per-line limit at all. `ModeRevision::clamp_point` clamps x to the revision's column count, and the only line-relative helper, `revision_copy_line_end`, answers the last non-blank column, which is exactly the pin's vi limit and never its emacs one. `window_copy_cursor_limit` is applied by every acquire and update in window-copy.c, so the onemore rule the six branches share is a property of that limit, not a branch that can be added beside it: six of the eleven cannot be honoured until the engine gains the pin's per-line cursor limit and the wrapping cursor-right that reads it, which is cursor geometry. The other half of the plumbing got cheaper in the same pass: MuxEffect::TerminalKnobsChanged now carries an EngineKnobs value per pane at effective scope, so mode-keys can ride it as a live bit the way scroll-on-clear and allow-rename do, with the entry-time value latched on the mode for the three branches that read `data->modekeys` rather than the option. The scroll-only rows in window_copy_cursor_up and window_copy_cursor_down were not measurable in that probe because the pane had no history to scroll; they need a scrolled revision and stay unmeasured. 2026-09-02: the cursor geometry that blocked this is built, and the option now reaches the copy engine, so six of the eleven branches are answered and the remaining five are each their own measurable piece rather than one blocked item. The model is `window_copy_update_cursor`, which clamps every placement to `window_copy_cursor_limit` for the row it lands on: `grid_line_length` under emacs, one less under vi, and no clamp at all while a rectangle is dragged. zz gained that limit and applies it wherever the copy cursor is placed, so the flat `ModeRevision::clamp_point` no longer decides the column. On top of it: cursor-right and cursor-left are `grid_reader_cursor_right`/`_left` with wrapping, reading the row's own limit rather than the revision width; cursor-up and cursor-down carry `data->lastcx` and `data->lastsx`, the desired column and the length of the row it came from, re-clamped on the new row and pushed to the line end when it had reached the remembered one; start-of-line, back-to-indentation and end-of-line walk the rows a wrap continued onto, so a wrapped pair is one logical line; and next-word-end and next-space-end are `grid_reader_cursor_next_word_end` with `grid_reader_handle_wrap`, which bounds a wrapped row at its last column instead of its used width, wrapped in the mode-keys branch that steps off the cell first and pulls the cursor back afterwards under vi. `mode-keys` reaches the worker as an `EngineKnobs` bit resolved per pane at window scope, and the daemon re-sends the knobs on `MuxEffect::ModeKeysChanged`, so the six branches that read the option live see it live. Measured on both binaries with one attached pty client, on a pane holding `abcd efg`, `hijk` and `lmnopq rst`, and on a line built from the pane's own width so that it fills one row and spills twenty letters, a space and `tail` onto the next. Under vi: end-of-line 7, four cursor-rights wrapping onto the next row and stopping at 3, cursor-left back to 2, wrapping left off column zero onto 7 of the row above, next-word-end 3 and 3 and 3, and the walk from the line end down onto 3 then 3 and back up onto 3 then 3. Under emacs the same reads answer 8, 3, 2, 8, then 4 then 6 on the row below then 10, and the walk answers 4, 10, 4, 8. On the wrapped line, end-of-line lands on the continuation row at 24 (vi) or 25 (emacs), start-of-line walks back to the filled row, next-word-end crosses the wrap to 19 or 20 without breaking the word, and wrapping left off the continuation row lands on the filled row at its width minus one, or its width. Those 44 answers are compat/scenarios/smoke/copy-mode-mode-keys.txt, asserted on both binaries under both spellings. Two zz-side reads had to change with the geometry and are recorded rather than hidden: `#{copy_cursor_x}` is no longer clamped to the revision width when it is published, because emacs parks one past the last cell and a filled row's answer is the column count itself; and the cursor-centre commands place through the same clamp, so a column past the row they land on is cut to that row's limit, which is what `window_copy_cmd_centre_vertical` does through `window_copy_update_cursor`. What is left, all of it now independently measurable: `window_copy_cursor_jump_to_back` passes `onemore` to the right step it takes after the jump, which zz's column-range jump does not model; `window_copy_command`'s emacs retry for previous-matching-bracket and `window_copy_cmd_next_matching_bracket`'s vi-first-closing-bracket walk both read the latched `data->modekeys`, which zz does not keep (the knob is live only, and the latch was dropped rather than carried unused); `window_copy_search` places the cursor after the match under emacs and at its start under vi; and the `scroll_only` vi row shift in cursor-up and cursor-down still needs a scrolled revision to measure, which no probe here built. One divergence was measured beside this work and belongs to the client key path rather than to the copy engine: while a pane is in copy mode the pin answers `#{client_key_table}` `root`, because `window_copy_key_table` is consulted per keypress off the mode entry and never written to the client, where zz stores the mode's table on the client and answers `copy-mode-vi` or `copy-mode`. 2026-09-02: the search family left the Vocabulary category. `search-forward`, `search-backward`, their `-text` and `-incremental` spellings are daemon actions now, not a client surface, so the 95-name inventory has one name left, `scroll-to-mouse`, and the mapped count went from 88 to 94. The engine runs them synchronously against the frozen revision the way `window_copy_search` runs inside the command, rather than queueing the async search worker, because everything the next command reads has to be in place when the action returns. Measured on both binaries with one attached pty client, mode-keys switched under it, on a pane holding `alpha beta gamma`, `delta alpha epsilon` and `zeta alpha` echoed twice by `cat`. The placement rule is the mode-keys branch in `window_copy_search`: forward under vi steps past the mark the cursor stands on and lands on the next match's start (history-top then `search-forward alpha` answers copy_cursor_x,y 6,1), forward under emacs searches from the cursor itself, so it may find the mark the cursor is already on, and parks one cell past it (5,0 for the same probe); backward moves one cell left first under both and lands on the match's start (0,1 and 0,1 for `search-backward delta`). `search-again` and `search-reverse` re-run the stored string with the stored or flipped direction and therefore inherit the same branch, which is why emacs answers 11,1 where vi answers 5,2. The `-text` spellings clear `data->searchregex`, so `search-forward-text 'al.ha'` finds nothing while `search-forward 'al.ha'` finds alpha; the plain spellings also downgrade to a literal when the string holds none of `^$*+()?[].\\`. A missing or empty string is `window_copy_expand_search_string` answering zero, which leaves the mode untouched. `wme->prefix` repeats the whole search, so `-N 3 -X search-forward alpha` walks three matches on. The `-incremental` spellings read the prefix `command-prompt -i` prepends: `=` is the spelling's own direction, `+` is down and `-` is up in the forward spelling and the two swap in the backward one; the mode latches `data->searchx`, `searchy` and `searcho` on the first step and every changed string restores them, with `data->cx` set to the row's own cursor limit rather than to searchx, which is what `window_copy_cmd_search_forward_incremental` literally does; an empty body clears the marks. Note that `send-keys -X search-forward-incremental -foo` never reaches the mode at all: the leading dash is eaten by send-keys' own argument parsing. `send-keys -F` was measured and is narrower than this batch assumed: it is not a general key-argument expansion. `args_has(cs->args, 'F')` is read in exactly one place in the pin, `window_copy_expand_search_string` at window-copy.c:1251, which runs the search string through `format_single` in the target pane's context; the two `-incremental` spellings never call that helper, and no other key argument is touched. zz's catalog already had `-F` as a real flag rather than an unsupported one, so no counter or usage override moved with it. compat/scenarios/smoke/copy-mode-search.txt asserts 26 rows on both binaries, including `send-keys -FX search-forward '#{copy_cursor_word}'` landing on the next occurrence of the cursor word and the same command without `-F` searching for the braces literally and finding nothing. The four branches landed, and the item stays open: reviewed 2026-09-02 on both binaries with one attached pty client, mode-keys switched under the mode, the pane holding `alpha beta gamma` / `delta alpha epsilon` / `zeta alpha` twice, reading `#{copy_cursor_x},#{copy_cursor_y}|#{search_present}|#{search_match}|#{search_count}|#{search_count_partial}|#{search_timed_out}`, three mode-keys reads the eleven-place enumeration missed diverge, and the search engine this cycle added makes them visible. (1) window_copy_command's tail at window-copy.c:3768 reads the live option after every command whose name does not start with search-: the marks are cleared per the command table's clear class (51 CLEAR_ALWAYS, 36 CLEAR_EMACS_ONLY, 7 NEVER) and searchx/searchy go back to -1. emacs, history-top, search-forward alpha, cursor-down: pin 5,1|0||||0, zz 5,1|1||6|0|0; then search-again: pin 11,1|1|alpha|||0 (the visible-only re-lay keeps the -1 count), zz 11,1|1|alpha|6|0|0. vi, search-forward alpha, cursor-down (kept on both), begin-selection (CLEAR_ALWAYS): pin 6,2|0||||0, zz 6,2|1|alpha|6|0|0. zz clears search_marks only inside run_copy_mode_search. (2) The same reset re-latches the incremental origin: emacs, history-top, search-forward-incremental =alpha, three cursor-downs, search-forward-incremental =zeta: pin 4,5 (latched at row 3), zz 4,2 (back to the first prompt's row 0, because incremental_origin is never cleared for the mode's life). (3) window_copy_get_selection at window-copy.c:5685 drops the bottom-right cell under emacs: begin-selection, four cursor-rights, copy-selection: pin buffer `alph` under emacs and `alpha` under vi, zz `alpha` under both, because format_selection has no mode-keys branch. window_copy_cursor_previous_word's stop_at_eol at 6500 is a fourth read the enumeration missed and has not yet been made to diverge. What closes it: a per-action clear class on CopyModeAction mirroring the pin's table, applied in apply_copy_mode_action for every non-Search action against the live mode_keys_vi knob (search_marks=false, search_count=None, incremental_origin=None), and an emacs branch in format_selection that drops the focus cell. The five search formats stay out of the accepted-native partition because their producer exists; their lifecycle is what this item still owes. `data->modekeys` is a latch, not the live option: window-copy.c reads it in `window_copy_command`'s emacs retry for previous-matching-bracket and in `window_copy_cmd_next_matching_bracket`'s vi first-closing-bracket walk, and zz now keeps the option's value on the copy session as it stood at entry. Measured on both binaries with one attached pty client on a pane holding `abcz`, `(one) [two]` and `plain text here`: with the cursor on the closing paren at 4,1, next-matching-bracket answers 0,1 under vi, which is the walk back to the opener, and 5,1 under emacs, which never takes that walk; with the cursor at 5,2 on a row with no bracket at all, previous-matching-bracket leaves it there under vi and answers 0,2 under emacs, which is `window_copy_cursor_previous_word(wme, close, 1)` with the closing-bracket string as its separator set. emacs also looks at exactly one neighbouring cell rather than scanning the line; zz keeps its wider vi scan, which is the widening this reason already recorded, and takes the pin's narrow rule for emacs. `window_copy_cursor_jump_to_back` passes `onemore` to the right step it takes after the jump, and reaching that step needed the jump reader to follow a wrap, which zz's column-range jump never did. zz's jump family is rebuilt on the pin's reader model: `jump-forward` starts one cell on, `jump-to-forward` two and then steps one left with wrapping, `jump-backward` steps one left first, and `jump-to-backward` steps two left, and both backward spellings walk onto the row a wrap carried the line from, picking that row's used length up as their right edge. Measured on a line built from each engine's own pane width so its last cell is `z` and twenty-odd more cells spill onto the continuation row: from column 3 of the continuation row, `jump-backward z` lands on the filled row at its width minus one under both spellings, while `jump-to-backward z` lands on the continuation row at column 0 under vi, because the target is the vi limit so the right step wraps, and on the filled row at exactly its width under emacs, which is the one-past column. The `scroll_only` rows in `window_copy_cursor_up` and `_down` are the last: the view moves one row either way, and under vi the cursor first steps one screen row against the scroll so it keeps the line it was on, while under emacs it keeps its screen row instead. Measured on a pane with forty lines of history behind the screen, with the cursor three rows up on L38: two `scroll-up`s answer `#{scroll_position}` 1 then 2 with `#{copy_cursor_line}` L38 both times under vi, and L37 then L36 under emacs, and a `scroll-down` answers 1 with L38 under vi and L37 under emacs. compat/scenarios/smoke/copy-mode-mode-keys-tail.txt asserts those 22 rows on both binaries. `scroll-to-mouse` is the last name in the inventory and closes as a named product decision rather than as an implementation. It is the scrollbar-drag arm: the pin binds it only from `MouseDrag1ScrollbarSlider`, measured as `bind-key -T root MouseDrag1ScrollbarSlider if-shell -F -t = "#{pane_in_mode}" { send-keys -X scroll-to-mouse } { copy-mode -S }`, and `window_copy_cmd_scroll_to_mouse` scrolls from `c->tty.mouse_slider_mpos`, the column and row where that client's tty grabbed the slider. zz answers `unknown key: MouseDrag1ScrollbarSlider` because its key vocabulary has no scrollbar keys at all: the raw TUI draws no pane scrollbar and the GPUI client owns its scrollbar entirely, so the daemon holds no slider grab to scroll from. The name stays in the Vocabulary category of the source-owned inventory with this decision beside it; reopen it if a client ever hands the daemon a slider position. Decided 2026-09-02 by the orchestrator under fabrico's instruction to close the campaign; reversible. 2026-09-03: the tail closes. The clear class is a property of the action now, not of the search runner. `CopyModeAction::clear_class` in crates/zz-terminal/src/interaction.rs carries `window_copy_cmd_table`'s clear column name by name, `clears_search_marks` folds in the `search-` prefix `window_copy_command` tests before it reads that column at all, and `apply_copy_mode_action` applies it against the live mode-keys knob, dropping `search_marks`, `search_count` and `incremental_origin` together the way the pin drops `searchmark`, `searchcount` and `searchx`/`searchy`. Correction to the sizing this record carried: the classes are 52 CLEAR_ALWAYS, 36 CLEAR_EMACS_ONLY and 7 CLEAR_NEVER, not 51/36/7, whose sum is 94 against a 95-row table. The missing row is `selection-mode`, the one entry that spells its class as the bare `0` rather than as `WINDOW_COPY_CMD_CLEAR_ALWAYS`; re-derived by splitting the table on `{ .command = ` and reading each block's own `.clear` field. A second correction fell out of the same probe: the re-lay after a clear is visible-only, because `window_copy_search` decides that from `wp->searchstr`, the pane's last search string, and not from whether the marks are still there, so `search-again` on a cleared mode lays marks with no count at all; `data->searchall` is set once, in `window_copy_init`, so a mode's first search is always full and every later search of the same string is visible-only. zz tied `visible_only` to `mode.search_marks` and now reads only the mode's remembered string. The emacs cell drop is `window_copy_get_selection`'s `keys == MODEKEY_EMACS` branch: `format_selection` takes the live spelling and stops one cell short of the bottom-right cell, while a rectangle drops that column on every row instead and only when the selection started left of the cursor, which is the `selx < data->cx` arm. The three selection builders that stand in for `window_copy_cursor_end_of_line` place their focus at the mode-keys cursor limit now rather than at the last non-blank column, which is what keeps copy-line and copy-end-of-line copying the whole line under both spellings. Measured on both binaries with one attached pty client on a second window holding `alpha beta gamma`, `delta alpha epsilon` and `zeta alpha` echoed twice by cat, reading `#{copy_cursor_x},#{copy_cursor_y}|#{search_present}|#{search_match}|#{search_count}|#{search_count_partial}|#{search_timed_out}`. Under vi: `search-forward alpha` 6,1|1|alpha|6|0|0, `cursor-down` (CLEAR_EMACS_ONLY, so nothing happens) 6,2|1|alpha|6|0|0, `search-again` 0,3|1|alpha|6|0|0, `begin-selection` (CLEAR_ALWAYS) 0,3|0||||0, `toggle-position` (CLEAR_NEVER) 6,1|1|alpha|6|0|0 and `back-to-indentation` (CLEAR_ALWAYS, not the emacs-only class its neighbours carry) 0,1|0||||0. Under emacs the same six answer 5,0|1|alpha|6|0|0, 5,1|0||||0, 11,1|1|alpha|||0 with the count gone, 11,1|0||||0, 5,0|1|alpha|6|0|0 and 0,0|0||||0. The incremental origin follows the same reset: history-top, `search-forward-incremental =alpha`, three `cursor-down`s, `search-forward-incremental =zeta` answers 0,2|1|zeta|2|0|0 under vi, where the origin is still the first prompt's row, and 4,5|1|zeta|2|0|0 under emacs, where the clear put searchx back to -1 and the second prompt latched at row 3. `begin-selection`, four `cursor-right`s and `copy-selection` buffer `alpha` under vi and `alph` under emacs, and with `rectangle-on` and a `cursor-down` before the copy, `alpha`/`delta` under vi and `alph`/`delt` under emacs. Those 22 answers extend compat/scenarios/smoke/copy-mode-mode-keys-tail.txt from 22 rows to 44 on both binaries. `window_copy_cursor_previous_word`'s `stop_at_eol`, the fourth read the eleven-place enumeration missed, is measured and recorded as a divergence zz cannot follow rather than implemented. It fires only when the row the backward walk steps onto ends in a cell `grid_in_set` calls whitespace, and `grid_line_length` trims trailing spaces, so the only cell that can sit there is a tab: `grid_in_set` answers a TAB cell's width for the WHITESPACE set, and `grid_line_length` keeps the cell because its data is not a single space. Probed on the pin with a pane holding `alpha` followed by a tab, then `gamma delta`, cursor at 0,1: `previous-word` answers 0,0 under vi and 8,0 under emacs, the tab-stop column the emacs limit allows, and a second `previous-word` brings emacs back to 0,0. zz's engine has no tab cell at all, because libghostty-vt runs HT as a cursor move and leaves blanks behind, so no row in a zz revision can end in a whitespace cell and the branch is unreachable rather than unimplemented; reopen it if the engine ever grows tab cells. One divergence was measured beside this work and belongs to the CLI rather than to the copy engine: zz's `show-buffer` ends its output with a newline the pin does not add, measured on both binaries with a five-byte `alpha` buffer that `#{buffer_size}` reports as 5 on both while `show-buffer | od -c` shows `a l p h a` on the pin and `a l p h a \n` on zz, which is why the scenario reads the buffer back through `save-buffer`. The first acceptance clause was re-scoped; it read: "A source-owned inventory keeps all 95 pinned window-copy action names classified: the 66 mapped names retain typed mux and terminal behavior, and the 29 missing names stay explicit across the seven action categories until each has measured behavior or a named product decision." Its mapped and missing counts were the ones this record started from in August; crates/zz-mux/src/copy_actions.rs has asserted 95 pinned names with one missing, `scroll-to-mouse`, since the search family stopped being a client surface on 2026-09-02, so the clause was rewritten to the counts the code holds while its seven-category promise was kept. Decided 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator under fabrico's instruction to close the campaign; reversible. One scope divergence stays open and is recorded rather than closed: the pin's remembered search string is pane-scoped and outlives the mode, zz's is mode-scoped. window-copy.c:566-569 copies wp->searchstr into data->searchstr at every window_copy_init, so a re-entered copy mode inherits the previous search; zz builds its mode with search: None (crates/zz-terminal/src/session.rs) and drop_view_search clears the view slot on cancel, so search-again finds neither the mode's string nor a view search. Measured on both binaries with the same 80x24 pane holding 'alpha beta' / 'delta alpha' / 'zeta alpha' and the format '#{copy_cursor_x},#{copy_cursor_y}|#{search_present}|#{search_match}|#{search_count}': the first search answers 0,0|1|alpha|3 on both, a re-entered mode answers 0,3|0||0 on both before any search, and then search-again answers 5,2|1|alpha|3 on the pin and leaves zz at 0,3|0||0. visible_only itself is faithful; only the string's lifetime differs. Reopen behind a pane-scoped search string if a scenario needs it.

closed.title: Complete copy-mode command fidelity
closed.resolution: flag:copy-mode:-s closed on 2026-09-02, the last item in the group. window_copy_init reads its screen from wme->swp, so the revision a -s entry needs is built on the source pane's own worker: the mux emits MuxEffect::ArmCopyModeSource, which is daemon-local, the daemon captures the source's ModeRevision through a synchronous terminal command outside the state lock, and the target's worker takes it as the backing of the copy mode the following entry opens. window_copy_clone_screen's trim runs only when wme->swp differs from wme->wp: it drops the source's trailing blank rows and moves the cursor to column zero on the last used row whenever the source's own cursor sat past them, which zz reproduces from the same used-row scan the scroll-on-clear rewrite uses, and the view opens at the bottom because window_copy_init leaves data->oy at 0 for a clone. window_copy_refresh_start refuses a view of another pane, so the mode carries a sourced bit that refuses refresh-on in the terminal and keeps the daemon's refresh timer off the session. Measured against the pin on 2026-09-02 with one attached pty client, a source pane holding SRC1 through SRC5 and a target holding DST1 through DST5: `copy-mode -s %0 -t %1` put %1 in copy-mode and left %0 with no mode entry at all, `#{copy_cursor_line}` answered SRC5 with `#{copy_cursor_x}` 0, `send-keys -t %1 -N 3 -X cursor-up` walked it to SRC2 and one cursor-down to SRC3, `send-keys -t %0 -X cursor-up` still answered `not in a mode` at status 1, `capture-pane -p -t %1` still held the five DST lines and no SRC line because the mode never replaced the pane's own grid, `refresh-on` followed by a new SRC6 on the source left the cursor line where it was, and `copy-mode -s %1 -t %1` parked on the live cursor row instead of the last used row, which is the trim staying off when the source is the target. compat/scenarios/smoke/copy-mode-source-pane.txt asserts those 19 facts on both binaries. catalog.rs promoted -s from an unsupported value to a real pane option; -S stays unsupported, so the pinned usage override remains. The group's acceptance asked for the initial scroll position as well; that clause was answered by semantic:copy-mode-command-counts on 2026-09-02, which measured the family at entry from the -c client. The -k and headless-target notes this group carried live on in clients.interactive-refresh, which still owns semantic:copy-mode-headless-target: a detached `copy-mode -t` answers `pane is not attached` on zz, which is why this scenario drives an attached pty client.
