Gate fix 2026-09-02: MuxEffect::ArmCopyModeSource parks the source on the daemon until the TerminalView effect enters the mode, and the first cut only took it after the attached-client and read-only checks, so a `copy-mode -s %1 -t %0` that failed with `pane is not attached` left the source armed and the next plain `copy-mode -t %0` would have cloned %1's screen; the effect arm now takes the armed source up front beside the armed kill and uses it only on the path that reaches the entry, with copy_mode_source_does_not_survive_an_errored_entry as the regression test.

closed.title: Place fixed copy-mode rows at column zero
closed.resolution: The top-line, middle-line, and bottom-line actions now move the copy cursor to column zero at the current frozen viewport's top, middle, or bottom row. Each action preserves the viewport offset and bounds its target to the retained revision. The full zz-terminal library suite passes 197 tests. This close covers only those three fixed-row placements; it does not claim history-bottom, logical-line, scrolling, wrapping, or wider action fidelity, which remains active under copy-mode.action-fidelity.

closed.title: Match remaining display-menu behavior
closed.resolution: Row shortcuts now go through the pin's own key parser and keep only the spellings a client attached to the menu can press, and an owning-client resize re-fits the live descriptor the way menu_resize_cb does: the box keeps its width, rows, selection, stay-open policy and commands, takes the new client and cell geometry, slides back inside the viewport, parks at the origin when it no longer fits, and never closes. Rows are now built against the client's own cells the way menu_add_item does: the room is the client columns less four, an action key is annotated when its bracketed form fits a quarter of that room or the whole name still fits beside it, otherwise only the annotation is dropped while the row keeps answering the key, and an overlong name keeps its last cells through format_trim_right's reading and gains the `>` marker, so a name past the room trims instead of shedding the whole descriptor. The drawn key and the pressed key are separate wire facts on protocol v90 (MenuItem.annotation). Descriptor action queues, refresh behavior, mouse handling, and close-mid-paste ordering still need focused comparison with the pin. One measured residue: the pin reads row enablement from the post-trim name (menu_key_cb skips rows via the stored name's leading '-'), so a disabled row whose overlong name loses its '-' to format_trim_right answers its action key on the pin; zz derives enablement from the pre-trim name and keeps such a row inert. Drawn names match either way; probed live on a 40-column client with a '-' plus 200-cell name. Queue ordering and action context closed on 2026-09-01 against clients attached on real ptys on both binaries (scenario display-menu-action-queue). display-menu holds the command queue while the menu is up, so a chained command has not run yet; leaving the menu lets the chain run either way, and choosing a row runs that row's action first while cancelling runs nothing. menu_add_item expands each row and each row command through format_single with the menu's own target client, so `#{client_name}` in an action names the menu's client and not the one that typed the command; zz was expanding those values with no client at all and produced an empty string, and now seeds the format facts from the target client the way the pin seeds `c`. The menu is already gone when its action runs, proved by an action that opens a second menu and answers its own key. A failing action neither fails display-menu nor stops the chain, and cmdq_error puts the message on that client's status line with the first letter raised for a run-time failure and a parse failure alike; zz was leaving the first letter alone on the menu path and now raises it. One measured residue the probe reads around: the pin draws the whole message across the status line, while zz's raw TUI clips it to the room its own sidebar and detach hint leave, so the probe compares the message prefix. A second measured divergence, found while probing overlay replacement for the chooser flags: display-menu -c on a client that already has a chooser open leaves the client's keys with the chooser in zz, so the menu's item never runs and the key that would have chosen it cancels the chooser instead, where the pin's menu takes the key and leaves the pane mode underneath alone. Mouse policy, close-mid-paste ordering, and style refresh still need their own comparison. Style refresh closed on 2026-09-01 against clients attached on real ptys on both binaries (scenario display-menu-style-refresh). menu_draw_cb calls menu_reapply_styles on every draw, so menu-style, menu-selected-style and menu-border-style are read again each time, and they are read from the current window of the session the menu's own client is attached to rather than from the window the command targeted; menu_reapply_styles gives up entirely when that client has no session. Since options_push_changes redraws every client that has a session after any set-option, a style set while the menu is up repaints the live box with no key pressed: measured with menu-selected-style moved from fg=colour46 to fg=colour214 on an attached 80x24 client, which redrew the selected row as ESC[38;5;214m with nothing typed. menu-border-lines is not part of that: menu_prepare copies it into the menu once and menu_draw_cb never reads it again, so setting it to double while the menu is up left the box drawing the same single-line glyphs. The command line -s, -H and -S styles are folded into the option-derived cell rather than replacing it: style_parse is read back for its foreground and background alone, both landing on the default when the command line names neither, so an attribute the option asked for survives a -s that carries none and a colour the option asked for is dropped when the command line names only the other half. Measured with menu-style 'bold,bg=colour17' plus display-menu -s 'fg=colour160', which drew the unselected row as ESC[38;5;160m ESC[1m with no 48;5;17 anywhere. A style style_parse rejects is dropped whole and leaves the option's cell alone. zz now composes the same cell and republishes the live overlay whenever a command changes what the option resolves to. semantic:display-menu-mouse-policy and semantic:display-menu-paste-close-ordering stay open. Mouse policy and paste ordering stay open, with the pin read at d77c9dc6 rather than driven: menu_key_cb treats a mouse move with no button held as highlight-only, because such a move reports as a release and a menu opened without a button already down would otherwise vanish as the pointer crossed it; with MENU_NOMOUSE any button other than 1 leaves the menu and button 1 is ignored; the hit box is px..px+4+width by py+1..py+1+count-1, so the title row and the bottom border sit outside it; outside that box a release that is not such a move closes a menu without MENU_STAYOPEN while a stay-open menu closes only on an event that is neither release, wheel nor drag, and either way the highlight is cleared and the overlay redrawn; inside it the same split chooses the row under the pointer instead of closing. For paste, server_client_handle_key0 hands every key to c->overlay_key before the command queue, and a bracketed paste arrives as one KEYC_PASTE_START event carrying the whole buffer; menu_key_cb matches it against no row key and no navigation key and answers 0, so the menu stays open and the pasted bytes are swallowed whole. The paste_key path that would have called window_pane_paste is never reached while an overlay owns the key, which is why the pin leaks nothing to the pane and runs no action twice. The style refresh republishes the whole menu, and the cycle-6 review measured that both zz clients rebuilt their cursor from it: open a two-row menu, press Down, `set-window-option menu-style` from another client, press Enter, and the pin runs the second row where zz ran the first, because menu_reapply_styles rewrites three grid cells and never touches md->choice. The raw TUI and the GPUI menu now keep their live cursor across a republish, clamped to the new item count, and seed from the daemon's selected row only on a fresh open; the style-refresh scenario presses Down before its restyles and checks that Enter still runs the second row. semantic:display-menu-mouse-policy and semantic:display-menu-paste-close-ordering closed on 2026-09-02 against pinned tmux d77c9dc6 with clients attached on real ptys on both binaries (scenarios display-menu-mouse and display-menu-paste). The reason recorded here on 2026-09-01 described both from a reading of menu_key_cb alone, and driving them refuted two of its claims, so both are re-scoped against the measurement. First refutation: the reason said a bracketed paste 'arrives as one KEYC_PASTE_START event carrying the whole buffer' which 'menu_key_cb matches against no row key', so 'the pasted bytes are swallowed whole'. tty_keys turns ESC[200~ and ESC[201~ into KEYC_PASTE_START and KEYC_PASTE_END and every character between them into its own key, and server_client_handle_key0 hands c->overlay_key each of them before the queue, so only the two markers are swallowed by menu_key_cb's fall-through while every pasted character is answered exactly as if it had been typed. Measured on an attached 80x24 pin client with a two-row menu keyed a and b: pasting ZW left the menu up with nothing run, pasting q closed it with nothing run, and pasting ZaXY ran the row a names and then put XY in the pane, so the characters after the close reach the pane as ordinary keys rather than as a bracketed paste - the markers were already consumed. Nothing leaks while the menu is up and no action runs twice. zz's raw TUI consumed a whole TerminalEvent::Paste; it now walks the run through the same menu key resolver character by character (zz-client resolve_menu_paste), keeps the live cursor a navigation character moves, and hands the tail after a closing character to the pane through the ordinary paste route. Second refutation: the reason described the hit box and the highlight-only move as if they applied to every menu. They do not. cmd_display_menu_exec sets MENU_NOMOUSE whenever the command carries no invoking mouse event and no -M, which is every display-menu typed on a command line, and that arm answers only MOUSE_BUTTON_1: MOUSE_BUTTONS(b) == 0 returns 0 and is ignored whole, anything else returns 1 and leaves the menu with nothing chosen. Since MOUSE_MASK_BUTTONS is 195, a button-1 press (b 0) and a drag with button 1 (b 32) are both ignored while a release (b 3), a motion with no button held (b 35) and a wheel (b 64) all leave. menu_prepare also resolves starting_choice only under MENU_NOMOUSE, so a -M menu opens with md->choice at -1 and Enter closes it with nothing to run, where a command-line menu opens on its first selectable row. Both measured on the pin. The full policy, proved with -M on both binaries: the box is drawn at md->px, md->py with menu->width + 4 by menu->count + 2 cells, and -y is anchored at the bottom (cmd_display_menu_get_pos subtracts the height), so -x 5 -y 5 on a two-row menu draws the top border on row 1 and the rows on rows 2 and 3. The hit box is px..px+4+width by py+1..py+1+count-1, so the title row in the top border and the bottom border are outside it while the column one past the right border is inside. A press or a motion inside moves the highlight; a release reaches `chosen` before md->choice is rewritten from the pointer row, so it runs the row the press left the highlight on and not the row under the pointer; a press outside only clears the highlight while a release outside closes a menu that is not stay-open; a motion outside clears the highlight, after which Enter closes with nothing to run. A stay-open menu instead closes on any report that is neither a release, a wheel nor a drag. Protocol v94 appends MenuState.mouse_keys so the client knows which policy it is drawing, the daemon sets it from -M and publishes selected as None for such a menu, and both the shared resolver in zz-client and the raw TUI route follow it. Two divergences are recorded rather than copied. zz has no invoking-mouse-event context in ExecutionContext, so only -M turns the full policy on; a menu the pin raises from a mouse key binding gets it there without the flag, which belongs with mouse.bound-context. And the GPUI menu stays native chrome: a left click on a row chooses it whatever mouse_keys says, because a desktop menu that ignores its own click is not a product zz ships. One paste edge is recorded: the tail typed after a menu's closing character reaches the pane through TerminalViewAction::Paste, and write_paste_bytes re-brackets it when the pane's application has bracketed paste on, where the pin delivers that tail as plain keys because menu_key_cb already consumed the ESC[200~/ESC[201~ markers; identical for the fixture's `cat`, a fresh bracketed paste versus keystrokes for an application that reads the mode.

closed.title: List display-message format variables
closed.resolution: display-message -a walks format_each and both items close against the re-scoped measurement. The expander gained a per-variable, per-context declines answer: `format_listing` walks the same 198-entry FORMAT_VARIABLES table in declaration order, skips every entry whose pin callback would return NULL, and then appends the command's own tree entries in key order, which is `command` for an ordinary command. The declines rule is derived name by name from format.c rather than from an empty value: the scope gate reproduces the `ft->s`, `ft->wl` and `ft->wp` null checks, the whole Client family is gated on the `format_cb_client_name` witness (with client_mode_format excluded, because its callback reads a global option, exactly like buffer_mode_format), the mouse_* names and the six session_group names never answer, session_attached_list and window_active_clients_list decline when their evbuffer would be empty, the three pane_dead names decline on a live pane, session_active needs a client as well as a session, and the delegated names decline when the daemon producer declines. One listing-only rule came out of the measurement: `format_each` prints a FORMAT_TABLE_TIME entry as tv_sec while `format_find` turns a zero time into NULL, so `session_last_attached=0` appears in the listing where the same name expands empty; the seven time entries whose callback answers whenever their scope object exists carry that fallback and buffer_created and pane_dead_time, the two that really do return NULL, do not. Four producer corrections were needed to make the sets match, each one the pin's behaviour: client_last_session and client_theme now decline instead of answering empty (THEME_UNKNOWN is a NULL, and the daemon now records a colour scheme only for a client that reported one rather than assuming the server's active scheme at registration); window_active_clients and window_active_clients_list are answered for command expansions from a new per-window client fact, where they used to be filled only on the status path and answered 0 and empty everywhere else; and session_attached_list now joins `client_format_name`, the tty for a pty client, where it used to join the device name the hello carries, which is what `loop->name` is in format_cb_session_attached_list. Proved by compat/scenarios/smoke/format-listing.txt on both binaries, 26 checks: 143 lines for a pane with no client, alphabetical table pass with `command=display-message` last, the 56 declining names named one by one, 172 lines with an attached client, the 28 added back named one by one, nothing removed by attaching, and the values both binaries own outright (wrap_flag=1, session_grouped=0, pane_pipe=0, pane_unseen_changes=0, session_last_attached=0, pane_index=0, window_bigger=0, session_active=1, client_theme=dark). -a runs before the template is looked at, so -l, a trailing message and a missing -p all leave the listing at 143 lines while the -F conflict is still refused first; the flag is promoted in catalog.rs. Two facts the fixture had to work around are recorded rather than claimed. client_theme is THEME_UNKNOWN on the pin under a dumb pty, so the pin's client answers nothing until the terminal replies to the `\033[?996n` query; the zz raw client hard-codes dark in its hello, so the differential makes the pin's client report dark with `\033[?997;1n` and both sides then list the name. And the mouse_* names decline here because no mouse event is in the tree; inside a mouse binding the pin answers them and zz does not, which belongs to formats.mouse-context.

closed.title: Honor display-message ignore-keys
closed.resolution: The catalog accepts display-message -N, and the mux carries its ignore-keys value to the daemon without changing the wire protocol. A positive-effective-duration ordinary Interactive display-message writes the destination client's sticky bit: -N sets it and a plain message clears it. Omitted -d resolves from the destination client's attached session, independent of the pane selected by -t; explicit -d still wins. A positive-duration Interactive PrintOrMessage producer also clears the bit. Explicit or inherited zero duration, clear, expiry, -p, Control clients, a missing destination client, -a, and -I leave it unchanged; detach keeps it with the registered client, while unregister removes it. An active message with the bit set drops writable terminal Key, standalone or paired Text, Paste, non-hover Mouse and wheel input, and ClientFocus before message dismissal, display-panes teardown, prompt handling, key dispatch, and activity accounting, so the message and terminal-publication freeze remain active. An ignored release retires its swallowed press decision without forwarding. Without -N, non-hover mouse and wheel input dismiss an active message; retaining bare hover is an intentional zz presentation adaptation. Ignored presses create their typed pending entry and suppression debt under the same daemon lock, using the committed character from KeyInput.text. Text matching selects the first entry with the same pane and lane, retires the skipped queue prefix and its linked debt, then retires the matched debt while preserving the later suffix. Browser-before-terminal ordering preserves the later terminal debt; terminal-before-browser ordering retires the skipped terminal debt as stale. Read-only input and native BrowserSurface input keep their prior paths. Focused daemon tests cover sticky replacement, destination-session zero and nonzero inheritance, PrintOrMessage reset, expiry, clear, missing-target CANFAIL, inert branches, unregister, every ignored input form, modal ordering, activity, committed text in both lane orders, release cleanup, read-only bypass, and browser-native input. The strict display-message scenario proves -N and -p -N acceptance beside target-client CANFAIL behavior.

closed.title: Complete display-message pane target grammar
closed.resolution: The client slot is resolved daemon-side rather than by threading a client handle through the mux resolver. cmd-find.c reads `@`, `{active}` and `{current}` off `cmdq_get_client(item)->session->curw->window->active`, so the daemon now pre-resolves exactly those three whole-target spellings from the invoking client and rewrites `-t` to the resolved pane; when that client has no session, which is every command client, it reports through the same channel `cmdq_error` uses. `route_source_error` is that channel: a Command client gets the line on stderr and `c->retval = 1` without the command failing, so the rest of the sequence still runs, which is what `CMD_FIND_CANFAIL` gives the pin. Measured on both binaries in smoke/display-message-client-aliases, 25 checks: `-t @`, `-t {active}` and `-t {current}` each print `no current client` on stderr, exit 1, and still write the command's empty expansion `S=|W=|P=` to stdout; `{last}`, `{marked}` and `~` stay quiet misses at exit 0 with the same empty expansion; a chained `set-environment` after the failing alias still runs and the whole sequence exits 1. One clause was re-measured rather than assumed: the earlier reason called the componentwise `a:1.@` case `a pane-slot @ that exits 0`, which is right about the status but not about the state. `cmd_find_get_pane_with_window` misses on `@`, `cmd_find_get_window` then resolves it as a window, and `fs->wp` falls back to that window's active pane, so `-t <session>:<window>.@` answers the real session, window and active pane on both binaries, not an empty state. The differential asserts that measured shape. The rewrite is scoped to display-message because that is where the group scoped it; every other CMD_FIND_PANE command still resolves the three aliases to nothing at status 0, and a client-aware resolver signature across zz-mux remains the general fix.

closed.title: Target display-message clients
closed.resolution: The catalog accepts display-message -c, the mux preserves the destination selector independently from -t, and the daemon resolves it against attached clients by exact client name, device name, full tty, tty without /dev/, or one trailing-colon variant. A nonprinting command with a missing destination quietly does nothing. The pin's CANFAIL target state falls forward componentwise: a missing session leaves pane, window, and session facts empty; a resolved session with a missing window uses that session's current window and active pane; and a resolved window with a missing pane uses that window's active pane. Nonprinting calls stay quiet and successful, while -p expands the retained or empty context, including when -c also misses. Parse, arity, delay, and ambiguous-target failures retain their earlier precedence. Nonprinting Interactive messages, freeze, replacement, and sticky -N state belong to the destination client. Omitted -d inherits display-time from that client's attached session rather than the independent -t pane session; explicit -d overrides it. Control destinations receive only their message event, and read-only destinations can receive a message while read-only callers remain subject to command authorization. Format client facts use the destination only when it belongs to the independently retained pane target's session; otherwise an attached target session uses its best client. Printing returns through the caller, uses the same destination-or-fallback format facts, and never arms message state. At this checkpoint, an attached target session with no -c still supplied no client facts under clients.context-formats; the protocol v83 closure now selects that session's best client. The later display-message.unattached-session-client-fallback closure handles the distinct valid-unattached-target widening. Focused tests cover same-session and cross-session formats and durations, exact-name CANFAIL targets, missing and aliased clients, caller-versus-destination delivery, freeze, -N inheritance, Control, read-only, and printing. The strict 27-step scenario creates a second window, proves that a missing pane retains that distinct valid window, and covers the missing-window and missing-session clauses with and without -c. Bare mouse targets and relative or special target grammar remain separately tracked. The change adds no wire fields or protocol version.

closed.title: Widen client fallback for unattached target sessions
closed.resolution: For a valid display-message target whose session has no attached clients, format expansion selects the globally most-active attached client when -c is absent, resolves to another session, or misses. Client activity orders candidates, and the oldest-created client wins an equal-activity tie. client_session comes from that selected client's actual attachment, while session, window, and pane facts remain scoped to the retained -t target. With zero attached clients, client facts stay empty; a missing target session leaves client, session, window, and pane facts empty through the existing CANFAIL path. At this checkpoint, an attached target session without -c still supplied no client facts under clients.context-formats; the protocol v83 closure now selects that session's best client. The fallback changes only the display-message command-format hook. Delivery, duration selection, printing routing and lifecycle, buffer-path context, and Command-client selection are unchanged. Sequential zz-daemon tests pass 599/599. Focused daemon coverage proves global activity selection and zero-client behavior; scoped attached-client probes pass on zz and pinned tmux for absent, cross-session, and unresolved -c cases. The debug build, strict daemon clippy, and fmt pass. One independent run completed the attached-client harness, but later current runs passed the scoped fallback probes and then failed at unrelated nested-attach terminal-query interleaving. The full harness is not stably green, and this close makes no canonical-suite claim.

closed.title: Trace display-message format expansion
closed.resolution: display-message -v prints the pin's ordered parse and replacement trace ahead of the result, and the corpus the acceptance names is asserted on both binaries by compat/scenarios/smoke/format-trace.txt (29 steps): a plain lookup, a missing name, a shorthand, a nested conditional, a condition the tree does not hold, the empty-string and last-arg branches, a modifier with arguments, a literal, both signs of the length limit, both signs of the padding width, a comparison, a substitution, the length and width post-transforms, a style body carrying a format, the ## style escape, the #, and ## character escapes, -v without -p, and -v with -l. Every trace line matches the pin byte for byte, including the indentation: format_log1 writes `#`, then es->loop spaces taken from a ten-space literal, and zz's expander logs at depth + 1 from expand while expand_replacement, which is called with depth + 1, logs at its own depth, so the two agree by construction. Both structural mismatches the earlier reason recorded were re-measured. THE FIRST WAS ALREADY GONE: zz's build_modifiers already expands each modifier argument while it parses the list and already implements the pin's punctuation-wrapper rule, so the `expanding format: 3` / `result is: 3` pair at depth three falls out of the existing structure and no expansion had to be moved. What was left of it was one line of bracket accounting: format_skip1's counter is signed, so the unmatched `}` in `#{=#{@three}:pane_title}` drives it below zero and no later `:` is ever seen at depth zero, the whole modifier list fails to parse, and the body is expanded as a plain format. zz's find_modifier_argument clamped that counter at zero, so it parsed the modifier and answered the plain title where the pin answers the literal `=3:pane_title`; the counter is signed now and both binaries answer `=3:pane_title` with the same trace, while `#{s/#{@three}/X/:pane_title}` still substitutes and `#{I/c:X}`'s body is still never expanded. THE SECOND MISMATCH STANDS AND HAS NO SITE: zz has no counterpart for format_check_time or the strftime overflow, so `reached time limit (N)` and `format is too long` cannot occur and are not faked. Beside those, the following pin lines have no reachable site in zz's expander and are recorded rather than emitted: the loop family (`session loop:`, `window loop:`, `window loop but no session`, `window name but no session`, `pane loop:`, `pane loop but no window`, `option loop:` in both forms, `environment loop:`, `client loop:`), whose zz implementations expand each row through a sub-expander that shares the trace sink, so the nested `expanding format:` and `found #{}:` lines inside a loop body do appear but the per-row header line does not; the expression family of seven (`expression has no valid operator:`, `expression precision`, `expression syntax error`, `expression left side is invalid:`, `expression right side is invalid:`, `expression left side is:`, `expression right side is:`, `expression result is`) and `operator %s has operand:`, which zz's expand_expression computes without the pin's staged operand parse; and the two content-search lines (`search '%s' but no pane`, `search '%s' pane %%%u`) and `repeat syntax error:`, whose zz implementations return a value without a matching decision point. Everything else in format.c is emitted: the expand frame (reached loop limit, expanding format, after time expanded, result is), the finds (found #{}, found #(), #() result, found #*N[, found #c, found #c: name), the modifier pair, the lookup pair plus expanding inner format, the conditional six, the comparison three, the post-transforms (substitute, applied length limit, applied padding width, replacing with length, replacing with width), the literal string, and the tail (replaced 'X' with 'Y', failed X). One line zz emits from a different site: a `#S` shorthand reads the format table directly instead of going through format_replace, so its `format 'session_name' found:` and `replaced 'session_name' with:` lines are written beside the `found #S:` line rather than by a nested replacement, which is why the pin and zz print the same three lines for it. -v was already carried as CommandOptionSpec::unsupported_flag on display-message and is promoted to a real flag, so the catalog's (supported, unsupported) counters move 469/34 -> 470/33 and the spec usage gains the v; PINNED_TMUX_USAGE_OVERRIDES already spelled the pin usage with v, so its length is unchanged at 20. One pre-existing divergence the corpus had to route around and which is not this group's: `display-message -p` of an empty expansion prints one empty line on the pin and prints nothing on zz, so the missing-name and unset-option rows wrap their result in angle brackets.

closed.title: Execute display-panes selection templates
closed.resolution: display-panes carries its optional template through the mux effect and runs it when a pane is chosen. cmd_display_panes_exec prepares the template with args_make_commands_prepare and `select-pane -t "%%%"` as the default command, and cmd_display_panes_key substitutes the chosen pane's `%id` as argument 1 before appending the result to the queue, so the trailing `%` in the default is cmd_template_replace's quoting form, not a third substitution. zz builds the same template in the mux (ARGS_PARSE_COMMANDS_OR_STRING, so a `{ ... }` block keeps its parsed command list) and the daemon runs it through the path command-prompt already used, now shared as submit_template with the origin name as its only difference. Proved on attached pty clients on both binaries in smoke/display-panes-template: a template that records the chosen pane answers `chose-<%id>` for the second pane, the omitted template selects that pane, and a template that fails at run time closes the overlay, leaves both panes alive, and lets the rest of the chain follow. One measured divergence stays open and belongs to the command-queue foundation rather than to this group: cmd_display_panes_key inserts the template after the issuing item with cmdq_get_state(item), so the template's printed output and its error status both stay with the command client that raised the overlay on the pin, while zz's submit_template runs the result in the interactive client's context. `display-panes -t C -d 0 'display-message -p "chose %%%"'` from a CLI prints `chose %1` on that CLI's stdout on the pin and nothing on zz, and `display-panes -t C -d 0 'kill-pane -t nosuchpanename'` exits 1 with `can't find pane: nosuchpanename` on the CLI's stderr on the pin and 0 with nothing on zz. The differential asserts what both sides agree on; the residue is carried by the reasons of pane.command-completion and control-mode.disconnect-cancels-command-queue, the foundation groups that own queue-state routing.

closed.title: Fall through display-panes Escape and unmatched input
closed.resolution: A writable valid display-panes selection is consumed without activity. An unmatched raw key or native GPUI Close tears down the overlay and then follows ordinary key dispatch and activity accounting; Close synthesizes Escape so its press falls through while its later release remains swallowed. Non-hover mouse press, drag, release, and wheel input likewise close the overlay before following ordinary terminal-view input, including latest-geometry and bell accounting. Bare buttonless Motion remains consumed without activity as a deliberate native hover-presentation choice. A deadline timeout closes the overlay without fabricating input or activity. Read-only raw keys and Close bypass overlay consumption into root-table resolution, native selection is rejected after activity and latest-geometry accounting, and safe local view actions reach the pane; each retains the overlay and preserves the pane bell.

closed.title: Wait for display-panes overlays
closed.resolution: cmd_display_panes_exec returns CMD_RETURN_WAIT unless -b, and cmd_display_panes_free calls cmdq_continue, so the issuing queue resumes whichever way the overlay ends. zz now parks a command or control invoker on a waiter stored in DisplayPanesSession; the waiter is released when the session is dropped, which take_display_panes, the deadline expiry, overlay dismissal and client disconnect all do, and a selection holds it until the template's own commands have run. Measured on both binaries in smoke/display-panes-template with an attached pty client: with -d 0 a chained set-environment stays pending until a pane is chosen and then runs, -b returns at exit 0 with the template still unrun and its answer landing later, -d 700 releases the chain after the timer with the template unrun, and -N keeps the wait while dropping the key handler so only the timer ends it. The wait is only installed for Command and Control invokers, the same limit display-menu already carries: zz executes an interactive client's own commands on the thread that would have to deliver the answering key, so blocking there would deadlock. That is a real divergence from the pin, where a key binding's queue blocks too, and it is the same foundation control-mode.disconnect-cancels-command-queue and pane.command-completion need. Two edges the first close left undisclosed were measured on attached pty clients at the 2026-09-02 gate and are now enforced. First, a second display-panes on a client that already draws one returns at once: cmd_display_panes_exec's first line is `if (tc->overlay_draw != NULL) return (CMD_RETURN_NORMAL)`, so with invoker A parked on the overlay and B issued from a second command client the pin answers B at exit 0 immediately, keeps A parked, and the key runs A's template only. zz's effect arm replaced the overlay through dismiss_overlays plus take_display_panes, which woke A with its template unrun and its chain already continued, parked B instead, and ran B's template; the route now answers a busy target with an empty execution before the mux runs, and smoke/display-panes-template checks all four facts (24 checks). zz checks only its own display-panes state where the pin checks any overlay_draw, so a menu or popup on the target does not make display-panes a no-op in zz. Second, a hook body never parks. Hook commands run with no client, and the thread that runs client-attached and session-created hooks is the reader of the connection that raised them: with `set-hook -g client-attached "command-prompt -p hook 'set-environment -g HOOKCP %%'"`, a client killed without detaching stayed in list-clients indefinitely on zz because its reader was blocked in the prompt waiter and never read the socket EOF, where the pin reaps it within a second, and the phantom then won resolve_client_target for later prompts so a live client's answer never landed. Both waits are now gated on the context having a client, so a hook-raised prompt or display-panes opens and returns the way -b does; key-binding hooks answer on both binaries either way (bind F1 select-pane with an after-select-pane command-prompt).

closed.title: Match remaining display-popup behavior
closed.resolution: A popup now keeps the origin and size it asked for and rebuilds the live box from them on every owning-client resize the way popup_resize_cb does — the smaller of the request and the viewport, the preferred origin whenever it fits, the clamped one when it does not, and the job resized to the content box — proved against the pin in scenario display-popup-resize-lifecycle. Style refresh, native popup pointer affordances, popup-to-pane conversion, and popup Kitty image presentation remain separate cross-daemon and client fidelity work. Real mouse and status format facts remain under formats.mouse-context; Control presentation and read-only popup policy keep their existing native-client owners. Style refresh closed on 2026-09-01 against clients attached on real ptys on both binaries (scenario display-popup-style-refresh). popup_draw_cb calls popup_reapply_styles on every draw, so popup-style and popup-border-style are read again each time from the current window of the session the popup's own client is attached to, and options_push_changes redraws every client with a session after any set-option, so a style set while the popup is up repaints the live box with no key pressed; measured with popup-border-style moved from fg=colour129 to fg=colour118 on an attached 80x24 client. popup-border-lines is copied into the popup when it is created and never read again, so setting it to double while the popup was up left the box on its single-line glyphs. The command line -s and -S styles are folded in the same way display-menu folds -s: style_parse is read back for its foreground and background alone, so an option attribute survives a -S that names none and an option colour is dropped when the command line names only the other half, and a style style_parse rejects is dropped whole. One measured residue stays open: popup_reapply_styles then zeroes the attribute field of both popup cells (pd->defaults.attr = 0 and pd->border_cell.attr = 0), so popup-style 'bold,bg=colour18,fg=colour190' drew ESC[38;5;190m ESC[48;5;18m with no ESC[1m on the pin, while zz carries the attribute to the client and draws it; that belongs with the non-colour half of the appearance bridge rather than with this refresh. semantic:display-popup-border-drag, semantic:display-popup-context-menu, semantic:display-popup-kitty-images and semantic:display-popup-to-pane stay open: the pin drives all three of the first from popup_key_cb's mouse arm, where button 3 on the left or top border (or anywhere outside the popup) raises the popup_menu_items menu (Close/Paste/Fill Space/Centre/To Horizontal Pane/To Vertical Pane), a meta drag or a drag started on a border moves the popup with button 1 and resizes it with button 3, and popup_make_pane hands the popup's job and screen to a freshly split pane through job_transfer. semantic:display-popup-kitty-images has no oracle to copy: the pinned tree has no kitty graphics support anywhere in its source and popup.c carries no ENABLE_SIXEL branch either, so popup content goes through input_parse_screen into the popup's own screen with no image path at all. The item is a zz-native presentation contract for the popup terminal rather than a fidelity gap, and closing it means proving zz's own rendering, replacement and close cleanup on an attached client. For paste, popup_key_cb answers a KEYC_PASTE_START with 0 whenever the popup has a job, so the bytes in the event buffer are dropped rather than written to the job, and a POPUP_CLOSEANYKEY popup explicitly excludes paste and mouse keys from the any-key close. semantic:display-popup-kitty-images stays open pending an attached-client proof. The pin measurement that makes this a zz contract rather than a fidelity gap was taken again at d77c9dc6: the string `kitty` appears zero times across every .c and .h file in the pinned tree, popup.c contains no image, sixel or SIXEL reference at all, and the built tree's config.h never defines ENABLE_SIXEL, so even the sixel branches guarded by it are compiled out of the pinned binary. Popup content reaches the popup's own screen through input_parse_screen with no image path anywhere, so there is nothing to copy and the item is zz's own presentation contract for a popup terminal. That contract was missing: the raw TUI's Renderer::reconcile_kitty_images walks model.layout.panes, which is the workspace layout, and a popup's pane is not in it, while every popup paint called KittyBridge::suspend first, so an image written inside a popup was placed by nobody and the popup drew its cells with the image missing. The renderer now reconciles the popup's own pane after painting it, against the content box inside the border, on both the full paint and the popup fast path in paint_frames, gated so a menu or confirm overlay above the popup suppresses it; the suspend before it has already retired every workspace placement, so the popup's images are the only ones on screen while it is up. Replacement and close cleanup fall out of the bridge that already had them. That code and its renderer test (an image placed inside a popup anchored at the content origin inside the border, replaced with the retired placement's delete, then the popup dropped with the delete and no new placement) stay in. What is still owed is the attached-client half of the acceptance, which is why the item is NOT closed: the kitty bridge only enables itself after a graphics probe the terminal has to answer, and the harness drives its clients on a plain pty that answers nothing, but that is a fixture limitation and not a structural one - pty-drive.py already reads and writes its master, so a fixture that answers the graphics query, prints an image inside the popup, asserts the `\x1b_Ga=p` placement escape at the content origin and the delete on close would prove it through a real attached client. The renderer test drives reconcile_popup_kitty_images directly and never goes through paint/paint_frames or the menu/confirm gate, so the two new call sites are exercised by nothing until that fixture lands. semantic:display-popup-context-menu, semantic:display-popup-border-drag and semantic:display-popup-to-pane stay open and still need the nested case first: any_overlay_present refuses a second overlay per client, so a menu cannot be raised over a popup at all in zz today, which is the prerequisite popup_key_cb's button-3 arm needs. semantic:display-popup-kitty-images was closed on 2026-09-02 and reopened at the same cycle's gate, because the review showed the close rested on a fixture that configures the gap away; what landed stays, and the measurement that reopened it is below. The fixture limitation the reason named is gone: graphics-drive.py forks a real pty, answers the raw TUI's startup graphics queries the way a Kitty terminal does (OK for the direct probe at image id 4294967295, an error for the file probe at 4294967294, plus DA1 and the cell-size reply), and drives the client with the same step protocol as chooser-drive.py, so the client's bridge enables itself on the harness's own pty. Scenario display-popup-kitty runs on both binaries and each asserts what its own binary owes across the same seven checks: the popup's text reaches the client on both; zz places the image at the content origin one row below and one column right of the popup's top-left corner glyph in the same paint, retires the placement it replaces with a=d,d=i when the popup clears its screen and prints a second image, and deletes what it placed when display-popup -C closes the popup while placing nothing new; the pin draws the same popup text and emits no graphics escape at all, which is the same measurement the paragraph above records from its source. One daemon gap had to close first and is the load-bearing change: publish_popup_terminal sent the popup's viewport without ever calling enqueue_kitty_images_for_viewport, which only ran for panes in streamed_terminals - the focused window's panes - and a popup's synthetic pane is in no window, so the client received placements for an image it had never been sent and drew nothing. Reverting that one call makes five of the seven checks fail, which is how it was verified. One residue is recorded rather than closed: the popup's images reach the client only on a publish where the terminal's per-view snapshot exists. watch_popup reads latest_viewport_for(TerminalViewId(client)) and falls back to latest_viewport(), and that fallback is built by the branch that sets kitty_placements to an empty Arc, while publish_viewport clears by_view outright, so a popup that never sees a per-view publish carries no placements to enqueue. A client resize republishes the view snapshot, which is why the scenario resizes the client before each snapshot and says so. That belongs to the terminal engine's view snapshot, not to the popup. The gate review measured what that residue means for a user: the same fixture with only its two `size` steps deleted (scenario smoke/zzreview-popup-noresize in the review worktree, both binaries) fails 5 of its 7 checks on the zz side, image-is-placed-inside-the-popup, placement-is-anchored-inside-the-border, replacement-retires-the-previous-placement, replacement-places-the-new-image and closing-the-popup-deletes-what-it-placed, while the popup's text still reaches the client. In the ordinary flow, where nobody resizes the client between printing an image and looking at it, a popup's Kitty image never reaches an attached raw TUI client, so the presentation contract the slug names (rendering, replacement and close cleanup on an attached client) is not delivered and the item is open again. The two replacement checks also cannot fail once anything is placed: every popup paint calls KittyBridge::suspend (render.rs paint() popup_visible branch and the paint_frames popup fast path), which delete_all_applied's the popup's own placement, and reconcile_popup_kitty_images re-places it, so `a=d,d=i` plus `a=p` appear on any popup repaint whether or not the popup replaced its image, and the fixture never compares image ids between the opened and replaced snapshots. What closes the item is the per-view viewport in zz-terminal (session.rs latest_viewport's fallback builds kitty_placements as an empty Arc and publish() clears by_view), so that publish_popup_terminal carries the placements without a resize, plus a fixture that drives no resize and compares image ids across the replacement; the daemon's enqueue_kitty_images_for_viewport call in publish_popup_terminal, graphics-drive.py and scenario display-popup-kitty stay as the partial proof they are (clean on both binaries, with the resize). The three pointer items were sized on 2026-09-02 and left open with the sizing written down, because the prerequisite is bigger than the nested overlay the earlier reading named. The client half of the nesting is already there: the raw TUI paints the menu after the popup and hides the cursor for it, and reconcile_popup_kitty_images is already gated on menu.is_none() and confirm.is_none(), so a menu over a popup would draw correctly today. What refuses it is the daemon: display-menu checks any_overlay_present at two points (before resolving the menu and again under the lock before inserting it), and any_overlay_present is popup_other_overlay_present plus inner.popups, so relaxing it to popup_other_overlay_present for the menu path is the whole nesting change. The pointer route is the real blocker. crates/zz-tui/src/input.rs popup_mouse_action drops every pointer event that is not inside the popup's content box, and drops all of them unless the popup's own application has enabled mouse tracking, so button 3 on the left or top border, and anywhere outside the popup, never leaves the client at all. PopupAction on the wire carries Text, Key, TerminalView and Close and has no shape for a border press, a drag or a resize, so all three items need a wire addition and the protocol bump with it, a client-side pointer policy for the border and the outside, and a daemon-side popup_key_cb mouse arm that raises popup_menu_items, moves the box with button 1 and resizes it with button 3. semantic:display-popup-to-pane needs popup_make_pane on top of that: the daemon would have to hand a live PopupSession's terminal to a freshly split pane the way job_transfer hands the job and screen over, which is a pane-creation path zz has nowhere today. semantic:display-popup-kitty-images closed on 2026-09-02 on the second attempt, and the cycle-9 recipe that reopened it named the wrong producer, so the measurement is written down here. That recipe said the placements were lost because watch_popup falls back to latest_viewport() and TerminalSession's fallback viewport is built by the branch that sets kitty_placements to an empty Arc while publish() clears by_view. Neither half survives reading: the popup's terminal is handed attach_view(TerminalViewId(client)) the moment it is spawned, so publish_active_views takes the per-view path and by_view is populated from the first publish on, and both the per-view snapshot and the fallback build their placements from the same KittyGraphicsState::placements call in build_snapshot - the only snapshot that hard-codes an empty Arc is copy_mode_snapshot, which a popup never reaches. The producer that actually failed is the VT's pixel geometry. Terminal::new takes cols, rows and max_scrollback and no cell size, and libghostty's Terminal.resize is the only thing that sets width_px and height_px ('Pixel geometry and synchronized output are updated on every valid resize attempt, including one that doesn't change the grid dimensions'), while a Kitty placement's render info is measured in cell pixels. So a session that had never seen a Command::Resize reported pixel_width and pixel_height of 0 for every placement and KittyGraphicsState::placements dropped them all on its info.pixel_width == 0 guard. An ordinary pane hides this because the first layout pass resizes it; a popup is spawned at the content size popup_content_size computed and is never resized again, so a popup's images only appeared once the user happened to resize the client. run_pty_worker now applies the spawn geometry's cell pixels to the VT immediately after Terminal::new, which is one resize call with the grid dimensions unchanged, so no reflow and no in-band size report. Scenario display-popup-kitty-noresize is the proof the item was missing: it drives no resize anywhere, and because every popup paint calls KittyBridge::suspend and re-places - so a delete plus a place on any repaint proves nothing - it also reads the image id out of the placement escape and asserts the id changes across the replacement and that the delete in the replaced snapshot names the id the opened snapshot placed. Nine checks on the zz side and the same nine on the pin, whose side asserts it emits no graphics escape at all, which is the same measurement recorded above from the pinned source. Before the one resize call landed, seven of those nine failed on the zz side (image-is-placed-inside-the-popup, placement-is-anchored-inside-the-border, both replacement placement checks, both replacement id checks and closing-the-popup-deletes-what-it-placed); only popup-content-reaches-the-client and closing-the-popup-places-nothing-new passed, the second of them vacuously. The engine half is guarded by session::tests::a_session_that_is_never_resized_still_publishes_kitty_placements, which fails without the call. semantic:display-popup-to-pane keeps the second acceptance clause open on its own half. The three pointer items closed on 2026-09-02 against clients attached on real ptys on both binaries, driven with SGR mouse reports, and one earlier reading was refuted first. The sizing said the nesting prerequisite was `display-menu`'s two `any_overlay_present` checks and that relaxing them to `popup_other_overlay_present` would let a menu be raised over a popup. The pin does the opposite: `cmd_display_menu_exec` returns CMD_RETURN_NORMAL the moment `tc->overlay_draw != NULL`, and `server_client_set_overlay` clears the existing overlay before installing a new one anyway, so `display-menu -c` on a client with an open popup is a no-op there. Measured on the pin with a popup up on an attached client: the menu never drew, its item never ran, and the key that followed went into the popup's job. zz's gate already matches that, so it stays. The menu the popup raises is the popup's own `pd->md`, not the client's overlay slot, and that is what zz now builds: `popup_key_cb`'s mouse arm inserts a `MenuSession` marked as the popup's, so the raw TUI - which already paints the menu after the popup and gates `reconcile_popup_kitty_images` on it - draws it over the live popup, and `input_menu` routes the chosen row through the row's key the way `popup_menu_done` switches on it rather than running a command. The pointer route is protocol v96: `PopupAction::Pointer { pointer, view }` carries the event in the client's own cell grid together with the `TerminalViewAction` the client would have handed the popup's job, and the daemon runs the pin's order over it - a drag already under way owns every report until the button lifts; outside the box only button 3 does anything and it raises the menu; button 3 with no modifier on the left or top border raises the same menu; a meta drag, or a drag whose previous report was not itself a drag and whose current one is on a border, arms MOVE for button 1 and SIZE for button 3; anything left over is the job's, and exactly one of the two runs. The pin's own shape was measured rather than assumed: a press on the border does not arm the drag, because `popup_key_cb` reads the border from the report it is handling and the button from the previous one, so the drag is armed by the first drag report that is still on the border and the move happens on the one after that; a press, one drag away from the border and a release moves nothing at all on the pin. Scenario display-popup-drag drives exactly that on both binaries and asserts the box lands ten columns and five rows from where it started, measured against the corner the client itself drew because the raw TUI's sidebar means the two binaries do not share absolute cells, plus that a drag started inside the content box moves nothing. Reverting the daemon's pointer arm makes the zz side fail that check, which is how it was verified. Scenario display-popup-menu asserts the button-3-outside menu carries the `popup_menu_items` rows on both binaries - Close, Fill Space, Centre, To Horizontal Pane, To Vertical Pane - and that choosing Centre moves the box; the menu is raised with a press and no release, because the release is itself a menu key on a mouse menu and closes it on both binaries. Scenario display-popup-to-pane asserts `popup_make_pane` through the daemon-side facts the two binaries share: one pane before, two after, the new pane active, the popup's own output read back with `capture-pane`, and `pane_dead` still 0 because the job was transferred rather than restarted. zz splits the model directly the way the pin splits below `cmd_split_window`, adopts the popup's `TerminalSession` into `terminals` instead of spawning one, carries the pid, tty and cwd onto the pane's runtime facts, resizes it to the pane's geometry, and closes the popup. `Fill Space` and `Centre` are the two `popup_menu_done` box moves; `Paste` writes the top buffer's bytes into the job the way `paste_get_top` plus `bufferevent_write` does, unbracketed. One residue is recorded rather than closed: the GPUI client still sends `PopupAction::TerminalView` for popup pointer events, so the border, drag and menu policy is the raw TUI's today; the acceptance names attached clients and the desktop client's own pointer path belongs with the GUI work. Five defects the cycle-10 review confirmed were fixed at the follow-up gate, each with the reviewer's own measurement reproduced by reverting the fix. (1) `menu_add_item` drops a row whose format expands empty instead of turning it into a separator, and refuses a separator that would follow another, so the popup menu on a server with no paste buffer draws two separator rows and not three; scenario display-popup-menu now counts the separator rows the client drew, 2 on both binaries and 3 on the zz side before the fix. (2) The popup's menu is `pd->md`, drawn by `popup_draw_cb` and freed by `popup_free`, so `take_popup` now drops a popup-owned `MenuSession` with the popup it belongs to and `retire_popup` publishes `Menu { state: None }` alongside `Popup { state: None }`; before it, a menu still up when an -E popup's job exited stayed in `inner.menus`, the raw TUI kept drawing it over the pane and swallowed every key until Escape. (3) The `m->lb`/`m->lx`/`m->ly` the arming condition reads are the tty's, and `tty_keys_mouse` refreshes them from every report it decodes, so `popup_pointer` now records the previous report whatever this one turned out to be - the job's reports and the outside ones it used to return on included; before it, a drag that began on the border, wandered into the content and came back onto the border armed a move on zz and not on the pin, where the previous report was itself a drag. (4) `popup_menu_done`'s 'F' sets `pd->sx`/`sy`/`px`/`py` and calls `server_redraw_client` and nothing else - only `popup_resize_cb` and the SIZE drag call `job_resize` - so Fill Space no longer resizes the popup's job and leaves the content at its old size in the corner of the enlarged box. (5) Neither 'F' nor 'C' touches `ppx`/`ppy`/`psx`/`psy`, so neither writes `popup.preferred` any more and the next owning-client resize puts the box back at the placement display-popup asked for, which is the contract display-popup-resize-lifecycle already proved. Scenario display-popup-menu-policy drives (2), (4) and (5) against clients attached on real ptys on both binaries, with a client resize narrow enough to shrink the box as the control that a resize of the box does reach the job, and scenario display-popup-drag drives (3); reverting the five daemon changes together fails exactly five named checks on the zz side and none on the pin's. The `ProtocolMessage::Popup` schema row in the wire protocol page was also missing the v96 `Pointer` variant its own changelog records.

closed.title: Expose buffer format facts
closed.resolution: List-buffers supplies row-local buffer facts to -F and -f, while choose-buffer supplies the same facts to -f and -K. Ordinary expansion selects the newest automatic buffer. All five tracked variables now read one retained name, data value, and creation time; buffer_sample applies tmux-compatible escaping and truncation, buffer_full preserves the complete lossy text, and #{command} remains a command-item fact. buffer_mode_format stays separate because zz uses a native buffer chooser. The focused cargo test -p zz-daemon --lib buffer_ run passes all 15 tests.

closed.title: Expand load-buffer and save-buffer paths
closed.resolution: `load-buffer` and `save-buffer` now expand their positional path exactly once through the shared daemon command hooks before home-directory expansion and filesystem access. A resolvable `load-buffer -t` client supplies its attached session, focused window, and active pane; an unresolved target stays quiet and uses the most-recent mux context instead of the invoker. The targetless path selects the invoking attached client, the best client on the invoking command client's origin session, or the global best attached client before falling back to the most-recent mux context. Canonical names survive built-in aliases, unique prefixes, and one-layer user aliases, while explicit item state retains precedence and replacement text is not expanded again. `load-buffer` rejects a raw or format-produced `-` before I/O and preserves the empty-file no-op before buffer-name validation. `save-buffer` resolves the selected buffer before path expansion and the `-` check. Standard streams remain under `protocol.binary-streams`, `load-buffer -w` remains under `buffers.clipboard-write`, target-client format facts later closed under `clients.context-formats`, while relative, attached-session, and remote file ownership remains under `buffers.client-file-context`.

closed.title: Expand five target-sensitive command arguments
closed.resolution: This close covers five target-sensitive argument paths: `rename-session` and `rename-window` expand their new names after resolving the target and before changing its old session or window facts; direct `show-options` and `show-window-options` calls perform one expansion of an optional option name in the target context, with `show-hooks` marking its forwarded name as expanded; and `select-pane -T` expands from the original target pane before a direction chooses the destination that receives the title. All five paths retain the canonical command-item name and explicit hook overrides. Both `new-session` names, the shared `new-session`/`new-window`/rename validation and cleaning path, literal `break-pane -n` cleaning, and the `load-buffer` and `save-buffer` file paths closed separately under focused format groups on 2026-08-25.

closed.title: Expose the invoking command format
closed.resolution: `#{command}` is now a command-queue-item fact for every command the mux engine runs, not a list-row fact: after `command-alias` expansion and canonical resolution the dispatch chokepoint wraps the incoming format hooks once with the canonical entry name and threads that wrapper through every arm, so `display-message`, the list commands, and every other mux-executed item expand it, a typed alias or unique prefix still reports the canonical name, and it stays empty outside a command item. The wrapper consults the inner and item-state hooks first, so an explicit outer `command` value keeps winning, and list rows keep it invariant while `key_*` and `command_list_*` stay disjoint per row. The daemon-preempted half closed separately under `formats.daemon-command-item-context`.

closed.title: Implement missing context-format producers
closed.resolution: The nine remaining literal producer tuples were all notify_monitor_cb, and they land with the set-hook -B monitor subsystem the pin fires them from. Re-measured on the pinned server on 2026-09-03 and every clause of the group reason held: monitor_parse splits the -B value on the first two colons into name, what and format and fails without both, `%*` is all panes, `%N` one pane, `@*` all windows, `@N` one window, and anything else the session, including the empty string, `junk`, a bare `%` and `@-1`; a non-canonical what reads back canonically, and `%0abc` reads back as `%0` because sscanf scans leading digits. cmd_set_option refuses a name that does not start with @ ("monitor hook name must start with @", status 1) and a value without both colons answers "invalid subscription: <value>" at status 1. `set-hook -Bu @watch` answers "invalid subscription: u" at status 1 and removes nothing because -B takes a value and swallows the u, while `set-hook -u -B @watch` removes. A one-second timer re-expands each subscription's format per subscribed object; the first sample of an object records the baseline and reports nothing because notify_monitor_add passes no MONITOR_NOTIFY_INITIAL, and a later sample reports only when the string changed. show-hooks -B lists the live subscriptions as name:what:format, one per line in name order, prints nothing for a user option with no monitor and answers "invalid option: @nomonitor" at status 1 for a name no option holds. One clause of the earlier reason was incomplete and is now measured: notify_monitor_add always asks for ne->expand, so notify_parse_hook format-expands the whole body string before parsing it, which is why a `set -g @fired "#{hook_value}"` body stores the expanded value while an ordinary after-* hook body, whose ne->expand is 0, stores the literal `#{hook_value}` on both binaries. zz now carries the subsystem: a monitor store keyed by option scope and name on MuxEngine with the monitor_parse grammar and the notify_monitor_to_string readback in crates/zz-mux/src/command.rs, the one-second tick in the daemon's existing status sampler thread reusing control_subscription_targets for the polling set, monitor_check_value's baseline-then-change detection and the all-panes and all-windows sweeps on the store, and the nine names as a producer on the hook-variable path beside hook_format_variables rather than as a format-table entry. -B needed no catalog move: it was already a real option on set-hook and a real flag on show-hooks, so no supported or unsupported counter and no usage override changed. The nine notify_monitor_cb tuples move from the missing partition into the mux literal partition, which is the recount compat_manifest_tests carries (mux literals 73 -> 82, missing literals 9 -> 0), and the missing-literal partition is now empty. compat/scenarios/smoke/format-monitor-hooks.txt asserts thirteen rows on both binaries: the nine names quiescent, an all-windows subscription silent on arm and while unchanged, the window, session and all-panes fire shapes with every one of the nine names, per-object polling across two windows, a bodyless subscription creating its own empty option, the name-ordered show-hooks -B listing and its single-name form, both parse failures, the unknown-name listing error, the -Bu non-removal and the -u -B removal, and a removed subscription going quiet. One divergence found beside the work and left alone because it is not this group's: the pin's initial pane_title is the host name and zz's is the pane command, so the scenario sets a title before arming the pane subscription rather than leaning on the default.

closed.title: Finish creation-name edge semantics
closed.resolution: Without an explicit destination index, new-window -S performs a second format expansion over the cleaned first-pass -n value for lookup while creation keeps the cleaned first-pass value. An explicit destination index bypasses that lookup expansion. An explicit break-pane -n disables window-local automatic-rename after both whole-window relinking and new-window creation. The full zz-mux library suite passes 379 tests, and the strict command-item-format and break-pane differentials pass 125 and 30 steps with zero topology, geometry, format, output, or warning differences and no skips.

closed.title: Expose the invoking command format for daemon-run items
closed.resolution: DaemonFormatHooks now carries an optional canonical command-item name after explicit item-state variables, so an explicit `command` override still wins without copying the name into ExecutionContext. execute_with_mux_source_raw passes the resolved entry through the daemon-owned immediate expansion surfaces: run-shell shell and string -C, if-shell conditions, capture-pane -S/-E, pipe-pane shell, list-buffers and list-clients formats and filters, display-popup title/directory/position, display-menu title/items/position, confirm-before string-command preparation, and the post-spawn PaneFormatOutput re-expansion for new-window and split-window -P/-F. Canonical names survive built-in aliases, unique prefixes, and one-layer user aliases. Typed command blocks skip the parent expansion and their children report their own commands; daemon-preempted hook bodies report their own command while retaining the trigger in `#{hook}`. Confirm prompts and delayed refresh-client subscriptions expand outside a queue item and keep `#{command}` empty. Popup argv and environment assignments remain raw. The pinned 24-step strict differential covers shell and -C routes, every resolution spelling, typed blocks, if-shell parent and child routing, hook routing, list-buffers, and both pane-creation print paths with zero TOPO, GEO, FMT, OUT, or WARN differences.

closed.title: Implement remaining format modifiers
closed.resolution: The I modifier is implemented from the pin's own arithmetic rather than from zz's published feature list, and the decomposition the previous pass wrote down held exactly. `tty_term_codes` (233 name and type rows) and `tty_features` (21 features with their capability lists and term flags) are ported into a new crates/zz-mux/src/terminfo.rs as `TtyTerm`, which is `tty_term_create` plus `tty_apply_features` plus `tty_feature_present` over a capability list handed in as the pin's own `name=value` strings. Reading the terminfo database is I/O, so it stays in the daemon: crates/zz-daemon/src/status.rs runs `infocmp -x -1 <TERM>` once per TERM name for the life of the process and caches the result, which is the only portable reader that prints the extended section the tmux capability names live in. The term object rides `ClientFormatFacts` beside the other client facts, so it is present exactly when the format tree's client is attached with a tty, which is `format_replace`'s null-client, null-term and CLIENT_UNATTACHEDFLAGS early exit. `#{I/e:}` reads that same client's environment rather than `client_environment_rows`, and the difference is measured: with a variable set only in the invoking shell and another set only on the attached client, the pin answers the target client's value for `#{I/e:}` and the invoking client's for `#{Vc:}`. The catalog side is the parser: `I` joins FORMAT_MODIFIER_SPECS (35 -> 36 modifiers, the missing-modifier partition in compat_manifest_tests empties), and the three flags are read in the pin's fixed source order c, f, e with each overwriting the last. Proved on both binaries in compat/scenarios/smoke/format-modifier-interrogate.txt, 85 checks against one attached 80x24 pty client on TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor and FOO=barvalue: every form empty on a detached server; thirteen capabilities straight from the entry (acsc, am, AX, bce, clear, colors, cup, kf1, kf63, setab, setaf, smcup, XT); thirteen written in by `tty_apply_features` (Ss and Se from cstyle, Ms from clipboard, Cs and Cr from ccolour, tsl and fsl from title, Enbp, Dsbp, Enfcs and Dsfcs from the bpaste, focus and title `tty_term_create` adds for a clear starting with CSI, and setrgbf and setrgbb from the RGB that COLORTERM=truecolor asks for); nineteen absent from both sources answering 0 (Clmg, Cmg, Dseks, Dsmg, Eneks, Enmg, Hls, ol, RGB, Rect, Smol, Smulx, Setulc, Spb, Swd, Sxl, Sync, smxx, Tc, U8); a real terminfo boolean tmux never reads (hs) and an invented name both answering 0; nine features answering 1 including 256 and mouse, which have no feature bit and pass only through `tty_feature_present`'s capability fallback; thirteen answering 0 including ignorefkeys, which the pin excludes by name; `I/e:FOO`=barvalue and an unset name empty; the overwrite order proved four ways (`I/cf:RGB`=1 against `I/cfe:FOO`, `I/fe:FOO` and `I/ec:FOO` all barvalue); `I:pane_id` answering the pane id and `I/z:RGB` empty, which is the parser's `argc < 1` break and a flag word with no c, f or e both falling through to the ordinary lookup; and the body being a literal name, with `#{I/c:#{l:smcup}}` and both empty bodies answering 0. A unit test in terminfo.rs pins the same matrix against the exact capability list `tty_term_read_list` produces for that TERM, so the port is checked without a live client too. Three facts are recorded rather than claimed. `client_termfeatures` stays zz's own renderer roster (16 names against the pin's 7 for this client) and the interrogate never reads it, which is why the scenario does not compare that name. Two options move the answer, `terminal-features` and `terminal-overrides`, and both reach the port through engine accessors: `tty_term_apply_overrides` is ported too, every row whose first item fnmatches the TERM walked with `tty_term_apply` semantics (`name@` removes the code, `name=value` sets it through strunvis, a bare name sets a flag, names outside `tty_term_codes` ignored), run once after the entry read and again after the feature pass, and recomputing the RGB, DECSLRM and DECFRA term flags from the capabilities each time. The stock `linux*:AX@` row is why the pin answers `#{I/c:AX}` 0 on TERM=linux, and `set -g terminal-overrides 'xterm*:Tc'` makes it answer `#{I/c:Tc}` 1 with the RGB feature following, both measured on the pin at review and now pinned in terminfo.rs; a zz user config that adds a row to either array (this box's own ~/.config/zz/mux.conf adds `xterm-256color:RGB:sync:clipboard:hyperlinks:extkeys`) moves both binaries' answers the same way, so the scenario runs on the stock arrays. The review of the port found four ways the single-TERM, COLORTERM=truecolor fixture could not see it drifting from `tty_term_create`, each measured on the pin with a pty client and fixed at the gate: ncurses 6.1 and later print a number past 255 in hex (`colors#0x100`), which the reader now converts to the `%d` form `tty_term_read_list` writes, so `#{I/c:colors}` answers 1 under brew's ncurses 6.6 as under Apple's 6.0; the reader now decodes terminfo string escapes the way `tigetstr` does (`\E`, `^X`, octal, `\,`), so a clear of `\E[H\E[J` starts with a real CSI and screen-256color, tmux-256color (pin `I/f:bpaste`=1, `I/f:focus`=1, `I/c:Enfcs`=1) and linux (pin `I/f:title`=1) get the three VT100-like features without XT, where the tip had answered 0; the feature loop honours cancels, so rxvt's stock `ignorefkeys` removes kf0..kf63 (pin `#{I/c:kf1}` 0) instead of adding them; and the overrides pass above. XT is read as a flag value (`XT=1`) the way `tty_term_flag` reads it. One platform artifact is recorded rather than matched: the pin on this box links Apple's /usr/lib/libncurses.5.4, whose tigetflag answers 0 rather than -1 for an absent user-defined XT, so that pin answers `#{I/c:XT}` 1 for screen-256color, tmux-256color, linux and rxvt where zz answers 0; a GNU-ncurses pin answers 0, and zz follows the GNU reading. And the item's fallback clause was narrowed with the measurement that forced it: `#{I:HOME}` cannot be the fallback proof because zz has no environment fallback in format expansion at all, so `#{HOME}` answers empty on zz where the pin answers the client's home; the scenario proves the same `argc < 1` break with `#{I:pane_id}`, which both binaries answer identically, and the missing fallback is recorded on clients.path-encoding where it was found. messages.tty-model is untouched: the daemon still drives no client terminal through terminfo, it now only reads one entry to answer this modifier. Instrument correction, 2026-09-05: the earlier claim that the scenario runs on the stock arrays and that smxx is absent does not describe the repaired fixture. On Ubuntu 26.04, removing only the fixture-local xterm-256color:smxx@ terminal-overrides row measured I/c:smxx=1 and I/f:strikethrough=1 on both zz and pinned tmux. The explicit cancellation makes both answers 0 and preserves the deterministic absence checks within the same 85 assertions across terminfo installations. This probe found no zz/pin divergence; the fixture now uses stock terminal-features and stock terminal-overrides plus this explicit cancellation.

closed.title: Unify creation and rename name semantics
closed.resolution: `new-session -n` now expands exactly once through the same command-item format context as `-s`, then rejects ASCII controls and applies tmux vis cleaning before `-s` is touched. Canonical, alias, and unique-prefix spellings expose `new-session`, explicit item state retains precedence, and only a genuinely attached client contributes session, focused-window, and active-pane facts. `new-window -n` expands once in the destination session context with the pin's session format type and then uses the same validation and cleaning helper before reuse lookup or creation. Both `rename-session` and `rename-window` use the resolved target's active pane and the pin's pane format type; each applies the shared helper after one target-context expansion. `break-pane -n` follows the pin's distinct literal path: it is never format-expanded, but it is validated and cleaned before placement, including before `-a` or `-b` can shift window indices. Empty and valid Unicode names survive, literal backslashes are doubled exactly once, cleaned values determine session collision and new-window reuse identity, and duplicate window names remain legal. An existing-session `-A` still expands and validates `-n` first and then ignores it. Every nested detached `-Ad` path now defers its refusal until a returned Attach effect: an expanded existing target is refused before application with target-only command-context restoration that preserves freshly derived client size and cwd, while an expanded miss creates detached even when the raw format text happens to name a literal session. The strict `command-item-format` differential covers formatted creation names, Unicode, backslash cleaning, cleaned reuse and rename collision, literal break-pane format tokens, and rename parity, including `session_format=0` and `pane_format=1`, with no topology, geometry, format, output, or warning differences. Focused mux tests pin the format types, a non-vacuous `break-pane -b` rejection before window 0 could shift to index 1, unchanged pane layout and window indices, ASCII-control rejection, exact `-n`-before-`-s` ordering, and expansion count because the line-oriented differential harness cannot carry control bytes or count hook calls. `formats.creation-name-edges` closed the pin's second `new-window -S` lookup expansion and `break-pane -n` automatic-rename side effect separately on 2026-08-25. The later `mux.error-shapes` closure matched nested non-detached precedence for the `-t` conflict, invalid window or session names, duplicates, and invalid session-group names.

closed.title: Expand the new-session name
closed.resolution: `new-session -s` now expands exactly once through the existing command-item format hooks before `-A` lookup, duplicate lookup, and creation. Attached Interactive and Control clients contribute their actual attached session, focused window, and active pane, including after a detached creation retargets the mutable command context; fresh Interactive and Command clients contribute no session defaults even when their execution context carries a most-recent target. Canonical, alias, and unique-prefix spellings expose `new-session` through `#{command}`, while an explicit outer item value retains precedence. Omitted `-s` keeps numeric allocation. Existing-session `-A` still ignores `-d` and creation-only flags; creation size, environment, cwd, and print handling still run only after the expanded name misses. The adjacent validation and vis-cleaning parity for both `new-session` names, `new-window -n`, both rename commands, and literal `break-pane -n` closed under `formats.name-validation-cleaning`, including the detached formatted `-A` nesting-guard correction. The strict `command-item-format` differential covers this path without duplicating its moving step count here. The later `mux.error-shapes` closure matched nested non-detached duplicate, invalid-name, and `-t` plus `-n` conflict precedence.

closed.title: Expose remaining pane process formats
