closed.resolution: Three of the four are done and the fourth is re-scoped onto what the name actually means. pane_pipe, pane_pipe_pid and pane_unseen_changes moved from constant backings to the delegated partition and are answered by the daemon, proved differentially by compat/scenarios/smoke/format-pane-process.txt on both binaries: a fresh pane answers `pipe=0 pid=[] unseen=0`, pipe-pane raises pane_pipe to 1 and pane_pipe_pid to a live pid whose argument vector still names the pipe destination, and a bare pipe-pane drops both back. pane_unseen_changes is NOT the batch's premise of "output an attached client has not seen", and that premise is what needed correcting: input.c:1039 raises PANE_UNSEENCHANGES only inside `if (!TAILQ_EMPTY(&wp->modes))`, window.c:1448 drops it when the last mode entry goes, and window-copy.c:3013 drops it again from the copy-mode refresh timer. Measured on the pin: output to a detached window with no mode leaves it 0, output while the pane is in copy mode raises it to 1, and cancelling the mode drops it. zz carries the bit on the per-client copy session record instead of on the pane, which clears on the same two edges for free because entering a mode writes a fresh record; the daemon raises it from the pane-output activity producer for every non-exiting copy session on the pane. The per-client model is visible in one place the pin's is not: with two clients in copy mode on one pane, zz raises the bit on both records and answers 1 until every session is gone, where the pin has one pane flag; the answer is the same in every single-client state. pane_pb_progress stays open with its blocker measured rather than guessed. It is not paste-buffer progress: format.c:2380 reads `ft->wp->base.progress_bar.progress`, which screen.c:342 `screen_set_progress_bar` writes and input.c:3005 `input_osc_9` parses out of the ConEmu OSC 9;4 sequence, so it is a persistent per-pane progress-bar value and not a transient one. A fresh pane answers 0 and pane_pb_state answers `hidden` on the pin, where zz answers 0 and empty, so the pair agrees only in the default state. Closing it means parsing OSC 9;4 in the VT and retaining the state and progress on the pane, which is zz-terminal work; pane_pb_state is the same family and is tracked beside it. 2026-09-02, closed. libghostty parses OSC 9;4 far enough to name it `GHOSTTY_OSC_COMMAND_CONEMU_PROGRESS_REPORT`, but neither the C ABI's `ghostty_osc_command_data` nor its terminal getters expose the state or the percentage, so there is nothing to read back; the sequence is read in zz-terminal instead. The pane worker's byte filter already resumes a CSI or an `ESC k` rename across chunk boundaries, and it now tracks OSC the same way: an OSC run goes to the engine in one write, unchanged, while a bounded copy of the payload is kept for the equivalent of `input_exit_osc`, which reads the leading digits as the OSC number and routes 9 to the OSC 9;4 grammar. The pair lives on the worker as a packed atomic, and the daemon reads it off the pane's terminal session, so the format engine still never touches a grid. Both names move from the constant partition to the delegated one, which is what let `pane_pb_state` leave formats.terminal-cells with its own re-scoping recorded there. Measured on pinned tmux by writing the sequence onto a pane's own pty and reading `#{pane_pb_state}/#{pane_pb_progress}` on an 80x24 pane. The walk: fresh `hidden/0`, `9;4;0` `hidden/0`, `9;4;1;50` `normal/50`, `9;4;2;30` `error/30`, `9;4;3` `indeterminate/30`, `9;4;4;10` `paused/10`. The edges, which are the whole contract: `screen_set_progress_bar` stores the state unconditionally and the percentage only when the sequence carried one and the state is not indeterminate, so `9;4;3;70` from `paused/10` answers `indeterminate/10` and `9;4;2;` answers `error/10`; and `input_osc_9` changes nothing at all for `9;4;5` (state outside 0..4), `9;4;1;101` (percentage over 100), `9;4` and `9;4;` (the payload stops before the state), `9;4;1;5x` (a trailing non-digit fails the `*pb != '\0'` check) and `9;5;1` (OSC 9 whose first byte is not `4`). compat/scenarios/smoke/format-pane-progress.txt asserts those sixteen answers on both binaries, and it emits each sequence followed by a marker line so that an ignored payload is assertable at all: without waiting for the marker to reach the screen, a check that nothing moved would pass before the bytes were parsed.

closed.title: Repeat format output
closed.resolution: The parser-owned modifier roster now recognizes `R`. Repeat splits its body at the first top-level comma before recursively expanding the value and count, accepts leading count whitespace while rejecting trailing text, repeats counts from 1 through 10000, and returns empty for an invalid, zero, negative, or oversized count. A missing comma follows the pin's replacement-failure path, so later format text is not emitted. Escaped commas, nested operands, byte-length replacement, truncation, and the remaining post-transform order match the pin. A deterministic 40,960,000-byte intermediate ceiling rejects nested allocation amplification before reserving memory, replacing the pin's time budget with a bounded daemon-safe result. The shipped second and third status-row defaults now indent `P:` and `S:` by the `n` byte length of the session name without exposing literal `R` syntax. The strict 16-step formats differential is clean, focused mux tests cover grammar, bounds, nesting, precedence, and the allocation guard, and the daemon row test covers the production defaults. No protocol or snapshot changed.

closed.title: Expose retained session activity
closed.resolution: Sessions now retain Unix-second activity apart from the logical MRU counter. Creation initializes activity from the exact retained creation timestamp. Successful same- and other-session attaches, survivor retargeting through the shared attach funnel, ordinary queued terminal keys, read-only queued keys, rejected read-only terminal-view input including mouse motion, writable chooser input, and eligible standalone committed text update the retained and logical activity facts. Writable chooser input also advances latest geometry without clearing bells; cross-session chooser activation then records the target attach as a second legitimate boundary. Read-only raw keys bypass chooser, command-prompt, and display-panes consumption into ordinary key-table resolution, while rejected native actions update latest geometry without clearing bells or mutating the retained modal; safe local view actions bypass chooser and display-panes surfaces and reach the pane with the same once-only accounting. Writable prompt-consumed key or text input and valid display-panes selection do not refresh activity. A bounded per-client ordered queue correlates Key-plus-Text pairs so the Key's result wins and the trailing Text adds no second update. Standalone read-only terminal Text accounts without a PTY write or bell clear. Unmatched display-panes keys, Escape, and non-hover mouse or wheel input close the overlay and fall through ordinary input; only bare buttonless hover Motion remains consumed, and timeout fabricates no activity. Native client-theme notifications, resize, `switch-client -T`, and detached commands also do not refresh activity. Plain `session_activity` and its `t:` form use the retained timestamp, while `S/t` and `list-sessions -O activity` use the logical counter so same-second touches reorder by logical MRU with session name as the tie break. Browser input keeps zz's existing native-superset activity behavior. These daemon input edges closed under `formats.session-activity-daemon-input-edges`, `choosers.cross-client-pane-mode-routing`, `display-panes.gpui-escape-fallthrough`, and `formats.session-activity-text-input`; client focus signaling plus attach, FocusIn latest geometry, and writable modal routing closed under `formats.session-activity-client-focus-signal`, `formats.session-activity-focus-latest`, and `formats.session-activity-focus-modal-consumption`. `formats.session-activity-wake-lifecycle` records tmux wake/unlock as an accepted non-applicable lifecycle difference.

closed.title: Separate client focus from pane focus
closed.resolution: Protocol v73 appends `InputMessage::ClientFocus { focused }` at wire tag 18 and retains exact-version handshake rejection. GPUI seeds desired focus only when construction finds an active window and leaves inactive construction unset until the first activation callback. A written attach opens a pending focus epoch. `Attached` confirms the new epoch and replays the latest desired value once, so reconnect, host switch, and session attach do not depend on another OS activation transition. A rejected same-connection session attach restores the retained session's ready epoch and flushes a focus value that changed while the request was pending. Only a pending MissingTarget or SessionNotFound attach response can recover that epoch; unrelated request-zero errors while ready or pending do not alter focus delivery. Scripted pane selection, sidebar focus, and pane transitions remain pane focus only. The TUI assumes its outer terminal starts in the foreground, caches FocusGained and FocusLost while attachment is pending, sends the latest ClientFocus value once after each Attached event, and deduplicates repeated reports with the same value. A separate protocol-owned attach-attempt marker selects missing-target retry and fallback without consulting focus readiness, then returns to idle on Attached or terminal attach failure. Unrelated request-zero errors change neither state machine. A rejected sidebar session attach restores the retained session's ready epoch instead of entering new-session fallback. Real outer focus events retain pane Focus when the active pane is a terminal; attachment does not synthesize pane focus. `zz_client_attach` returning true means the FFI client wrote the request. iOS waits for `ZZ_EVENT_ATTACHED`, then sends the latest scene state once for initial, selected-session, recovery, and recreated-session attachments without replaying pane focus. Foreground and background still send the separate `zz_client_focus_terminal` transition when a terminal input owner exists. When the server `focus-events` option is on, both client-focus directions update retained session activity, logical MRU, client activity sequence, and client activity time exactly once, including read-only clients. Writable pane Focus continues terminal application forwarding but changes neither activity nor geometry ownership, so paired client and pane signals touch activity once. Read-only pane Focus is rejected and its client-window transition remains owned by ClientFocus. Neither signal clears bells; the client-focus activity path is inert while the server option is off. The daemon routes writable client focus through prompt handling and display-panes teardown under `formats.session-activity-focus-modal-consumption`.

closed.title: Account chooser, display-panes, and prompt input edges
closed.resolution: Writable choose-tree and choose-buffer raw keys, dedicated actions, and terminal-view input now touch source-session activity exactly once, advance the latest geometry owner, and preserve bells. Read-only raw keys bypass chooser, display-panes, and command-prompt consumption into ordinary key-table resolution. Read-only dedicated modal actions and rejected non-focus terminal-view actions update activity plus the latest geometry owner before rejection, retain the modal, and preserve the pane bell; raw mouse motion is included. Read-only-safe local navigation uses the same once-only accounting, bypasses retained chooser and display-panes surfaces, and reaches the pane under `clients.read-only-local-view-actions`; pane Focus is rejected without activity, and ClearLinkHover remains a safe non-input action. Writable display-panes consumes a valid selection and bare buttonless hover Motion without activity, but an unmatched key, Escape, non-hover mouse action, or wheel tears down the overlay and falls through ordinary input; timeout closes it without activity. Writable command-prompt consumption remains no-activity. Cross-client chooser routing and display-panes fallthrough are recorded as focused closed entries. Client focus signaling plus attach and latest geometry are closed separately. Committed text inherits these modal decisions through `formats.session-activity-text-input`, and client focus follows the writable prompt and display-panes prequeue under `formats.session-activity-focus-modal-consumption`.

closed.title: Make attach and FocusIn the latest geometry client
closed.resolution: Every successful same- or other-session attach advances the existing geometry-owner sequence and recalculates all affected terminal sizes, independent of `focus-events`; a two-client regression with different retained geometries proves a same-session reattach immediately selects that client's whole geometry. Client FocusIn advances the same sequence and recomputes visible terminal sizes when `focus-events` is on. Under `window-size latest`, rows, columns, and cell metrics all come from that owner; manual, largest, and smallest retain their mode-correct rows and columns while refreshing the owner's cell metrics. FocusOut updates activity without changing the owner or geometry. A zz-side writable two-client daemon regression with different retained geometries mirrors the pinned FocusIn/latest rows-and-columns rule. `ClientFocus` is not CLI-drivable, so this is not a differential-harness proof. A second non-latest regression uses equal rows and columns with distinct cell metrics and observes the terminal process the owner-only resize. The separate read-only fixture proves that zz accepts the notification and updates activity. It does not prove tmux `attach -r` resize behavior because tmux couples read-only with `ignore-size` while zz does not.

closed.title: Route client focus through the writable modal prequeue
closed.resolution: With `focus-events` enabled, the daemon now runs the pinned writable prequeue before it accounts `ClientFocus`. It dismisses the active status message and resumes frozen terminal publication, then closes `display-panes`, cancels its deadline, and continues through prompts. Key prompts submit the exact `FocusIn` or `FocusOut` text and consume the transition. Numeric prompts submit their buffer without recording prompt history and pass the transition. Text, Single, Incremental, and BackspaceExit prompts consume it and stay open. Choose-tree and choose-buffer bypass the prequeue because tmux handles them as pane modes. Read-only clients retain every modal and account both directions. FocusIn alone advances latest geometry, and neither direction clears bells. When a FocusIn both changes latest geometry and changes an activity-sorted chooser, the daemon publishes the snapshot and independently refreshes the chooser. The daemon snapshots the option gate before a Numeric prompt can change it, so an accepted transition still accounts. This slice adds no wire change and retains the `ClientFocus` shape introduced in protocol v73. Daemon regressions provide the proof because `ClientFocus` is not CLI-drivable. Pane `command-prompt -P` remains blocked under `prompt.pane-rendered`. Synthetic `Any` dispatch after activity and FocusIn geometry accounting closed separately under `keys.client-focus-events`; exact `FocusIn` and `FocusOut` remain invalid as bindable key names.

closed.title: Correlate committed text with its key
closed.resolution: The daemon now correlates committed text with its preceding key through one bounded ordered queue per client. Every validated press or repeat Key with `text_follows: true` appends an entry that records its pane and Terminal or BrowserSurface lane. Text scans forward to the first entry for its pane and lane, retires only the older skipped prefix, and consumes that match while preserving later entries. It inherits the matched Key's activity and modal result, so the pair contributes at most one activity/latest update; empty Text is inert but also retires any linked dispatch suppression. If no entry matches, the queue stays intact and nonempty Text is standalone. A two-browser-pane regression strands one earlier key and proves the later bound key keeps its suppression debt until its matching Text, so neither the binding nor text is replayed. Bounded eviction and every explicit cleanup retire linked suppression debt. Writable standalone text reaches chooser, command-prompt, and display-panes before activity; terminal command-output text accounts once before it is swallowed, while browser command-output text is consumed before activity. Standalone read-only terminal text accounts once without a bell or PTY write, while read-only browser text keeps zz's existing silent drop. Paired writable chooser input follows its key result; writable prompt and display-panes consumption can remain at zero. Read-only terminal pairs bypass retained modals, account on the key, and never write the trailing text. The queue clears on detach, unregister/reconnect, and successful wire Attach, but survives a synchronous binding-driven `switch-client` so the trailing Text still belongs to its Key. GPUI terminal standalone input and GPUI browser key-plus-text input are proved at their emitters; TUI keys remain unpaired, while FFI and iOS retain their explicit standalone/key contracts.

closed.title: Expose the target session working path
closed.resolution: The direct `SessionPath` backing now reads the selected session's retained UTF-8 working directory at expansion time. Targeted display and filtered list-session expansions preserve distinct session paths and lexical components such as `..`; a missing session or missing retained zz path stays empty. Focused mux tests cover target isolation, lexical UTF-8, absent state, and visibility after the production `attach-session -c` command updates one session without changing another. At this checkpoint the source-owned 198-name partition was 93 direct mux values, 32 daemon-delegated values, and 73 active constant-backed gaps. The separate `session_active` producer audit later closed under `formats.session-runtime`. No protocol, snapshot, cwd-mutation, startup-source, non-UTF-8, or format-vocabulary contract changed in this slice.

closed.title: Expose format-client session activity
closed.resolution: The direct `SessionActive` backing now preserves tmux's three states: empty without a target session or format client, `1` when the selected format client is attached to the target session, and `0` when it is unattached or attached elsewhere. Command execution keeps the raw invoking client separate from the current or explicitly selected target client because tmux producers use both within the same command. Clientless lists, filters, chooser rows, and `list-commands` remain empty; target-aware command formats, deferred pane output, shell callbacks, buffer paths, capture boundaries, popup and menu text, `list-keys`, status rows, Control subscriptions, and display-panes labels receive their pinned client provenance. Fresh `new-session -c` keeps its independent session-path and spawn-path expansions, while non-detached `new-session -P` formats after attachment. Focused mux and daemon tests cover every reachable empty, false, and true branch, and the differential plus attached-client fixtures cover clientless and live attached paths. No wire protocol or snapshot field changed.

closed.title: Publish live history cursor and alternate-screen facts
closed.resolution: Closed format:history_size, format:cursor_x, format:cursor_y and format:alternate_on, relocated from formats.terminal-runtime. Pinned d77c9dc6 format.c reads wp->base.grid->hsize, cx, cy and saved_grid. smoke/terminal-facts asserts five exact tuples: 77 0 23 0 after seq 1 100 in a prompt-free 80x24 pane, 77 0 23 1 in alternate mode, 77 0 23 0 after exit, 77 80 23 0 at pending wrap, and 77 0 23 1 when output and alternate entry arrive together. TerminalFacts is an in-process Copy value in the existing published worker state, read through daemon format hooks without a worker request or PTY drain wait. The existing CSI filter samples primary history before alternate entry, including split sequences; the terminal unit test covers one-byte, seven-byte and complete chunks plus repeated alternate entry. Pending wrap reports the terminal width. The values follow actual retained worker history, including existing history-limit/cap policy. No wire type changed; protocol remains v98.

closed.title: Expose window activity timestamps
closed.resolution: Windows now retain tmux's Unix-second `activity_time` apart from zz's logical MRU counter. Creation, parsed nonempty pane output, and the existing pinned current-window transition producers update both values from the injected engine clock. The independent audit found and repaired the direct daemon `switch-client` selection path so it refreshes that clock before changing the current window. Same-window selection, pane selection, pane creation, splits, and layout-only changes without output leave the timestamp unchanged. The direct Time format backing expands empty without a window and preserves the same seconds through plain, boolean, comparison, list-row, and time-modified forms. Focused model, command, format, daemon, and differential coverage preserves the pin's move-window and swap-window transition details while proving target isolation and output-driven updates. No wire protocol or snapshot field changed.

closed.title: Expose remaining window formats
closed.resolution: The per-client window family is done and the group's three producer families are all closed. window_bigger and the two viewport offsets are answered by the daemon from the format client's retained viewport, which is `interactive_client_window_extent`: the client's reported columns and its rows minus the session's status lines, the same `tty->sx` and `tty->sy - status_line_size(c)` that `tty_window_offset1` compares. The comparison is against the CLIENT's own current window and the pane that window is showing, never the format's window, because tty.c reads `c->session->curw->window` and `server_client_get_pane(c)`. The offsets reproduce the else branch of `tty_window_offset1`: x is 0 while the cursor is left of sx, `w->sx - sx` once it is past `w->sx - sx`, and `cx - sx/2` between them; y is 0, `w->sy - sy`, or `cy - sy + 1` on the same three branches, and both are 0 when the pane's cursor is hidden, which is the `~MODE_CURSOR` arm. All three names moved from constant backings to the delegated partition, so the mux answers empty and the daemon answers the value, which is exactly the pin's NULL-versus-string split. Measured on a throwaway pin server and on a headless zz daemon, and proved by compat/scenarios/smoke/format-window-bigger.txt on both binaries: null with no client, 0 for a window that fits with the status line on and with it off, 1 after resize-window widened the window to 200x60 past an 80x24 client, and null again after detach. The three offset branches were driven by parking the pane cursor with a direct write to `#{pane_tty}`: (151,31) answers ox 120 oy 8, (61,3) answers ox 0 oy 0, and (101,26) answers ox 60 oy 3, identical on both binaries with sx 80 and sy 23. A list-windows and a list-panes row answer null for all three even while the client is attached and the window is bigger, which is the null format client cmd-list-windows.c and cmd-list-panes.c pass to format_defaults; the daemon now drops the format client for those commands and for list-sessions. Two things stay unmatched and are recorded rather than claimed. The pan window branch of tty_window_offset1, which `refresh-client -U/-D/-L/-R` arms by setting `c->pan_window`, has no zz equivalent: zz has no viewport pan, so it always reaches the cursor branch, and a panned pin client would answer `c->pan_ox`/`c->pan_oy` where zz answers the centred offsets. And `#{window_width}` itself is not comparable between the binaries, because the zz raw client reserves about 29 columns and 2 rows of chrome, so the differential compares the boolean and the offsets rather than the window measurement they are derived from; the middle band this opens, a window wider than the zz pane area but narrower than the pty, answers 0 in zz while the pane area really does scroll. Only an Interactive client with a terminal carries a viewport; a Control client sized by refresh-client -C answers null for all three, which the pin does not.

closed.title: Reset hyperlink history
closed.resolution: The acceptance had asked for a terminal-owned action that clears normal history and resets the VT hyperlink registry atomically. It was re-scoped on 2026-09-02 against two measurements. cmd_capture_pane_exec runs the same window_pane_reset_mode_all and grid_clear_history for both spellings and adds exactly one call under -H, screen_reset_hyperlinks(wp->screen), which drops the pane's hyperlinks structure so cells keep their ids and the ids resolve to nothing. Probed on a throwaway server with a pane holding `ESC]8;;http://e.com ESC\\ LINK ESC]8;; ESC\\`: `capture-pane -pe` answered `^[]8;;http://e.com^[\\LINK^[]8;;^[\\` before, the same after a plain `clear-history`, and plain `LINK` after `clear-history -H`. The second measurement is that zz has no such observable: its `capture-pane -pe` answered plain `LINK` for the same pane before any clear, because hyperlink URIs are not in zz's capture transports at all, which is capture.rich-transports. libghostty stores hyperlinks per cell behind ghostty_grid_ref_hyperlink_uri and exposes no registry, no reset, and no writer; the only primitive that would drop them is ghostty_terminal_reset, which takes the whole terminal with it. So the reset has no primitive and no observer, and the honest product stance is that the flag stops failing: catalog.rs promotes -H from an unsupported flag to a real one, clear-history runs its ordinary history clear under either spelling, and `bind-key ... clear-history -H` binds where it used to be refused. compat/scenarios/smoke/clear-history-hyperlinks.txt asserts those ten facts on both binaries through an attached pty client, because a detached `clear-history` still answers `pane is not attached` on zz under clients.interactive-refresh. Reopen when capture gains hyperlink transports under capture.rich-transports, because a captured URI would then make the missing reset visible.

closed.title: Produce pane focus and clipboard hooks
closed.resolution: window_pane_update_focus is the pin's only pane-focus producer, and the daemon now carries the same per-pane flag on ServerState and evaluates it only where the pin calls it: attach and detach through server_client_set_session, the tty focus keys, an overlay opening or closing, and the window_lost_pane that follows a pane removal run unconditionally, while window_set_active_pane and session_set_current run only while focus-events is on. The pane counts as focused while it is its window's active pane and some attached, focused, overlay-free client has that window current, an exited pane is skipped, and a hook is raised only on a flag edge. The 2026-09-01 revert's two measurements both hold now. With the option off, the walk attach / select-pane / new-window / select-window / kill-pane / detach raises exactly one pane-focus-in at attach and one pane-focus-out at detach on both binaries; with it on the transitions queue ahead of window-pane-changed, session-window-changed, client-session-changed, client-attached and client-detached, and after window-pane-changed on the pane removal, because that is the one call site the pin evaluates after its own notify. Both runs are asserted as raw timelines in smoke/hooks-pane-focus, which drives one real pty client on a throwaway server per side and compares the pin's queue order to zz's. smoke/hooks-pane-focus-clients drives two pty clients on one pane and proves the rest of the predicate: only the last client to lose focus and the first to regain it move the flag, the tty focus keys update the pane before the client-focus-out notify and after the client-focus-in one (tty-keys.c orders those two differently), a display-panes overlay opening drops the flag and its key closing restores it, and switch-client evaluates the old session's window then the new one ahead of client-session-changed. Two of the three zz-only residues the revert found are fixed with it: attach now re-sets the client focused flag the way server_client_set_session does, so a switch-client no longer leaves the client unfocused, and the TUI no longer replays a focus report after every attach, so a pty attach raises no client-focus-in where the pin raises none (the daemon already assumes a fresh attachment is focused, which is what made the replay redundant). The third is fixed in the transition itself, though only by construction and not by a differential row: pane_focus_transition returns early for a pane the engine marks dead, the way window_pane_update_focus returns early for PANE_EXITED, so a pane whose process exited under remain-on-exit keeps whatever flag it had and raises nothing. A side probe with remain-on-exit on, focus-events on and one pty client produced the same hook timeline on both binaries across a pane death and the select-pane after it, but it does not isolate the skip on its own. Two divergences stay and are recorded in knowledge/tmux/divergences.md rather than here alone: zz's clients report focus regardless of the focus-events option, where the pin only enables terminal focus reporting while the option is on and therefore never receives a focus key with it off, so a zz client that loses focus with the option off still moves the pane flag; and new-window queues window-linked after session-window-changed on the pin and before it in zz, which is why neither differential logs window-linked. pane-set-clipboard closed earlier under the same group. Two edges measured at the 2026-09-02 gate review stay as residue. With destroy-unattached on, detaching the last client logs pane-focus-out:%1 then session-closed on the pin, while zz queues pane-focus-out in the same place but detach_with_event_hooks runs enforce_destroy_unattached before the queued events, so the hook body expands #{pane_id} empty against a pane that is already gone; pre-baking the pane into the event's variables or running the detach's events first would close it. And hook bodies see no format client in zz (a pre-existing gap owned by formats.context-producer-fidelity): with #{client_name} in a pane-focus hook body the pin resolves the session's attached pty client and zz expands it empty, so the client half of the group's first acceptance clause is not differentially asserted; add #{client_name} to smoke/hooks-pane-focus once hook format-client resolution lands.

closed.title: Classify after-queue as explicit-only
closed.resolution: Pinned tmux registers after-queue as a session hook but has no automatic queue-completion producer for it. Ordinary single-command and multi-command queues leave the hook untouched; universal set-hook -R executes the stored hook exactly once. zz already matches both behaviors through its stored hook table and generic RunHook effect, so no runtime implementation was needed. The daemon inventory now partitions the 68 pinned names into 64 automatic producers, explicit-only after-queue, and three active pane-event gaps. The existing three-step args-parse-set-hook differential now proves ordinary queue inactivity, exact explicit execution count, and continued inactivity after manual runs on both engines. The oracle's hook roster describes registered names, not automatic producer paths. No protocol change was needed.

closed.title: Construct clean command and status job environments
closed.resolution: Shell-form run-shell and if-shell now construct each child from an empty environment, then apply server-global values followed by resolved session values. Hidden and unset entries disappear, and an explicit missing target becomes sessionless. During startup they preserve modeled TERM-family values; afterward they force TERM from default-terminal, TERM_PROGRAM=tmux, TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION=3.8-zz, COLORTERM=truecolor, and TMUX with the resolved session id or -1. Status #() follows the same clean construction with global-only state and a TMUX suffix of -1. Visible modeled TMUX_PANE survives but is not synthesized. The private tmux launcher is prepended to modeled PATH, stale private values are rejected, and current zz transport and reentry values are injected only where needed. Focused daemon tests cover overlay precedence, hidden and unset values, startup and post-startup identity, missing targets, status scope, and the private launcher. The three-step differential gives eight assertions per engine, and the attached fixture proves global-only status state. Delayed callback timing, copy-pipe and popup environments, and status cwd remain active separately. No mux or wire protocol changed.

closed.title: Normalize remaining job environments
closed.resolution: display-popup now spawns its PTY from the pinned producer scope, the way job_run builds one from environ_for_session plus the -e environment. The child starts from the global overlay and the target pane session's overlay with hidden and child-unset entries dropped, then the multiplexer identity — TERM from default-terminal, TERM_PROGRAM=tmux, TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION=3.8-zz, COLORTERM=truecolor — then TMUX carrying that session's id, and only then the -e assignments, so a repeated -e wins by its last occurrence and an -e can override TMUX, TERM or a hidden name; an -e with no '=' or an empty name is dropped in silence, as environ_put drops it. The working directory owns PWD last, so -e PWD loses to a -d or target-client cwd. TMUX_PANE is no longer synthesized: a popup is a job, not a pane, and only a modeled TMUX_PANE reaches the child. The terminal worker now stamps its identity before the spawn environment rather than after, and the session scope drops the TERM family so a pane's own zz identity is unchanged. The two-popup differential runs four checks over twenty assertions per engine. Copy-pipe closed earlier under the same group; no mux or wire protocol changed.

closed.title: Order immediate background run-shell environment sampling
closed.resolution: Absent-delay and -d 0 background run-shell jobs now launch at the end of the command group that queued them, sampling the job environment and default-terminal at that boundary instead of at command-handling time. The 8-check differential fixture sources a config group that sets ORDER_V and default-terminal before the job and again after it: on both sides the background child reads the after values, while the foreground forms read the before values and the next command in the group only runs once the job has exited. This closure covers server-side groups (sourced files, command blocks, alias groups, and inserted command bodies). Chains split across separate client requests - an argv `;` chain or a Control-mode line - still start the child before the later request arrives, because the daemon receives one command per request and has no batch boundary to defer to; the same holds for a hook body appended with set-hook -a, where each appended element is its own group.

closed.title: Sample positive-delay run-shell environments at launch
closed.resolution: Shell-form run-shell with an explicit numeric delay greater than zero now retains its command, target identity and numeric session id, expanded text and numeric arguments, and cwd string at scheduling. When the timer fires, it samples current global state, the live original-session overlay or the retained original overlay after destruction, default-terminal, and the startup TERM gate. Same-name session recreation cannot replace the retained original overlay, while a target missing at scheduling stays global-only with a TMUX suffix of -1 even if a matching session appears before launch. Cwd existence fallback runs at child launch against the retained cwd string. Deterministic foreground daemon coverage waits for active_shell_jobs before mutating state. The three-step differential fixture proves the background live, destroyed and recreated, missing and later created, and startup-crossing cases, including frozen formats, numeric arguments, target identity, cwd, launch environment, and default terminal. It reports twelve assertions per engine with zero differences. run-shell -C, if-shell, absent -d, -d 0, immediate background ordering, cwd producer selection, copy-pipe, and popup jobs retain separate owners. No wire protocol or snapshot field changed.

closed.title: Select pinned working directories for shell jobs
closed.resolution: Shell-form run-shell and if-shell now select cwd in pinned order: literal -c, startup client, unattached provenance client, explicit target session, attached invoking-client session, HOME, then root. Positive-delay jobs freeze that selection before the timer and retain launch-time existence fallback. Status #() uses the attached session path instead of pane_current_path, and its command cache is scoped per client. Focused daemon and status tests pass. The three-step differential completes eight checks per engine. The attached fixture keeps the pane in a distinct command cwd, proves status cwd, and covers 24 real Interactive and Control run-shell and if-shell cases across valid, missing, and omitted targets on zz and pinned tmux. No protocol or snapshot field changed.

closed.title: Dispatch client focus through Any bindings
closed.resolution: With focus-events enabled, writable ClientFocus runs through the modal prequeue, then session activity and FocusIn-only latest-geometry accounting, then synthetic Any dispatch. The daemon selects transient tables in chooser, copy-mode or command-output, and effective-root order. A transient Any binding wins; an unbound transient table falls back to the effective root without retiring the mode. A root Any binding runs when no transient mode applies. The daemon resolves attachment and pane context again after prompt submission before it dispatches the selected command. Disabled focus bypasses accounting and dispatch. Read-only focus retains its modal bypass, resolves the whole Any binding, authorizes every command before any effect, and rejects a mixed safe and unsafe chain atomically. Exact FocusIn and FocusOut remain invalid key names, and even injected exact bindings do not replace Any. Synthetic ingress preserves pending copy jump capture, numeric prefix state, repeat metadata and deadlines, table fallback and retirement, prefix synchronization, client isolation, and the next real key. The focused daemon cluster passes 9 of 9 tests, and an independent Codex read-only review returned CODE GO. ClientFocus is not CLI-drivable, so this closure makes no differential or canonical-suite claim.

closed.title: Fix emacs word-end and vi numeric repeat dispatch
closed.resolution: The emacs M-f default stores the pin's send-keys -X next-word-end action. Vi numeric capture consumes the buffered count at the first send or send-keys command whose option prefix contains -X. If that command already contains -N, its stored repeat wins; otherwise zz inserts one separate -N count pair immediately before the option argument containing -X. The engine does not scan onward after a stored -N, a command list with no qualifying -X leaves the count armed, and later actions do not inherit it. One exhaustive typed policy carries a u32 count through one flat TerminalViewAction::CopyModeCounted action: movements, jumps, matching brackets, and repeat-search execute count times; other-end swaps only for odd counts; select-line spans count logical lines; copy-end-of-line spans through the end of row N and copies once; other toggles, selection, copy, cancel, and later actions execute once. Counted raw key sends carry one repeat field instead of preallocating N tokens. Terminal delivery stops on the first full input queue. Browser events and both clients cap their native repeat path at MAX_BROWSER_KEY_REPEAT (9,999), because tmux has no browser pane. Direct -N parsing expands the last value, accepts 1 through UINT_MAX, preserves attached and clustered forms plus command abbreviations, and reports the pin's invalid, too-small, and too-large errors. Protocol v75 appends flat counted-copy tag 28 and browser-repeat tag 7; tests reject the removed recursive action tag and nested payloads. The strict send-keys-repeat differential covers separate, attached, clustered, duplicate, formatted, alias, prefix, and error forms. Invalid nonempty -X grammar returns the pin's neutral prefix value 1, represented as no buffered count, so the next digit starts a fresh prefix. Multi-digit vi capture remains bounded at 9,999 per client; bare no-key counts and `-N <n> -X` with no action remain pane-prefix residuals under terminal.key-control. The nine digit bindings retain their native copy-mode-repeat list-keys shape under keys.copy-mode-native-numeric-prefix; unrelated cursor-word, search, goto-line, and jump command shapes remain open under keys.copy-mode-binding-fidelity.

closed.title: Match shared copy-mode binding commands
closed.resolution: Cursor-word search, prompted search, goto-line, and character jumps retain divergent stored command shapes; this gap does not assume their native behavior is exact. `binding:copy-mode:g` joined the group when the emacs goto-line key was installed: it renders the same command vi ':' renders, now a structured `command-prompt -p "(goto line)" { send-keys -X goto-line -- "%%" }` block rather than a string template, so the only remaining difference from the pin on both keys is the -P pane-cell prompt flag. That flag is the shared cause of fourteen of these sixteen items: the pin renders vi '/', '?', ':', 'f', 'F', 't', 'T' and emacs 'g', 'C-r', 'C-s', 'f', 'F', 't', 'T' through command-prompt -P, and `prompt.pane-rendered` accepted -P as loudly unsupported because painting a prompt into pane cells would mean the daemon writing another client's grid. The remaining two, vi '#' and '*', need `send-keys -F` format expansion plus the pinned `#{copy_cursor_word}` format, which zz does not publish; zz reaches the same behavior through the native `search-backward-cursor-word` and `search-forward-cursor-word` action names instead. Closing any of the fourteen therefore needs the `prompt.pane-rendered` decision reopened or this acceptance re-scoped onto behavior rather than the rendered command string. The -P claim is measured, not inferred: with the goto-line keys rebuilt as command blocks, the differential prints `command-prompt -p "(goto line)" { send-keys -X goto-line -- "%%" }` on zz against `command-prompt -P -p "(goto line)" { send-keys -X goto-line -- "%%" }` on the pin for both `copy-mode-vi :` and `copy-mode g`, identical apart from that one flag. Re-examined on 2026-09-02 with `#{copy_cursor_word}` now published. The format half of vi '#' and '*' is no longer the blocker, but the stored shape is `send-keys -FX search-backward "#{copy_cursor_word}"` and `search-forward`, and neither `search-backward` nor `search-forward` is a mapped copy action in zz: both are still in the Vocabulary category of copy-mode.action-fidelity's inventory, together with the four incremental and -text spellings and scroll-to-mouse, because copy-mode text search in zz is a client surface driven by `MuxEffect::TerminalUi` and `TerminalUiCommand::BeginSearch`, not a daemon action. Installing the pin's shape today would replace two bindings that work, `send-keys -X search-backward-cursor-word` and its forward twin, with a `-X` name the parser answers `None` for, which the mux turns into a bare `CopyModeRepeat` no-op: the keys would render like the pin and do nothing. So these two now wait on the search action family reaching the engine, not on the format. `send-keys -F` is the other half and is unbuilt: `cmd_send_keys_exec` expands every key argument as a format in the target pane's context before key lookup, while zz's catalog still records -F as a compatibility no-op. Closed on 2026-09-02, both halves. The fourteen -P items closed against the re-scoped `prompt.pane-rendered`, which now accepts `command-prompt -P` as a presentation hint the client owns: the flag is a real catalog option, the daemon raises the same client-surface prompt it raises without it, and the fourteen bindings carry the pin's exact stored strings, `command-prompt -P -T search -p "(search down)" { send-keys -X search-forward -- "%%" }` for vi `/`, the `-1P` single-key form for the four jump keys in both tables, and `command-prompt -Pi -I "#{pane_search_string}" -T search -p "(search up)" { send-keys -X search-backward-incremental -- "%%" }` for emacs `C-r`. compat/scenarios/copy-mode-bindings.txt prints all sixteen keys plus `n` and `N` from `list-keys` on both binaries and every row is identical. The two cursor-word items closed with `send-keys -F`, which turned out to be much narrower than a general key-argument expansion: `args_has(cs->args, 'F')` is read in exactly one place in the pin, `window_copy_expand_search_string` at window-copy.c:1251, which runs the search string through `format_single` in the target pane's context. With `search-backward` and `search-forward` now mapped copy actions, the pin's stored shapes `send-keys -FX search-backward -- "#{copy_cursor_word}"` and its forward twin replace zz's native `search-backward-cursor-word` and `search-forward-cursor-word` bindings, and the native names stay in the parser. One implementation detail is worth keeping: the search string is `args_string(cs->wargs, 0)`, so the expansion has to skip the action's own flags and the `--` the stock bindings carry, not just take the first argument after the action name. Behaviour was proved from a real attached client's keyboard on both binaries, driving the pty rather than the CLI, and reading the copy-mode format family back: `/` then `zeta` lands copy_cursor_x,y on 0,2 with search_match zeta; `?` then `alpha` wraps to 5,5; `*` and `#` on the word `alpha` land 6,1 and 5,5 without a prompt at all; `f g`, `t g`, `F a` and `T a` land 11,0, 10,0, 9,0 and 5,0 in both tables, each from a single-key prompt; `C-s` then `zeta` moves the cursor to 4,2 before Enter, which is the incremental prompt running the search on every keystroke, and `C-r` then `alpha` moves it to 0,0; and `:` then `5` and emacs `g` then `7` move `#{scroll_position}` to 5 and 7 on a pane with forty lines of history behind it. Two things are recorded rather than closed. `#{pane_search_string}` in the `C-r` and `C-s` `-I` value expands empty in zz, so those two prompts open empty instead of pre-filled with the last search; that is the accepted `format:pane_search_string` item in `formats.pane-runtime`, whose stance is that the search query genuinely differs per viewer in zz, and it is unchanged by this work. The `copy-mode-search-prompt` command that used to be bound to `/`, `?`, `C-r` and `C-s` still exists; only the stock bindings moved off it. The armed count survives a prompt binding the way wme->prefix does: the pin's numeric prompt hands the first non-digit key on with send-keys -N already run, and window_copy_command resets the prefix only after the answer ran, so from column 0 of `alpha beta gamma` `3 f a` lands 12,0 and `2 / alpha Enter` lands 5,2 on both binaries. The branch's engine consumed the prefix at the command-prompt binding and answered 4,0 for the counted jump; fixed at the gate on 2026-09-02, and smoke/copy-mode-prompt-bindings now presses both counted shapes.

closed.title: Add supported stock emacs non-navigation defaults
closed.resolution: Added the six remaining stock emacs keys whose typed actions already existed: C-[ runs cancel, C-k runs copy-pipe-end-of-line-and-cancel, C-w runs copy-pipe-and-cancel, N runs search-reverse, R runs rectangle-toggle, and n runs search-again. Each binding stores the pin's single send-keys -X command and carries no repeat bit. KeyEngine tests cover the six bindings and retain the prior Escape, M-w, and C-g bindings; exact equality with the audited stock key set proves that none overwrote another key. Mux tests cover cancel, both copy variants, forward and reverse search repetition, and rectangle toggle as typed terminal effects. The 17 absent stock keys remain under keys.copy-mode-prompt-defaults and keys.copy-mode-unsupported-default-actions.

closed.title: Add supported stock emacs copy-mode navigation keys
closed.resolution: Added the pin's 13 previously absent emacs navigation keys with exact send-keys -X command shapes and nonrepeat metadata: C-Down, C-M-Down, C-M-Up, C-M-f, C-Up, End, Home, M-<, M->, M-Down, M-R, M-Up, and Space. Their existing typed actions cover line scrolling, semantic-prompt navigation, matching brackets, line endpoints, history endpoints, half pages, top-line positioning, and page-down without a new terminal action or UI flow. KeyEngine and mux effect tests cover every key and action, and shifted Alt input reaches M-R, M-<, and M->. At this historical closure 23 stock keys remained: six supported non-navigation defaults, ten prompt-backed defaults, and seven keys behind unsupported actions. The later keys.copy-mode-defaults closure reduced the current residual to 17.

closed.title: Add prompt-backed emacs copy-mode defaults
closed.resolution: All ten keys are installed, so the emacs copy table no longer swallows M-1 through M-9 and g. M-1 through M-9 arm zz's per-client numeric capture with the same `copy-mode-repeat <digit>` command the vi digits use, and the capture rule that only vi digits could extend now covers both copy tables, so M-1 2 accumulates to 12 exactly as the pin's PROMPT_NUMERIC prompt accumulates digits after its -I seed. The next copy action consumes the count through the same engine path as vi: the count lands as one `-N <count>` pair before the argument containing -X, which is what the pin's `{ send-keys -N "%%" }` block does when it writes wme->prefix for the following action. g opens the same goto-line prompt vi ':' opens, and both now carry a structured `{ send-keys -X goto-line -- "%%" }` command block instead of the old string template, so submission edits the leaf argument in place and a typed line number cannot inject a second command. The exact stored command shape in this group's acceptance was not reached and did not vanish: the pin renders both families through `command-prompt -P`, whose pane-cell prompt is loudly unsupported by the accepted `prompt.pane-rendered` decision. The nine M-digit shape divergences moved to `keys.copy-mode-native-numeric-prefix`, which already owns that stance for the vi digits, and `binding:copy-mode:g` moved to `keys.copy-mode-binding-fidelity` beside `binding:copy-mode-vi::`. Nothing wire-reachable changed.

closed.title: Implement missing stock copy-mode actions
closed.resolution: All seven stock keys are installed with the pin's stored `send-keys -X <action>` shape and its nonrepeat metadata. The last two, `copy-mode-vi r` and `copy-mode r`, waited on refresh-toggle, which is a re-sync of the frozen backing rather than a cursor move. window_copy_refresh_start refuses a view of another pane and view-mode and does nothing when the refresh is already running; window_copy_refresh_timer skips a tick unless the pane has unseen output with no selection and no cursor drag; and window_copy_do_refresh re-clones the backing, keeps the view on the row it was already showing, and only follows new output when oy is 0 and the cursor is on the last row. zz keeps the frozen revision on the client's terminal view and the terminal worker owns no timers, so the daemon runs one 50ms thread while any copy session asks for a refresh and the engine decides which ticks do anything; the three toggle actions carry the bit on both the frozen view and the daemon's copy session, and CopyModeAction gained RefreshOn, RefreshOff, RefreshToggle and the daemon-driven RefreshRevision tick, which is the v94 protocol bump. Measured on the pin against a pane printing a line every 50ms with an attached pty client: `#{scroll_position}` and `#{copy_cursor_line}` both hold after entry with the refresh off, the position climbs after `refresh-on` while the cursor line does not move, `refresh-toggle` freezes it and a second toggle restarts it, a live selection holds it even with the refresh running and clearing the selection resumes it, `refresh-off` freezes it, and with the view at the bottom and the cursor on the last row the position stays 0 instead of climbing. compat/scenarios/smoke/copy-mode-refresh.txt asserts those thirteen facts as comparisons rather than absolute rows, because the two clients render panes of different heights, and both binaries answer identically, including `list-keys` rendering `send-keys -X refresh-toggle` for `r` in both tables.

closed.title: Separate literal and hex DEL key identities
closed.resolution: Literal DEL, caret plus DEL, and textual 0x7f now retain distinct key identities and pinned rendering across bind, list, filter, unbind, prefix, prefix2, and backspace. Raw DEL renders as C-?, caret plus DEL renders as C-C-?, and textual 0x7f renders as a raw DEL byte. send-prefix and configured BSpace emit one literal DEL for raw and textual-hex values while the caret-modified value emits nothing. Focused mux tests and live PTY capture cover both transport paths. The strict 40-step differential completes 196 fixture checks per engine with no differing channel.

closed.title: Deliver shifted special keys from both clients
closed.resolution: Proved semantic:shift-special-key-names and key:root:S-Up, key:root:S-Down, key:root:S-Left, key:root:S-Right, key:root:BTab, key:root:S-Home, key:root:S-End, key:root:S-PPage, key:root:S-NPage, key:root:S-Insert, key:root:S-Delete, key:root:S-F1, key:root:S-F2, key:root:S-F3, key:root:S-F4, key:root:S-F5, key:root:S-F6, key:root:S-F7, key:root:S-F8, key:root:S-F9, key:root:S-F10, key:root:S-F11, key:root:S-F12. Pinned d77c9dc6 key-string.c prints C-, M-, S- in that order; tty-keys.c decodes xterm modifier 2 as shift and CSI Z as BTab. smoke/keys-shift-attached sends identical bytes to both real pty clients: ESC[1;2D runs previous-window and reads window_index=0, ESC[1;2C runs next-window and reads window_index=1; all 23 named keys fire marker bindings individually. The shared input_key_name now retains shift on special keys (Insert/Delete use the pin canonical IC/DC bases), maps shifted Tab to BTab, and validates the emitted names. The TUI preserves CSI modifiers and additionally decodes modified CSI F1-F4. Desktop platform events use that fold in both terminal and prefix capture; terminal_view::platform_shifted_special_keys_keep_their_daemon_names is the desktop unit proof, not a pty proof. The old desktop Shift+PageUp/PageDown local-scroll interception consumed those bindings; it was removed so the daemon receives them. Existing mouse scrolling remains. No wire variants, fields, or types changed. The chooser record formerly said "S-Up and S-Down cannot be delivered by zz at all"; this group supersedes that limitation without claiming chooser swap defaults were added.

closed.title: Match tmux key-name validation
closed.resolution: The tmux command parser now accepts the pin's key vocabulary while rejecting long Ctrl- and Alt- aliases, malformed function-key names, out-of-range User keys, and invalid hex forms before any binding or option state changes. F1 through F12 use the pin's exact grammar; User and hex numbers follow its signed, whitespace-tolerant, prefix-consuming, 32-bit wrapping rules. Caret followed by a literal control byte from 1 through 31 works across bind, list, filter, unbind, prefix, prefix2, and backspace. Printable ASCII hex keys retain identity distinct from their literal forms while rendering like the pin, including independent bind, list, filter, unbind, option readback, and send-prefix behavior. The shared native key parser remains permissive outside tmux commands. A 40-step differential and 161 fixture checks pass on both engines. Literal DEL, caret plus DEL, and hex 0x7f remain split into keys.literal-delete-identity.

closed.title: Reset explicit client key tables and retry in root
closed.resolution: Proved semantic:key-table-reset-after-dispatch and semantic:unbound-key-retry-in-root. Pinned d77c9dc6 server-client.c server_client_key_callback resets the client table before a non-repeat binding dispatch; an unbound non-root key retries root, and a miss there is dropped unless it began in root or repeating state. A repeating binding retains the table while repeat-time runs; a non-repeat key during repetition retries root with ordinary forwarding allowed, and the prefix interrupts an explicit non-prefix table. KeyEngine now distinguishes persistent pane copy-mode tables from explicit switch-client tables, including an explicit copy-mode table. switch-client -T uses switch_client_table at its sole changed daemon callsite. Copy-mode setup and output-overlay table restoration keep their existing setter; restoring a non-copy table keeps one-shot semantics. active_table hides an expired repeat deadline so client_key_table reads root before another press. Attached proof smoke/keys-table-lifecycle: M-r Left changes pane_width 30 to 25 and reads root; M-r a reads root and capture-pane contains no a while an ordinary root key canary reaches cat; an unbound b retries its root binding; two repeat Right presses read resize and widths 30 then 35, followed by root after the 1500ms timer. Shared unit tests additionally cover root Any fallback, explicit root forwarding, repeat expiry/zero repeat-time/non-repeat fallback, prefix interruption, and explicit versus persistent copy tables. No wire type or version changed.

closed.title: Finish list-keys output fidelity
closed.resolution: list-keys now implements the pin's optional positional key, -1, -O, and -r grammar, including clustered and attached options, --, repeated -O last-wins behavior, exact one-positional and missing -O errors, key-before-sort-before-table error precedence, valid-but-absent and note-filtered unknown-key errors, global and per-table note sorting, and reversal only when an order is selected. Sorting and filtering happen before -1, while repeat and width aggregates are computed after truncation. Literal stored space bases render as Space and C-Space, widths use those spellings, and positional matching compares base, type, and modifiers without stored spelling or key flags. Command and Control clients receive the selected line on stdout; attached Interactive clients receive a display-time-backed frozen status message without a command-output overlay. Stock copy-mode and copy-mode-vi bindings now publish no repeat bits while persistent copy-table movement, jump capture, and numeric repetition remain runtime key-engine behavior. Equal-base, cross-table, inapplicable-field, and four-byte Unicode comparator cases are bounded separately under list-keys.deterministic-sort-ties, and the existing long Ctrl-/Alt- spelling overacceptance remains under the strict-key divergence.

closed.title: Construct config and source groups before effects
closed.resolution: Each config file is now parsed, alias-expanded, and statically validated as one construction unit before any command from that file runs. The first construction failure retains earlier bare environment assignments but discards every command effect from that file. Parse-only source-file -n performs the same validation using the pre-file environment for expansion, while applying neither assignments nor commands. Startup roots and files matched by one source invocation remain independent file units constructed in path order before batch replay, so one bad file drops only itself and later siblings continue. A nested child receives a fresh construction snapshot; its failure drops the child without stopping its parent's later physical groups. Runtime target and effect errors remain sequential and prune only their own physical group. Control reports one located config error without a sourced-command guard. Verbose source output includes successful alias-subparse traces and completed physical groups before the first failure, including parse-only files. Focused parser and daemon regressions cover assignment visibility, alias snapshots, diagnostics, startup, sibling, nested, Control, verbose, and runtime contrast behavior. The strict two-step config-chain-parse-abort differential matches the pin across all comparison channels. Exact typed-position behavior for recognized unsupported choose-client and switch-mode commands, multi-command alias bodies, non-UTF-8 config bytes, and source-file standard input remain with their existing tracker owners. No protocol change was needed.

closed.title: Match shared command arity errors
closed.resolution: The old eight-command runtime gate is gone. Every implemented upstream command with a finite maximum now consumes its catalog maximum after leading option grammar and the required minimum, before unsupported-capability rejection, target resolution, or effects. The pinned oracle contains 80 finite maxima: eight belong to explicitly unimplemented commands and all 72 executable commands use the shared validator. The daemon's common parser covers its finite roster, confirm-before now uses that parser, and all three lock commands share it without changing native target-only parsers. Stored bind-key and set-hook commands validate child minima and maxima after alias expansion and option grammar but before unsupported-capability rejection or prior-state replacement. One exhaustive daemon-path test executes every canonical name and built-in alias with maximum plus one arguments and proves the canonical diagnostic and unchanged state. The strict three-step fixture checks all 71 generic-CLI-routed finite commands and 62 aliases at exit 1 with empty stdout, exact stderr, and unchanged pane, buffer, and file state. Exact native attach keeps its positional-session extension and remains outside this generic CLI proof. Variadic commands, eight catalogued unimplemented commands, zz-native commands, and inner callback grammar are unchanged. No protocol change was needed.

closed.title: Match shared command flag errors
closed.resolution: One catalog-driven tmux option parser now covers all 83 implemented upstream canonical commands and 74 built-in aliases across mux execution, the daemon's preempted command paths, and stored bind-key and set-hook children. Exact native attach uses the same leading-option diagnostics while retaining its positional-session and --restart-daemon extensions; its first positional ends flag scanning. The parser emits canonical unknown-flag, invalid-flag, usage, and missing-value diagnostics, preserves required-value absorption and optional-value lookahead, and scans the full option grammar before positional arity and catalogued unsupported-capability rejection. Recognized parked flags therefore lose to a too-few or too-many diagnostic, matching the pin. The catalog keeps product-truthful usage strings for list-commands and completion while exposing the pinned usage text only for diagnostics. The strict three-step fixture runs 516 byte-compared probes against zz and the pin: 513 exact failures plus three required-value absorption successes. It also proves unchanged panes, buffers, files, bindings, and hooks. Inner args_parse callback grammar, zz-native commands, and whole-command-group prevalidation remain with their existing tracker owners. No wire protocol or version change was needed.

closed.title: Preflight warm command arguments before effects
closed.resolution: Against an already-running compatible local default or explicit-socket daemon, a Command client now applies the existing static tmux validator to every ordinary unaliased invocation in the daemon's immutable prepared vector. Canonical names, built-in aliases, unique prefixes, recognized parked commands, flags, arity, required values, and nested blocks therefore resolve before the CLI captures stdin, selects attach or TUI routing, or executes the first effect. Callback construction, user-alias validation, and native zz commands retain their existing paths. Exact unaliased attach and attach-session bypass generic validation only in vector position zero, where the CLI's dedicated native parser owns the positional-session and --restart-daemon extensions; later exact spellings and every user alias to attach use ordinary catalog grammar. The ClientKind gate leaves Control preparation and framing unchanged. A later preparation error returns the pinned diagnostic without applying an earlier mutation, while runtime target and effect errors keep sequential queue ordering and prune only later commands. Focused daemon coverage proves canonical, built-in alias, prefix, parked, native, callback, user-alias, and position-sensitive attach behavior. The 112 CLI integration tests prove the three generic argument-error classes, both later exact attach spellings, native position-zero attach routing, and runtime ordering; the existing Control regression proves its framed preparation behavior is unchanged. The strict three-step cli-chain-parse-abort differential now runs six warm probes plus its existing cold matrix with zero differences. No protocol or snapshot change was needed.

closed.title: Match remaining command errors
closed.resolution: Nested non-detached new-session now follows pinned tmux d77c9dc6 through generic option and arity parsing, target-plus-command or window-name conflict, expanded window-name validation, expanded session-name validation, existing-session -A delegation, duplicate detection, unresolved session-group name validation, and start-directory expansion before the nesting refusal. The refusal still precedes width and height validation, and every early path is mutation-free. A narrow routing parser admits catalogued -t only while selecting the terminal client and running this nested preflight; normal mux execution still reports new-session -t as unsupported, so session groups remain excluded. Canonical, built-in alias, unique-prefix, and user-alias forms share the path, including a later member of a CLI command list. Fresh -d creation, Control fresh creation and -A miss, and already-attached fresh creation remain allowed. Existing -A and -Ad hits still refuse through attach handling, while -Ad misses remain detached. Focused mux, daemon, and app tests cover validation order, one-time canonical format expansion, lifecycle branches, routing, and unchanged state. The real attached-client differential compares exact exit status, stderr, session roster, client count, aliases, and command-list stop behavior on zz and the pin and passes on both. No protocol, catalog capability, or wire-version change was needed.

closed.title: Abort invalid local CLI groups before autospawn
closed.resolution: Against a missing local socket, the CLI now applies an alias-free static tmux syntax pass to the complete raw command vector before routing, stdin capture, TUI handoff, daemon spawn, startup config, or effects. The pass resolves canonical names, built-in aliases, and unique prefixes; validates flags, arity, callback argument types, and nested typed blocks for all 83 implemented and nine parked upstream commands; and parses an exact native attach before validating its tail. Arbitrary user-alias names cannot trigger autospawn, while startup config can still shadow a canonical spelling. A successful raw pass spawns a generation-identified daemon, which prepares the full vector under one post-config alias snapshot before execution. Invalid startup aliases and callbacks return nonzero before effects, and a one-shot ownership lease stops only the newly spawned empty daemon after the bootstrap client receives the error and disconnects; startup reentry, a competing external client, or any command commits the daemon. Focused CLI and daemon tests cover routing-sensitive new-session and attach forms, -N, canonical startup shadows, arbitrary startup aliases, nested alias failures, contender and pipeline races, and parked-command syntax. The strict three-step fixture retains its row and adds eleven cold probes on both engines without changing the differential artifact. Runtime failures, remote --host, Control, warm unaliased argument-group validation, config and source-file group construction, rollback, native zz command grammar, and unsupported-command execution remain outside this closure. No protocol or snapshot change was needed.

closed.title: Abort typed local CLI preparation errors before effects
closed.resolution: Against an already-running compatible daemon, local default and explicit-socket CLI preflight scans the complete prepared vector for typed name and alias-body errors before stdin capture, attach or TUI routing, or command execution. A later unknown command returns exit 1 with the pinned error shape and no earlier effect; malformed alias bodies use zz's loud unknown-command shape while aliases.command-bodies remains open. Prepared runtime command failures keep sequential queue ordering, including earlier effects and pruning later commands. A focused binary regression uses a malformed live alias after a mutating command, and the strict three-step smoke scenario proves unknown-name parse atomicity and runtime-error ordering with zero differential mismatches. The later mux.local-cli-autospawn-parse-abort closure extends whole-vector preparation across the missing-daemon seam, and mux.command-group-argument-parse-abort later closes warm ordinary argument validation. Remote --host remains excluded; config and source-file replay remains open under mux.chain-parse-abort.

closed.title: Match command positional maximums
closed.resolution: Catalog metadata initially limited choose-buffer, choose-tree, display-message, display-panes, load-buffer, save-buffer, and set-buffer to one positional argument and select-pane to none. Mux and daemon parsing emitted the pin's exact canonical maximum error after valid leading options but before target resolution, callbacks, buffer mutation, or file I/O. The daemon parser followed tmux's first-positional stop rule, so later option-looking tokens counted as positionals. Focused production-path tests covered canonical commands and aliases with unchanged sessions, panes, overlays, buffers, and files. The command palette consumed the same catalog contract, so select-pane offered live pane targets only after -t and never as a bare positional. The three-step differential initially exercised all eight canonical names and all six aliases with exact status, streams, and unchanged state. Required positional bounds later closed under mux.positional-minimums, mux.command-arity-errors later removed the partial roster, and mux.command-flag-errors later closed the shared flag and usage diagnostics. The later mux.error-shapes closure matched nested new-session precedence.

closed.title: Match command positional minimums
closed.resolution: A sorted catalog sidecar records the fourteen nonzero required positional bounds: thirteen commands require one argument and if-shell requires two. Every other command defaults to zero, keeping optional catalog slots optional. Mux parsing validates the minimum after flags and before maximum checks, targets, or effects. The shared daemon parser covers if-shell, load-buffer, save-buffer, and wait-for at the same boundary, while display-menu and confirm-before use the same validator before targets or effects. Focused production-path tests cover all fourteen aliases, canonical diagnostics, missing-target precedence, and unchanged sessions, menus, confirmations, waits, buffers, and source effects. The three-step differential exercises every canonical name and alias with exit status 1, empty stdout, exact stderr, and unchanged pane, buffer, and file state. The later mux.command-arity-errors closure applies the same minimum and maximum validation to stored bind-key and set-hook children before replacing state, and mux.command-flag-errors later closed the shared flag and usage diagnostics. No protocol change was needed. Callback bodies and incomplete menu triples remain under their existing owners. The later mux.error-shapes closure matched nested new-session precedence.

closed.title: Model optional resize-pane direction amounts
closed.resolution: This was a catalog-only reconciliation. Runtime already accepted bare -D, -L, -R, and -U with the default amount 1, plus attached and separated integer amounts. Static CommandOptionSpec metadata now marks the four direction values optional while retaining attached-value support, and manifest reconciliation compares that shape with the pinned oracle. No handler, effect, wire field, tag, or protocol version changed. Nine focused resize tests pass, along with 175 protocol unit tests and 14 protocol framing tests. The strict 16-step resize-directions differential and the checked-in canonical summary have zero differences and no skips. resize-pane -M and -T remain open under their existing owners. The later mux.command-flag-errors closure consumes these optional shapes for exact lookahead. The later mux.error-shapes closure matched nested new-session precedence.

closed.title: Consume the client attach command and mouse focus options
closed.resolution: Closed on 2026-09-02 against pinned tmux d77c9dc6 with both binaries driven on real ptys (scenarios default-client-command and focus-follows-mouse). `default-client-command`: server_client_dispatch_command sees argc == 0 for a client that reaches the server with no command of its own and queues server_client_default_command, which reads the option as a command list and inserts it after the callback, so the bare client runs the list and exits with its status. zz's launcher on PATH hard-coded `new-session -A` for an empty command line; it now marks every command line it forwards with the private `--bootstrap-launcher-client` argument, and the bundled executable, on an empty command line carrying that mark, asks the daemon for `show-options -sqv default-client-command`, parses the answer with the same config parser a bound command string goes through, and runs the result through the ordinary command-chain path, so the list picks up TUI attach routing, the daemon spawn, and the error channels an explicit argument gets. Measured on both binaries: `display-message -p custom` writes `custom` and exits 0; the two-command list `display-message -p one ; display-message -p two` writes both lines in order; `new-session -d -s NAME` creates that session and lets the client exit 0; and an unknown command is refused when the option is set, with the pin's `unknown command: no-such-command` on stderr, status 1, and the stored list left alone, which zz already matched. The acceptance clause's read-only half was re-scoped after measurement. It read "keeping the pin's read-only refusal for a list that is not all read-only commands"; that branch of server_client_default_command cannot be reached by any client the pin's own command line can produce. CLIENT_READONLY is reachable on the pin before any command is dispatched: server_acl_join sets `c->flags |= CLIENT_READONLY` for a user whose ACL entry carries SERVER_ACL_READONLY (server-access.c), and server.c calls it when the client connects, so a second Unix user granted `server-access -a -r USER` who runs a bare `tmux -S sock` reaches server_client_default_command with the flag on and gets `client is read-only` for a list that is not all read-only; attach-session -r, switch-client -r and a later refresh-client -f read-only set it directly too. zz cannot produce a read-only client at join because its socket is single-user 0600 and `server-access` is accepted-native under command:server-access, so no zz client the launcher path can produce carries the flag, which is why nothing in this group claims the refusal - not because the pin branch is unreachable. The pin's usage string is `tmux [-2CDhlNuVv] [-c shell-command] [-f file] [-L socket-name] [-S socket-path] [-T features] [command [flags]]` and `tmux -r` is answered with `unknown option -- r` and status 1, measured on the pin. One recorded divergence is deliberately kept: the option's own default, `new-session` with no arguments, still becomes zz's `new-session -A`, which is the create-or-attach launcher behavior knowledge/tmux/divergences.md already records as silent and product-friendly. Any other stored value runs verbatim, so setting the option is what a script sees, and setting it to `new-session` restores the pin's create-another-session launcher only by spelling it differently. `focus-follows-mouse`: server_client_check_mouse turns a KEYC_TYPE_MOUSEMOVE resolved inside a pane that is not the window's active one into window_redraw_active_switch plus window_set_active_pane while the option is on, and tty.c forces MODE_MOUSE_ALL on the client so a real terminal reports motion at all. The value now rides the option map every client already receives: protocol v94 appends MuxOptionKey::FocusFollowsMouse, the daemon stamps the session-effective value into effective_mux_options beside `mouse`, a set at any session scope raises MuxOptionChanged from stored_scalar_execution, and both clients gate their pointer route on it - the raw TUI in handle_mouse before it decides who owns the event, the GPUI workspace with an on_mouse_move listener on every inactive pane surface. Two measurements shaped that placement. The pin reads the option before the mouse key becomes a binding, so the switch runs with `mouse` off as well: on an attached 79x24 pin client with `mouse off` and `focus-follows-mouse on`, a bare SGR motion report over the right pane still selected it, which is why zz's check sits ahead of its own mouse-option route rather than inside the workspace branch. And a report with a button held is a KEYC_TYPE_MOUSEDRAG, which never reaches that arm, so a drag leaves the active pane alone on both binaries. The scenario drives a 79-column client on both engines, where the one-column divider lands on column 39 and the right pane on columns 40..78, and reads the result through #{pane_active} from outside the client. One hook divergence is recorded rather than copied: the pin's server_client_check_mouse calls window_set_active_pane directly, so a focus-follows-mouse switch fires window-pane-changed but NOT after-select-pane, while zz spends the switch as a `select-pane -t %N` command (the raw TUI's pointer_focus_follows_mouse and the GPUI on_pane_pointer_focus both go through pane_select_command), so after-select-pane also fires on zz - once per motion report that crosses into a new pane. A user with an after-select-pane hook sees it run on every pointer switch in zz and never in the pin; the hookless daemon path that would match the pin (an effect that calls the engine's active-pane setter without the command wrapper) is later-cycle work.

closed.title: Complete option-name format coverage
closed.resolution: The exact 105-name option-consumer roster now resolves as format variables before format-table, command-item, and environment values. Server, session, window, and pane options follow the pinned target and inheritance chain, including active children, attached-client fallback, explicit missing targets, and S/W/P loop retargeting. Flags render as 0 or 1 while other types keep their raw tmux spelling. command-alias, status-format, and update-environment support whole arrays plus normalized numeric and literal named indices, with numeric-before-named ordering and whole-array local shadowing. Mux-owned expansion reads live state.
