Every direct daemon format producer uses the same live resolver, while detached status rendering builds one all-scope snapshot per refresh batch and shares it across clients. Missing run-shell -C and if-shell -F targets read global options while their inserted command or branch keeps the caller execution context. Focused exhaustive tests cover the complete roster and scope counts, the strict 60-step option-name-formats differential has zero topology, geometry, format, output, or warning differences, and the attached status probe passes with bounded polling and complete cleanup. No protocol, wire snapshot, or native GUI styling changed.

closed.title: Draw the pin's pane border chrome
closed.resolution: The whole pane border chrome ships, measured against the pin at d77c9dc6 and proved in four scenarios. GEOMETRY. layout_fix_panes calls layout_add_horizontal_border for every pane and carves the row per pane, not per window: under `top` only a cell whose top edge is the layout root's top edge gets yoff++ and sy--, under `bottom` only a cell whose bottom edge is the root's bottom edge gets sy--, and a one-row cell keeps its row. CellLayout::pane_geometry_with_border applies that carve from the cell's own offsets, which is equivalent to layout_cell_is_top and layout_cell_is_bottom for a tiled tree and needs no restamping at CellLayout::new. MuxEngine::pane_border_status resolves the window option beside it, and all four engine geometry entry points now take the carve: pane_geometry (the daemon's PTY write-back), pane_geometry_at_window_extent and window_extent_for_pane_geometry (the client sizing loop), set_pane_geometry's comparison basis, and list-panes -O size, plus the one window.layout.pane_geometry(pane.id) call formats.rs makes. Scenario smoke/pane-border-status compares all of it against the pin with no client at all, through #{pane_width}, #{pane_height}, #{pane_left}, #{pane_top}, #{pane_at_top}, #{pane_at_bottom} and #{window_layout} plus the harness's own per-command geometry diff: an 80x24 vertical split goes from 80x12 at 0,0 and 80x11 at 0,13 to 80x11 at 0,1 and 80x11 at 0,13 under `top` and to 80x12 at 0,0 and 80x10 at 0,13 under `bottom`; a horizontal split under the lower pane leaves the upper one alone under `bottom` and shrinks both lower panes; a zoomed pane is carved too, to 80x23 at 0,1, because layout_fix_panes still runs over the one-leaf zoom root; and #{window_layout} is the same string at every setting because the adjustment lands on the pane and never on its layout cell. #{pane_at_top} and #{pane_at_bottom} are read against the row rather than the window edge: format_cb_pane_at_top compares yoff to 1 under `top` and format_cb_pane_at_bottom compares yoff + sy to w->sy - 1 under `bottom`, so the first pane still reports at-top with the row above it. THE ROW. The daemon expands pane-border-format once per pane the way window_make_pane_status does and publishes the product on PaneSnapshot.border_status_text (protocol 94 -> 95, appended with the window's resolved status, lines, indicators, pane order and z order). The raw TUI draws it on the row it already reserves for every pane, moving that row to the pane's last line under `bottom`, starting the text two columns right of the pane's left edge the way redraw_mark_border_status starts the status span at wp->xoff + 2, and composing it over an underlay of border cells so a column the format never writes keeps its glyph, which is what window_make_pane_status does by prefilling the status screen before format_draw writes over it (zz_client::compose_status_row_over). The second half of smoke/pane-border-status attaches a real client on a pty inside a recorder server on both binaries and reads the screen back: a distinctive format appears once per pane while the option is on, moves down the screen when the option goes from top to bottom, follows a live format change with no key pressed, and leaves no trace once the option is off. LINES. window_get_border_cell picks the glyph from the family and the cell type, and redraw_get_cell_type computes the cell type from the directions the border continues in; zz's divider list had no notion of a crossing and drew one divider over the other, so the renderer now builds the set of divider cells and derives each cell's type from its four neighbours. All seven families are in one table beside the popup's, including `number`, which draws the owning pane's index (window_pane_index, which is why WindowSnapshot now carries pane_order too) and keeps the single-line bullet on CELL_NONE. Scenario smoke/pane-border-lines proves every family on an attached client through its straight run, its T where one divider meets another, and its cross where two meet head on. INDICATORS. The acceptance clause called this 'active-pane marking'; the measurement re-scopes it, and the clause is rewritten to what the pin does. pane-border-indicators is two independent switches, not four modes, and neither of them gates the active pane's border colour: redraw_get_pane_for_border_style prefers the active pane whatever the option says. redraw_mark_border_arrows only marks under `arrows` or `both`, and it marks a cell on every side of every pane at xoff + 1 and yoff + 1, after which redraw_draw_border_arrow draws an arrow there only where the active pane owns that cell, pointing at it (left owner is a left arrow, then right, then top, then bottom) - so an arrow lands on a cell the active pane never touched with its own xoff + 1, which is how a 60x16 pin window with the top pane active draws two up arrows on the single divider row. redraw_mark_two_pane_colours only runs under `colour` or `both`, and only for a window with exactly two tiled panes: it hands each half of the single divider to the pane on that side (wy <= w->sy / 2 for a left-right pair, wx <= w->sx / 2 for a top-bottom one) by setting style_wp, which outranks the active pane. Measured on an attached pin client on a 40x12 window with pane-border-style fg=colour196 on the upper pane, fg=colour46 on the lower and pane-active-border-style fg=colour21: `colour` and `both` drew both 38;5;196 and 38;5;21 on the divider row while `off` and `arrows` drew only 38;5;21. Scenario smoke/pane-border-indicators crosses the two switches on attached clients on both binaries, reading the divider owner as a glyph through pane-border-lines number so no colour encoding has to match. Z ORDER. presentation:border-style-owner-z-order closes with them. w->z_index is a second pane order that MuxSnapshot now carries as pane_z_order: window_add_pane appends every tiled pane to its tail however the split ordered w->panes, join-pane inserts the moved pane right after (or before) its destination in both lists, swap-pane exchanges the two positions in both, break-pane puts the pane at the head of its new window, and layout_parse rebuilds the whole list from the layout tree, which is what makes select-layout with a serialized layout reorder it while the named presets do not touch it at all. mux-model maintains exactly those five moves. redraw_build_scene walks the list with TAILQ_FOREACH_REVERSE and each pane overwrites the side it owns, so the pane earliest in z_index wins, and the raw TUI's BorderOwners::mark now ranks by that order instead of by the lowest PaneId, falling back to the lowest PaneId only when two panes share a rank. The tie is narrower than it looks: a border cell has one pane on each side, so the only cells where two panes claim the same side are the junctions, where the inclusive column and row ranges of two neighbours overlap. Scenario smoke/pane-border-zorder builds that junction, locates it by its up tee under `single` and reads the owner's index off the same cell under `number`: created in place the junction goes to the middle row's own pane, and it still does after join-pane moves the oldest pane on the server in beside it, where the lowest-PaneId rule gave it to the joined pane instead (verified by reverting the rank and watching the scenario diverge, want=1 got=2). RESIDUES AND DIVERGENCES. (1) Scope. pane-border-status and pane-border-lines are window-and-pane options in the catalog, but a tiled pane never reads the pane copy: window_get_pane_status reads w->options and window_pane_get_pane_lines reads wp->window->options unless the pane is floating, so `set -p pane-border-status` and `set -p pane-border-lines` are stored, show in show-options, and change nothing on a tiled pane. zz resolves both at window scope for the same reason. pane-border-format is different: window_make_pane_status reads options_get_string(wp->options, ...), so its pane scope is live and zz resolves it per pane. (2) top-floating and bottom-floating fold to off. window_get_pane_status maps both to PANE_STATUS_OFF for every tiled pane, so they carve no row and draw none; measured on the pin (80x12 at 0,0 and 80x11 at 0,13, unchanged from off) and carried in the scenario. PaneBorderStatus on the wire is the folded three-value form. (3) The raw TUI reserves a row for every pane whatever the option says, because its own pane header lives there. pane-border-status therefore moves that row and changes what it draws rather than creating or destroying it, and the client's pane rects are not cell-comparable with the pin's anyway (a sidebar of about 29 columns and two rows of chrome). The comparable geometry is the daemon's, and that is proved exactly. (4) Native GPUI chrome stays theme-owned by the same product decision options.theme-palette takes: none of the four options reach it. (5) The non-colour half of a border style is still dropped on the way to a client; that is presentation:renderer-style-residue, closed under this group on 2026-09-02 as a written list. (6) zz's raw TUI writes Unicode box glyphs whatever the client's locale says, while the pin writes ACS through tty_acs and only translates to UTF-8 for a UTF-8 client, so the four scenarios attach their clients with LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 to compare glyphs at all; that belongs with the terminal capability work, not here.

closed.title: Consume pane chrome options
closed.resolution: The eleven items split by which side of the model they fall on instead of sharing one basket. The four scrollbar options went to `options.native-pane-scrollbars` as native: the pin's scrollbar is made of pane cells and takes a column off every pane, measured as 40x24 and 39x24 becoming 39x24 and 38x24 on an 80x24 horizontal split, and its style option prescribes a cell width and cell padding, while zz's scrollbar is GPUI chrome outside the grid drawn from the terminal worker's published scrollbar state. `known-pane-scrollbar-columns` keeps that difference measured. The remaining seven went to `options.pane-border-chrome` parked, with the pin's border-status geometry measured into that group's reason, a per-client recipe that puts border lines, indicators, and the status row in the raw TUI while native GPUI chrome stays theme-owned, and a `pane-colours` recipe that needs no new engine primitive because libghostty already takes a 256-entry default palette through the appearance the daemon publishes per pane. The two presentation items keep their earlier meanings and are now written down: mutable tiled z-order transport for the border-style owner, which will carry a protocol bump, and the non-colour half of the appearance bridge for the renderer residue. Nothing wire-reachable changed.

closed.title: Consume the pane VT engine knobs
closed.resolution: The four knobs libghostty can be steered into now reach their pane's terminal through the same effect path allow-passthrough and wrap-search use, and the four that need a primitive libghostty does not have moved to options.terminal-engine-limits. MuxEffect::TerminalKnobsChanged carries an EngineKnobs value per pane at effective scope; a byte filter ahead of vt_write rewrites the erase, drops the alternate-screen mode switches, and takes ESC k off the wire; encode_key and the pty's termios carry the backspace key. Measured against the pin on 2026-09-02 with detached panes on both binaries. scroll-on-clear: screen_write_clearscreen hands a full-screen erase to grid_view_clear_history, which scrolls one line per row up to the last row holding a written cell, so twelve lines fed into a pane survive `ESC[H ESC[2J` with the option on and the four on screen are gone with it off; screen_write_clearendofscreen takes the same branch only with the cursor at the origin, and a blank screen finds no used row and scrolls nothing. zz emits `ESC[<used>S` ahead of the erase, which libghostty pushes into scrollback with the cursor left alone, measured in-crate before the rewrite was written. alternate-screen: screen_write_alternateon and screen_write_alternateoff return before touching the screen when the option is off, so 1049, 1047 and 47 all become no-ops in both directions and a pane keeps printing on the primary grid; zz drops those numbers out of the private mode list and keeps the rest of the list, so `ESC[?1049;2004h` still arms bracketed paste. allow-rename: input_exit_rename ignores the collected string unless the option is on, an empty string removes the window's own automatic-rename entry instead of setting a name, and the bytes never reach the screen either way. input.c's rename table (measured at the 2026-09-02 gate review on the pin: `ESC k ESCCSI ESC [0m` renames to ESCCSI, `ESC k CAN 0x18` to CAN, `ESC k A BEL B ST` to AB) drops every C0 byte but its terminators, and every exit from the state runs input_exit_rename, so BEL never joins the name while ESC, CAN and SUB all commit it; zz's filter now follows that table, consumes the sequence unconditionally, and raises a rename event the daemon runs through set-option and rename-window with their after-command hooks suppressed, because input_exit_rename writes the name with window_set_name and the pin fires window-renamed but never after-rename-window (both asserted in smoke/pane-engine-knobs-input, 24 checks). The filter itself was restructured at the gate so a chunk with neither rewrite point reaches vt_write in one span and only a sequence that straddles two chunks is buffered; an ESC inside an unfinished CSI now reaches the engine, which aborts the sequence the way the pin does. Release-build measurement on a 200x50 terminal, three rounds each, PassthroughFilter alone against feed_pty_output: 26MB of coloured ls-style output 73ms to 85ms, 26MB of plain text 30ms to 37ms, and 75k `ESC[H ESC[2J` frames 0.21s to 4.7s, which is the remaining cost of this close: about 60us per full-screen erase of an empty primary screen, spent finding the last used row cell by cell because libghostty exposes no per-row used count; the alternate screen and any erase that is not the whole screen pay nothing. One edge stays: under a DECSTBM region the pin's grid_view_clear_history ignores the region and pushes the used rows into history, while zz's `ESC[nS` scrolls only the region and libghostty discards the rows. backspace: input_key writes one byte for an unmodified BSpace, `C-?` giving 0x7f, `C-h` 0x08, `C-w` 0x17, `Space` 0x20 and `0x41` the letter A, while spawn.c's VERASE keeps only a key code below 0x7f, so the `0x08` spelling reaches the child's stty as ^H but `C-h` and `0x41` both land on ^? because their key codes carry a modifier or literal flag. That split contradicted this group's own reason, which had said spawn.c forces VERASE to the same key; zz now derives the two bytes separately. compat/scenarios/smoke/pane-engine-knobs.txt runs 26 checks and smoke/pane-engine-knobs-input.txt 19 on both binaries. Both count markers in capture-pane rather than reading `#{history_size}` or `#{alternate_on}`, which are still pinned to their inactive values on zz under formats.terminal-runtime, and because a detached pane's terminal has a different row count on the two engines. Two edges stay: `backspace BSpace` writes a truncated key code on the pin and nothing on zz, and an ESC k with an empty name only removes the window's automatic-rename override, so the pin's extra window_set_name when automatic-rename is globally off is not reproduced.

closed.title: Render remain-on-exit-format in retained panes
closed.resolution: The group's reason had said terminal core has no post-worker VT injection seam, which the measurement refined rather than refuted: the Terminal lives on the pane worker's stack and is dropped the moment that worker returns, so there is no VT to inject into after the exit, and the daemon cannot expand the template before the exit because #{pane_dead_status} and #{pane_dead_signal} only exist once the mux has marked the pane dead. The fix is a bounded handshake rather than a second owner: the worker publishes the exited status, then waits up to five seconds (DEAD_NOTICE_WAIT in session.rs) on its own command channel for one dead-notice command before returning, and the daemon sends it from the retained branch of close_exited_terminal, right after mark_pane_dead_with_hooks, expanding the raw template through the same pane-scoped format context style values use. Nothing blocks on that wait: the daemon has already seen the exited status, so only the worker thread lingers. The wait has one rule that took a corpus run to find. A worker that stops serving its command channel while it waits strands whatever arrives there, and the daemon's own retained-pane paths lean on that channel disconnecting: capture-pane on a dead pane tries a live capture first and only falls back to the frozen frame on an actor-stopped answer. Waiting on one receive and returning on anything else made a concurrent capture-pane end the wait, so the notice never landed for two of the five windows in the scenario under corpus load. The wait now runs to its deadline and drops every command that is not the notice: dropping one drops its reply channel, which is the same actor-stopped answer the caller would have got a moment later, so every fallback still fires. Read against the pin on 2026-09-02: server_destroy_pane draws only when the pane is retained and the template is not empty, and it resets the scroll region with screen_write_scrollregion(0, sy - 1), parks the cursor at column zero of the last row, linefeeds once so the screen scrolls, hands the expanded text to format_draw with the pane width as the available width so it is clipped rather than wrapped, and clears MODE_CURSOR. zz writes the same sequence, `ESC[r`, `ESC[<rows>;1H`, a linefeed, the text clipped to the pane's own column count by codepoint width, and `ESC[?25l`. Measured on a 40x6 pane on both binaries: `exit 7` drew `DEADFMT[7][]`, `kill -TERM $$` drew `DEADFMT[][term]`, `exit 0` drew `DEADFMT[0][]`, an empty template left the pane's own `MARKER` output untouched, `remain-on-exit failed` retained and drew for `exit 5` and closed the window for `exit 0`, and `remain-on-exit off` closed it too. compat/scenarios/smoke/remain-on-exit-format.txt asserts those eight facts on both binaries. It reads only the visible rows and never counts them, because a detached pane's terminal has a different row and column count on the two engines: the pin clipped the default template at the 40-column pane width while zz's detached terminal is wider and wrapped it, which is the same geometry divergence the pane-engine-knobs scenarios route around, not a divergence in this draw. Gate fixes 2026-09-02: server_destroy_pane expands with format_single and draws with format_draw, so `#[bold]X#(echo SHELL)Y` draws XY in bold on the pin (capture-pane -pe answers `^[[1mXY^[[0m`) while the first cut drew the template's `#[bold]` and `#()` text literally; the daemon now expands a template carrying `#(` too (the job-less format_single answers nothing for it), parses the styled segments and hands the worker one SGR run per segment, which the worker's clip passes through without counting, and the scenario asserts the drawn text and the bold parameter ahead of it (10 checks). An empty template now hides the cursor the way `wp->base.mode &= ~MODE_CURSOR` does regardless of the template, without the linefeed that the non-empty guard skips. The worker's dead-notice wait is five seconds, not the 250ms an earlier record said. Cycle-9 gate fix 2026-09-02: the notice's own linefeed scrolls the child's last output row into scrollback, and that regressed capture-pane on a retained pane. zz answered a dead pane's capture out of the published visible viewport (capture_frozen_frame over latest_viewport), whose only rows are the visible ones, so a negative -S clamped to visible row 0 and the scrolled-off row was unreachable: new-session-environment and pane-spawn-options both went from clean to two OUT divergences each, on `capture-pane -p -S -1 -E -1` steps that the pin answers with the child's `last` output. A retained pane keeps its whole `struct screen` on the pin, so the worker now freezes the entire grid, scrollback included, on its way out: after the notice draw it captures a ModeRevision (the same grid copy copy mode takes) and publishes it beside the viewport, and capture_frozen_frame resolves -S/-E against that history exactly the way a live capture resolves them, with the visible screen starting at the revision's maximum offset. The freeze is gated on the notice text the daemon's retained branch sends, so a closing pane, which gets None to release the same wait and is never captured after its worker returns, does not pay for a grid copy that can reach 128 MiB. Measured on the pin, 40x6, ten lines then `exit 2` with the notice on: `capture-pane -p` answers L07..L10, a blank and the notice, and `capture-pane -p -S -` answers L01..L10, a blank and the notice, so the six rows the screen no longer holds are still there. Three checks in the scenario assert that on both binaries with thirty lines (13 checks now): the whole blank-stripped history is L01..L30 plus the notice, the visible capture holds neither L01 nor L08, and the full capture holds both. Thirty rather than ten because of a divergence measured beside this one and recorded in knowledge/tmux/divergences.md: `new-session -d -x 40 -y 6` gives the pin a six-row pty (`tput lines` answers 6) while zz spawns the pane's pty at 24 rows and only its mux geometry says 6, so both engines report pane_height 6 and #{pane_width}x#{pane_height} stays clean while their screens hold different numbers of rows. That is the same geometry divergence this scenario's visible-row reads already route around; it is not in this group's contract and nothing here closes on it. One more retained-pane fact is recorded rather than closed: the frozen grid answers capture-pane only. TerminalSession::history on a retained pane still fails with ActorStopped because the worker that served history requests has returned, so a GUI client scrolling a dead pane's scrollback gets nothing even though capture-pane now reaches it; that request path belongs to the terminal engine (crates/zz-terminal/src/session.rs), the same lane as the freeze, and is open work beside this group. Instrument correction, 2026-09-05: smoke/remain-on-exit-format previously required the literal DEADFMT[][term] on both platforms. The Linux pin instead draws DEADFMT[][15] because sig2name falls back to a decimal number without HAVE_SYS_SIGNAME; zz still draws term. The notice-rendering and history checks remain, and the fixture now asserts the platform-derived pin spelling plus the explicitly named zz difference. Signal spelling remains open as formats.dead-signal-platform-name.

closed.title: List hooks through show-options -H
closed.resolution: With `-H`, `show-options` augments only no-positional listings with hook arrays in the pin's final option-table block and hook declaration order. Plain listings exclude hooks, named hook queries work without `-H`, server scope has none, and global-session, global-window, and inherited pane listings expose 57, 11, and 7 hooks. Empty, populated, indexed, named, value-only, pane-fallback, and whole-array-shadowing shapes match the pin, including the inherited empty array's `name*` in a full listing and bare `name` in a named query. `show-window-options` retains its surface without `-H`.

closed.title: Consume terminal behavior options
closed.resolution: All eighteen options now carry an explicit decision instead of sitting in one undifferentiated basket. Seven went to `options.client-terminal-negotiation` as native: terminal-features, terminal-overrides, user-keys, extended-keys, and extended-keys-format all exist to rewrite or query a terminfo entry for a client terminal that zz's daemon never opens, xterm-keys is marked `no longer used` in the pin's own options table, and assume-paste-time is a heuristic the pin itself disables on any terminal reporting bracketed paste, which is every zz client. Eight went to `options.pane-engine-knobs` parked: allow-rename, alternate-screen, scroll-on-clear, backspace, get-clipboard, codepoint-widths, variation-selector-always-wide, and input-buffer-size each need a per-pane knob channel, and half of them additionally need a libghostty primitive that does not exist, with the pinned behavior for each measured into that group's reason on 2026-09-01. Two went to `options.client-attach-and-focus` parked: default-client-command and focus-follows-mouse are ordinary client work blocked only on option values reaching the client. `editor` went to `pane.floating-model`, which already owns the floating-pane stance its only pin-side read depends on, and whose startup seeding zz already reproduces exactly. Three tests derived from those pin measurements now hold the classification honest: zz-terminal proves `send-keys BSpace` writes the pin's default 0x7f and that clearing the whole screen leaves history alone, which is the pin's scroll-on-clear off case and the parked divergence, and zz-tui proves a bracketed-paste run carrying 0x02 arrives as one Paste rather than as a C-b key, which is the case the pin's own assume-paste-time guard skips. Nothing wire-reachable changed.

closed.title: Consume window-status-separator in status rows
closed.resolution: The daemon expands `window-status-separator` after each nonfinal item in the `status-format[]` window loop. It resolves the separator in that window's option and format context, including per-window overrides, nested formats, and style directives; the last item emits no separator. The TUI owns exact tmux row output. The native GUI derives its window controls from snapshot state and does not paint this separator.

closed.title: Complete two-phase pane command completion
closed.resolution: split-window -W is a real flag now. catalog.rs promotes it out of unsupported_flag (the supported/unsupported pair moves 467/36 to 468/35 and zz's own usage gains W), the mux emits MuxEffect::PaneWaitForExit for it beside PaneCreated, and the daemon parks the invoking Command or Control thread on that pane between the raw execution and the after-split-window hook, which is where cmd_split_window_exec parks: the hook is already inserted after the item, so the pin runs it after the wait and so does zz, for any status: window_pane_wait_finish only sets c->retval, so the daemon picks the after hook from the unchanged execution and converts a non-zero status for an unattached client only after the hook ran. Measured 2026-09-02 on both binaries and pinned in smoke/split-window-wait: `set-hook -g after-split-window 'display-message -p HOOK'; split-window -d -P -W 'exit 2' ; display-message -p AFTER` prints the pane, HOOK and AFTER and exits 2, and a command-error hook stays silent. The waiter entry is removed by the parked invoker alone; the PanesRemoved arm only wakes it, because removing it there let a child that exited before the invoker read the channel answer 0 (measured: 6 of 80 instant `exit 7` runs answered 0 with the removal, 0 of 80 without). The waiter lives in ServerState.pane_exit_waiters (new_wp->wait_item) and close_exited_terminal wakes it with the child's status before retention or removal, the way server_child_exited calls window_pane_wait_finish before window_pane_destroy_ready; a pane removed some other way wakes it with 0 the way window_pane_destroy does. The status is WEXITSTATUS, or WTERMSIG plus 128, and it only becomes the client's exit status when that client has no session, which is window_pane_wait_finish's own `c->session == NULL` guard. One divergence stays and is deliberate: only a Command or Control invoker parks. An Interactive client's commands run on the daemon thread that would deliver the wake, so parking it would deadlock the client that has to keep drawing; the pin parks any client's queue. This is the same line every existing overlay wait draws (display-popup, display-menu, confirm-before, command-prompt, display-panes) and the GUI has no queue a user can observe the way a script can. The wait is registered under the same lock that creates the pane, so a child that has already exited by the time the invoking command returns left its status in the channel instead of racing it -- measured: with the registration done afterwards instead, `-W 'exit 3'` answered 0 under corpus load while the pin answered 3. A parked wait also gives up if the queue that owns it is freed, so a client that dies with a live pane cannot strand the worker. Measured on tmux d77c9dc6 and reproduced in smoke/split-window-wait: `split-window -d -W -t =s: 'exit 3'` answers 3 with empty channels, `-W true` answers 0, `-W 'kill -TERM $$'` answers 143, `-P -F '#{pane_index}' -W 'exit 5'` prints 1 and answers 5, `split-window -d -W 'sleep 1; touch M' ; display-message -p AFTER` prints AFTER with M already present, and while a `-W 'sleep 1'` item is parked the client has not returned and the pane is still there, which is the detached-client shape. Every -W pane is gone at the end because remain-on-exit is off. RE-SCOPED: the first acceptance clause read `A bounded two-phase command lifecycle closes a successful Control guard as soon as split-window -W creates its pane, then parks later items from that command queue until the pane exits.` The parking half is what landed. The guard half is not a -W fact at all: cmdq_fire_command prints `%end` for any command whose exec returns CMD_RETURN_WAIT, so on the pin a blocking `run-shell` closes its guard immediately too, while zz's control guard is the client's own request frame and closes when the response arrives. Measured on 2026-09-02: `printf "run-shell 'sleep 2; touch M'\n" | tmux -C attach-session` prints %begin/%end and exits with M landing seconds later, and zz now matches that only because the client releases a parked request at end of file (control-mode.disconnect-cancels-command-queue). A live Control client still sees zz's guard close late for every parking command, -W included. One more Control-only line beside it: a Control client at end of file parked on `-W` sees one extra %layout-change between its empty guard and %exit on zz, where the pin's CONTROL_SHOULD_NOTIFY_CLIENT drops notifications once CLIENT_EXIT is set. That is one divergence, it belongs to the control guard rather than to this flag, and it is recorded here and in that group's closure rather than left implied. The clause now names what -W owns. STILL OPEN, recorded here and in control-mode.disconnect-cancels-command-queue's closure: the display-panes template residue. cmd_display_panes_key inserts the chosen template after the issuing item with cmdq_get_state(item), so `display-panes -t C -d 0 'display-message -p "chose %%%"'` prints `chose %1` on the invoking CLI's stdout and a failing template exits 1 with its message on that CLI's stderr; zz runs the template through submit_template with the interactive client that pressed the key, so the CLI still sees nothing at exit 0. The pieces it needs now exist -- DisplayPanesSession.waiter already parks a Command or Control invoker, and the per-connection worker this cycle added means the invoker is no longer the connection reader -- so what is left is carrying the invoker's (client, kind) on the overlay, running the template in that context in select_display_pane, and widening the waiter's channel from () to the template's output and status. smoke/display-panes-template's failing-template case still says its exit status is not asserted, which is the same residue seen from the other side.

closed.title: Model pane selection controls
closed.resolution: select-pane -m, -M, -d, -e, -g, and -P are promoted out of the unsupported catalog and the four marked formats now read live state. Measured on the pin with a throwaway server: the mark is one server-global tuple (server.c server_set_marked and cmd_find_valid_state), so `-m` on a second pane moves it, `-m` on the pane that already holds it clears it through server_is_marked, `-M` clears whatever holds it, and killing the marked pane drops it in window_lost_pane. `pane_marked` is 1 only on the holder, `pane_marked_set` is 1 server-wide while any mark exists, `session_marked` and `window_marked_flag` are 1 only for the owning session and window, and window_printable_flags emits M between the `-` last-window flag and `Z`, so a marked zoomed current window reads `*MZ`. `-m` refuses a pane hidden by zoom (window_pane_is_visible) while `-M` still clears through the same target. zz models one window per session, so the pin's four-part find state collapses to the session and window the mark was taken in plus the pane, and validity is checked on read the way server_check_marked defers to cmd_find_valid_state, which walks marked_pane.s->windows for marked_pane.wl and ends at window_has_pane: break-pane and join-pane move the marked pane into another window and drop the mark, a swap inside the same window keeps it and follows the new index, move-window and swap-window keep it inside one session because server_link_window and cmd_swap_window_exec retarget marked_pane.wl, and both drop it across sessions because neither retargets marked_pane.s. Measured on the pin, `move-window -d -s w:0 -t other:5` and `swap-window -d -s w:1 -t other:1` leave the moved window's pane reading `0:0:0:0` for pane_marked, pane_marked_set, session_marked, and window_marked_flag, which a zz-mux test and the `pane-selection-marked` differential both carry. cmd_select_pane_exec order is reproduced: `-l` first (routing -e and -d at the last pane), then -m/-M, then -P, then -g, then the directional search, then -e before -d, then -T, then the selection. `-P` writes the pane-local window-style and window-active-style with options_set_string, which never validates, so `select-pane -P bogus=zzz` stores the raw string and exits 0 where `set-option -p window-style bogus=zzz` answers `invalid style: bogus=zzz` and exits 1; the deprecated `-g` prints the pane's effective window-style and returns before selection, while a bare `-P` falls through and selects. Input-off enforcement already lived in the daemon input path (resolve_input_sinks), so -d and -e only needed the mux state they toggle.

closed.title: Complete split-window placement flags
closed.resolution: -k and -m are promoted out of the unsupported catalog. Measured on the pin, both write remain-on-exit `key` on the new pane's own option table and touch nothing wider: the window and global scopes stay unset, so a plain sibling split still dies while the flagged pane is retained after a clean or failing child exit. -m additionally stores its argument as that pane's remain-on-exit-format, raw and unexpanded, and -k alone leaves that format unset. Both spellings keep the pin's arity, so a bare -m answers `command split-window: -m expects an argument` and exits 1, and `split-window -?` now prints the pin's usage byte for byte. The retention decision and the key dismissal both reuse the existing paths unchanged: RemainOnExit::Key already retains every exit in retain_exited_pane, and the daemon consults dead_pane_dismisses_on_key only from the key handler, so mouse and paste input cannot dismiss a retained pane while the next key kills it. -W stays loudly unsupported under pane.command-completion; it enters the pin's floating two-phase path and blocks the command queue, which is why no scenario exercises it.

closed.title: Style pane borders per adjacent span
closed.resolution: Raw zz-tui styles each shared divider per adjacent pane span instead of per full segment. In an A|(B/C) split with C active, the A/B span renders inactive, while the junction cell and the A/C span render with the active style; directional fallback resolves top, bottom, left, then right. Aligned same-side ties from splits resolve by PaneId creation order. The 10-step LC_ALL=C strict differential proves the red upper span with green junction, horizontal, and lower spans against pinned tmux with zero divergence, and the exact base fails its renderer marker row, so the coverage discriminates. This closure is bounded: same-side ties after join-pane, swap-pane, or serialized select-layout stay open under presentation:border-style-owner-z-order, and tiled z-order transport belongs to the pane-border z-order contract.

closed.title: Complete command-prompt semantics
closed.resolution: The last four items closed on 2026-09-02, and the piece that unlocked them is that zz's TUI was editing the prompt itself for text modes and only relaying keys for -1, -N and -k. The pin has no such split: status_prompt_key owns the buffer, the cursor, the history and the key table, and the client only renders. The TUI now relays every prompt key on the pane key path, which deleted its local editor and made the daemon's prompt_key the single implementation; smoke/command-prompt-target and smoke/command-prompt-chain still pass unchanged through it. option:status-keys and semantic:command-prompt-vi-editing: CommandPrompt gained pr->keys, PROMPT_COMMANDMODE and pr->word_separators, filled once at creation the way prompt_set_options fills them from the raising session, through a new MuxEngine::prompt_key_options beside scalar_option_effective. word-separators is not in the scalar option store, it has its own global_word_separators and session_word_separators pair, and the first cut read the scalar table and silently got an empty separator set that made every motion behave like its big-letter variant, which is why the accessor reads word_separators_for_session. prompt_translate_key is implemented whole: insert mode passes its fixed list of control keys and the cursor keys to the emacs handler, takes Escape or C-[ into command mode with the index stepped back, and appends everything else (a control chord it does not name is dropped, because append_key can only take a key that fits in one character); command mode maps BSpace to Left, A/I/C/s/a and S and i out of command mode, and the rest onto emacs keys and the KEYC_VI word motions. The three word motions were rewritten from whitespace-only scans to prompt_forward_word, prompt_end_word and prompt_backward_word, which classify each character as space, separator or word and stop at the class change, with the vi variants skipping to the start of the next word and the big-letter ones passing no separators at all; C-w now deletes exactly the span prompt_backward_word would move over, and C-Left, C-Right, M-b and M-f share the same code, so emacs word motions also gained the separators they did not have. semantic:command-prompt-key-spelling: a -k prompt now answers with key_string_lookup_key's spelling rather than the typed text. Space and BTab are the two names input_key_name never emits, so prompt_key_spelling adds them, reusing the menu's own shifted-Tab-is-BTab rule; 0x08 stopped being folded into Backspace in the TUI's legacy control-byte decoder, so it decodes as C-h the way the pin's key table names it, and only 0x7f is BSpace. The zz-only residue beside it went with the relay: C-c and C-g were already mapped to Close in command_prompt_edit_key and the TUI was swallowing them, so all three of Escape, C-c and C-g close a prompt now. semantic:prompt-message-freeze needed no code: measured against the pin with a -b prompt seeded ab and a display-message from a command client, both binaries already agree. A plain -d 5000 message leaves the buffer alone and cd plus Enter answers abcd, -N -d 1500 eats every key for the delay so an XY typed inside the window is lost and the later cd still answers abcd, and -d 0 splits on what came before it: status_message_set assigns message_ignore_keys only when the delay is non-zero, so a standalone -d 0 message on a fresh client clears on the next key and that key reaches the prompt (cd plus Enter answers abcd on both binaries, re-probed at the gate with a real pty client), while a -d 0 message issued after the -N -d 1500 one inherits message_ignore_keys, never clears, and the parked prompt never closes on either binary, which is the prompt-never-closed row the fixture asserts identically on both sides. That last pair is the case the earlier reason left unclaimed. Differential coverage for all four is smoke/command-prompt-editing, 39 checks on one real pty client per side: fifteen -k spellings, nineteen editing answers across vi and emacs with a custom and the default word-separators, the two close keys, and the three message cases. Two findings. First, pinned tmux d77c9dc6 has a heap overread in prompt_key: the KEYC_DC and C-d branch copies (size + 1 - index) entries from buffer + index + 1, one entry past the buffer, and a vi command-mode x at index 3 of a four-character buffer killed the pinned server outright and took the probe with it. The differential deliberately never presses Delete inside a prompt. Second, zz still has no C-y (prompt_paste), no C-t (transpose) and no C-v (quote-next), so those three emacs chords and the vi p that maps onto C-y are no-ops rather than edits, and CommandPromptState carries no command-mode flag, so the pin's separate command cursor style is not rendered. Neither is one of these four items; both belong to whoever takes the prompt's remaining rendering and yank work. The vi table, word-separators and the C-c/C-g close reach the raw TUI client, which is the compat surface; the GUI palette in crates/zz/src/command/palette.rs still edits locally and sends CommandPromptAction::Update, and the TUI paste path edits locally too, so those two keep their own affordance until a client-lane slice hands the palette the same key relay.

closed.title: Keep the prompt on the client surface, -P included
closed.resolution: The old clause read: "Native client prompt surfaces keep the prompt contract, and `command-prompt -P` stays loudly unsupported rather than being accepted as a no-op", on the grounds that "painting a prompt into pane cells would mean the daemon writing another client's grid, so the flag stays loudly unsupported". The cost of that stance was measured and is the reason it changed: the one flag was the whole difference between zz's and the pin's rendered commands for fourteen stock bindings, vi `/`, `?`, `:`, `f`, `F`, `t`, `T` and emacs `g`, `C-r`, `C-s`, `f`, `F`, `t`, `T`. The pin's -P was measured on 2026-09-02 on a throwaway server with one attached 80x24 pty client. cmd-command-prompt.c reads `args_has(args, 'P')` once: with it the prompt belongs to the target pane (`window_pane_set_prompt`) instead of to the client, and a second -P on a pane that already has a prompt returns CMD_RETURN_NORMAL without opening anything, the same refusal the flag-less form makes when the client already has one. The template is prepared by `args_make_commands_prepare` before that branch is taken and the same callback runs it, so -P changes where the prompt is drawn and which object owns it, and nothing about the answer. screen-redraw.c `redraw_draw_pane_prompt` draws it at redraw time on the pane's last row (`wp->yoff + wp->sy - 1`), or on its first row when `status-position` is top, across the whole pane width, through `tty_draw_line`. That is an overlay and not a write into the pane: measured with `command-prompt -P -p '(pane prompt)'` up, the attached client's byte stream carries `(pane prompt) ` painted in the message style on screen row 23, while `capture-pane -p` of that pane answers an empty row, and a one-row pane made by `split-window -l 1` still gets the prompt drawn on its single row. A pane whose prompt row is outside the client's visible offset is simply not drawn. No format reports the prompt either way: `#{command_prompt}`, `#{prompt_input}`, `#{prompt_type}` and `#{prompt_flags}` all answer empty from `display-message -p` with a -P prompt up and with a status prompt up, because prompt.c `prompt_expand` is the prompt's own expansion context and not the format tree, which is the stance `formats.native-typed-context-producers` already carries; and `#{client_key_table}` answers `root` throughout. New stance, decided 2026-09-02 by the orchestrator under fabrico's instruction to close the campaign; reversible: the prompt contract is the client surface, and the pane-cell placement is presentation zz does not copy. `-P` is a real catalog flag now, accepted and ignored by the daemon, which raises exactly the prompt it raises without it: the raw TUI's message line and the GPUI client's native prompt. The daemon still never writes another client's grid, which is what the old reason was actually protecting. The fourteen stock bindings carry the pin's exact command strings, `command-prompt -P`, `-1P` and `-Pi` included, so `list-keys` renders them identically; compat/scenarios/copy-mode-bindings.txt asserts all twenty rows on both binaries and compat/scenarios/smoke/copy-mode-prompt-bindings.txt drives them from a real attached client's keyboard. The catalog counters moved with the promotion: supported 467 to 468, unsupported 36 to 35, and command-prompt left PINNED_TMUX_USAGE_OVERRIDES because its usage now matches the pin, taking the override count from 21 to 20. The item `flag:command-prompt:-P` leaves the registry with the promotion, because a supported catalog flag cannot carry a flag item, so the stance now lives here rather than in an accepted group; reopen it as an accepted-native group if the pane-cell placement is ever wanted. Instrument correction, 2026-09-05: the statement "nothing about the answer" covered the original terminal-copy-mode probe, not retained command output. compat/attached-client.sh probe_command_output_prompt_lifecycle measures the stock / prompt discarding zz command output before either cancellation or submission while the pin preserves it. That behavioral residue is open as clients.command-output-pane-prompt; client-side placement does not justify it.

closed.title: Close bounded geometry reporting gaps
closed.resolution: Closed 2026-09-04 by putting zz's resize loop in the pin's order. The measurement this record was left on stands and was not re-derived: a GUI client floors its pixel box to a grid (crates/zz/src/terminal/element.rs::terminal_grid_size answers 120x24 for a 960x384 box at an 8x16 cell and 119x23 for a 959.5x383.5 one), and that floored report used to reach the pty while #{pane_width} kept the layout's cell, so the two numbers stood one cell apart. The direction an earlier note prescribed, make the format follow the pty, stays refuted: formats.rs fills pane_width, pane_height, pane_left, pane_top, pane_right, pane_bottom and the four pane_at_* flags from one displayed_pane_cell and #{window_layout} encodes the same cells, so moving pane_width alone would leave pane_right off by one from pane_left + pane_width - 1 and pane_at_right wrong. The pin never has that incoherence because window_pane_resize moves the layout cell, the pane's screen and the pty together. Measured again on pinned tmux d77c9dc6 with throwaway -f /dev/null servers: on a 199x49 window split -h both panes report 99x49, pane_left+pane_width-1 equals pane_right on both (0/98 and 100/198), #{window_layout} encodes 99x49 twice, and both shells' stty size answers 49 99; after resize-window -x 199 -y 49 on a 188/10 split the same shells answer 188 and 10. So the pty was made to follow the settled layout. terminal_geometry_for_mode now takes a GeometrySource: the write-back that back-solves the window extent keeps the owner client's report (ClientReport, because a GUI client reports only per-pane grids and never a tty size, so the back-solve is the only thing that moves the window), and the pty size is re-derived from engine.pane_geometry after that extent has settled (LaidOut), the way the Manual arm always did. Two write-backs that were skipped for non-aggressive windows, the focus-change pass and the detach pass, now always run, and refresh_terminal_visibility writes back too, because it is where visible_terminals changes and under the new order a pane whose owner moved without the layout following would report one size and run at another; the aggressive_only parameter is gone, the owner set already being what aggressive-resize decides, and a write-back that moves a layout there publishes the mux snapshot through a new non-recursive publish_mux_snapshots. The one-cell guard was not removed: implied_window_extent scales a pane report up to a window extent, so a one-cell drift on a ten-column pane of a two-hundred-column window would move the whole window by twenty, still pinned at 8 -> 160x50. Instead the back-solve is now per axis. On an axis the pane spans in full the inverse is exact, the report plus the border row layout_add_horizontal_border carves out; only an axis the pane shares with siblings keeps the guard. An unsplit window, which is the attached GUI case this item names, is therefore exact on both axes, and window_extent_for_pane_geometry shares the same helper so the two back-solves cannot drift apart. Proofs at the tip: zz-daemon's a_floored_client_measurement_sizes_the_pty_from_the_pane_it_reports drives a real Interactive client's ResizeTerminal reports through the daemon and pins the floored 119x23 reaching the pty (wait_for_terminal_dimensions) and #{pane_width}x#{pane_height} together with the whole family, '119x23 0,0 118,22 1111 119x23', then splits -l 10 and pins that a nine-column report on the ten-column pane leaves both the format and the pty at the layout's 10x23 with '10x23 109,0 118,22 0111 119x23' and #{window_layout} encoding 108x23 and 10x23, and that the left pane's stale 119-column report no longer reaches its pty; crates/zz-mux/tests/attached_pane_width.rs keeps both earlier tests, the unsplit one re-pinned to the exact path (199x49 report -> 199x49 pane, window and layout) and the narrow-pane one unchanged as the anti-amplification floor, and adds the per-axis case where a nine-column report on a ten-column pane is swallowed while the spanned height is taken exactly; crates/zz/src/workspace/view.rs::attached_pane_measurement_floors_below_the_laid_out_box is untouched and still pins the GUI measurement itself. split-window-zoom, manual-window-size-transition and split-window-zoom-hidden-width run clean under --strict-geometry. The 141x31, 101x21 and 73x19 attached-client rows were proved by running probe_attached_client_sizing on its own, not by compat/attached-client.sh, which never reaches that probe on this box: the fixture is already red at origin/main 559fd8a from two failures neither this item nor this branch causes, probe_command_output_navigation on the zz side (the command-output search prompt does not open within ten seconds) and probe_command_prompt on the pin side (the rename prompt does not become prompted, last output mainprompted), both reproduced at that commit with a clean build. The gate does not notice, because compat/results/summary.md still ends with an Attached-client fixture Status: PASS footer that nothing regenerates while the fixture is red, and compat/run.sh --check-summary passes on that stale line. The cycle-13 integration ran the fixture twice at this tip and it failed both times at a different probe (probe_side, then probe_command_output_navigation), so the fixture is unreliable on this box rather than red at one place; it needs an owner of its own and is carried into the cycle-13 handoff as one. What zz still owns, and the pin never does, is back-solving a window extent from a pane report at all; the cell a shared axis swallows now costs one drawn column instead of a disagreement between the format and the pty. One narrower divergence is recorded rather than changed: a Control client's declared per-window geometry still clamps the pty below the layout cell (the ceiling in terminal_geometry_for_mode), which the pin has no concept of, because that ceiling predates this item and no acceptance clause names it.

closed.title: Align new-session cwd edge behavior
closed.resolution: When new-session -A finds an existing session, zz now shares the attach-session retargeting path: it resolves the target first, expands -c exactly once with the invoking client and resolved target session, window, and pane, stores the cwd before terminal preflight, and publishes that mutation even when opening the terminal fails. Clientless calls remain inert, permitted Control clients attach and update the target, and nested Control, attached Interactive, and -A -d calls refuse before target selection, expansion, retargeting, or mutation. Fresh creation and an -A miss now preserve an explicitly empty session cwd while leaving the initial pane cwd unset so the existing donor or caller fallback still applies; omitted -c continues to inherit normally. Focused mux and daemon tests cover single expansion, target isolation, failure ordering, every refusal class, and explicit-empty behavior. The strict 10-step new-session-cwd differential matches the pinned tmux build with zero topology, geometry, format, output, or warning differences.

closed.title: Preserve native default-config argument order
closed.resolution: Runtime source-file no longer special-cases the active zz/mux.conf. At this close, every declared path expanded and matched in caller order, and each match entered the ordinary config loader immediately in glob order, producing DAD for default, after, and default. The later config.replayed-command-output closure changed that immediate replay timing: one invocation now parses all matches in declared and glob order, then replays them in the same order while preserving DAD and path order. A loud miss returns status 1 without preventing later matches from loading; quiet misses remain silent. Ordinary diagnostics and -v lines retain declared path and match order. That later closure also pins presentation as one complete verbose batch, then replay, then buffered command-name and parser diagnostics for each invocation. Source no-match, glob, and actual OS or path read failures retain their existing error channels. Explicit zz-native reload-config still rediscovers the first existing default candidate, replaces #{config_files}, resets key tables, rebuilds appearance, and reapplies stored mux overrides. Startup still discovers the first existing zz-owned candidate, while ordered explicit -f files remain the intentional startup roots. Parse-only and nested source paths keep their existing behavior. Focused CLI and daemon tests, strict daemon clippy, and fmt pass. The strict 12-step source-file-diagnostics and 40-step source-file-format differentials have zero differences and no skips. At this close the source-file-control row had five clean steps; the later nested-queue proof grew the current row to six clean steps. This closure makes no canonical-suite claim.

closed.title: Select the current client cwd for event-hook sources
closed.resolution: Measured against the pin, a deferred event hook has no client to select: cmd_source_file_exec asks server_client_get_cwd with a NULL session, and notify_add appends the hook callback with a NULL client, so every event-hook source resolves against the server's own HOME no matter which client caused the event. zz's sentinel-client event-hook context already lands on the same directory, and the 4-check differential now pins it: session-created raised by a plain client and by a Control client, plus window-linked and pane-exited, each triggered from a client whose cwd holds a decoy leaf, against a session created with a third cwd that holds another decoy, and with a fourth decoy at the repository root. Both sides load the daemon-home leaf in all four cases. The registry's earlier suspicion that zz needed to select a current or best attached client did not reproduce, because the pin never consults one on this path.

closed.title: Complete source-file controls
closed.resolution: source-file now accepts -n, -t, and -v through one mux effect and replay-loader options path. -n parses the whole invocation, retains lexer diagnostics and optional verbose lines, and applies neither parser environment assignments nor commands. At that checkpoint it did not claim whole-file command-name and argument prevalidation. The later config.parser-abort and mux.chain-parse-abort closures added that atomicity. Later shared flag and arity closures match exact diagnostics when each replayed command reaches dispatch. -t resolves a pane target once, preserves the invoking client cwd, supplies that context to -F and replayed commands, and follows CMD_FIND_CANFAIL by loading with an empty target context when lookup fails. -v formats normalized command groups with source and physical line in declared-path and glob order, inherits through nested sources, and stays suppressed for Control clients. The later config.replayed-command-output closure proves that Command and Interactive clients receive one complete verbose batch before that invocation's replay and buffered command-name or parser diagnostics. Source no-match, glob, and actual OS or path read failures retain their existing error channels. It also proves that -n applies no bare assignments across files and produces no replay output. The attached proof first covered transcript presentation and dismissal; the later clients.tui-command-output-navigation closure added interaction inside the TUI output view. The strict source-file-format differential runs 40 steps with no differences, including parse-only state, target and target-based -F context, a missing target, verbose output, and multi-file order. The source-file-control probe proves that Control executes an explicit -v source without leaking verbose lines. Runtime error delivery closed separately under config.replayed-command-errors. At this checkpoint, config alias snapshots, native default-config multi-file ordering, nested Control queueing, sourced-hook cwd, and stdin remained in their explicit groups. The later source-file.default-config-multi-file-order closure removed the default-config residue.

closed.title: Match source-file glob semantics
closed.resolution: Unix source-file matching now uses glob(3) with tmux's cwd quoting, backslash escaping, leading-dot exclusion, nonrecursive repeated stars, malformed-pattern handling, per-pattern ordering, and declared-path diagnostics.

closed.title: Keep the invoking client cwd through nested source replay
closed.resolution: A source-file invocation from any registered real client now snapshots the same daemon-local base chosen for its top-level paths and carries that immutable base through every replay recursion. Relative nested paths use resolve_source_path with the existing cwd glob quoting even after an ordinary sourced command executes through the sentinel replay client and clears the mutable ExecutionContext cwd. At this checkpoint, sourcing the active default zz/mux.conf took the daemon's native reload branch and forwarded the same captured base. The later source-file.default-config-multi-file-order closure removed that runtime special case, so the same file now enters the ordinary source loader with the captured base. Direct zz-native reload-config later gained the same registered-client base under source-file.reload-config-client-cwd; startup remains clientless under source-file.startup-client-cwd. The pinned differential runs an ordinary command before the nested source and supplies a containing-file decoy; the CLI regressions repeat that shape from a caller cwd containing spaces and glob metacharacters, including the then-active default reload branch with a second decoy beside mux.conf. Deferred event hooks retain their sentinel-client gap under source-file.event-hook-client-cwd, and hooks raised by sourced ordinary commands retain their replay-client gap under source-file.sourced-hook-client-cwd. Exact attached session-cwd selection later closed under clients.attach-session-cwd. The later config.replayed-command-output closure preserves successful Command and attached output through this direct recursion as depth-first invocation frames. Parser-owned Control framing closed under control-mode.sourced-command-frames and source-file.nested-control-queue. The later control-mode.indirect-source-frames closure covers synchronous foreground inserted recursion. At this checkpoint immediate-hook and background-callback flags-0 framing remained open under control-mode.hook-command-frames and control-mode.background-inserted-command-frames. Later closures closed both groups. Hook cwd still remains under source-file.sourced-hook-client-cwd.

closed.title: Match nested source-file Control queue semantics
closed.resolution: No production change was required. The existing source loader preflights all declared paths for one parser-owned source-file command before recursing. In a three-level Control replay, the root command therefore publishes its missing-path guard first, the middle command publishes its missing-path guard second, and the leaf publishes its output guard last, each exactly once. The focused nested_source_control_guards_precede_deeper_replay regression passes, the daemon suite passes 601 tests, and the strict six-step source-file-control differential has zero differences and no skips. This close covers parser-owned cross-depth diagnostic and output guard ordering. The later control-mode.source-file-exit-status closure completed Control return-status and detach precedence and grew the focused run to eight clean steps. The stored canonical row remains at three steps. The later control-mode.indirect-source-frames closure carries the Control recipient through synchronous foreground shell-evaluated `if-shell`, immediate `if-shell -F` including `-bF`, and foreground `run-shell -C`. At this checkpoint immediate-hook and background-callback flags-0 framing remained open under control-mode.hook-command-frames and control-mode.background-inserted-command-frames. Later closures closed both groups. Neither focused run makes a canonical-suite claim.

closed.title: Report nested source-file paths as declared
closed.resolution: Nested source-file no-match and glob errors now retain the post-F declared argument; a quiet no-match stays silent. Command clients receive stderr and exit 1, and Interactive clients receive a warning. Protocol v76 puts parser-owned Control no-match and glob diagnostics inside the source command's own flags-1 guard; a hit plus miss ends `%end`, while an all-miss ends `%error`. At this checkpoint matched child actual OS or path read failures used zz's typed standalone Error path, whose internal identity had closed under control-mode.source-diagnostic-typing. The later protocol-v78 control-mode.hook-source-read-diagnostics closure closes the pinned external raw placement and invisible source-completion numbering. Invalid UTF-8 was a zz-side typed error at this checkpoint; config.non-utf8-file-bytes owns the later pinned semantic mismatch. Per-command framing closed under control-mode.sourced-command-frames, and the later source-file.nested-control-queue closure proved cross-depth parser-owned diagnostic ordering. The later control-mode.indirect-source-frames closure covers synchronous foreground inserted sources. Immediate hook and background callback flags-0 framing closed later under control-mode.hook-command-frames and control-mode.background-inserted-command-frames. Registered-client nested cwd rebasing closed separately under source-file.nested-client-cwd, while startup and deferred event-hook base selection remain active.

closed.title: Match source-file nesting limits
closed.resolution: Counting the initial source-file as invocation 1, 50 concurrent source invocations now run and invocation 51 is refused before any of its paths are matched or loaded. Command clients get `too many nested files` on stderr and exit 1, Protocol v76 Control clients get the same lowercase text inside the refused command's own flags-1 `%begin`/`%error` guard while the outer line continues, and attached clients get the pin's capitalized `Too many nested files` status message. `-q` does not suppress it, one diagnostic is emitted per refused command rather than per path, and the containing file keeps running its later lines. The later source-file.nested-control-queue closure proved cross-depth ordering. A malformed invocation at the refused depth is diagnosed as malformed rather than as depth on both sides, because the pin rejects it while parsing the containing file and never consults its depth guard. Later shared arity and flag closures matched that malformed text as well. The later config.parser-abort and mux.chain-parse-abort closures prove that a parser or construction failure drops every command from that file. Same-line removal closed separately under config.same-line-error-group, and cumulative startup accounting closed separately under source-file.startup-depth-accounting.

closed.title: Keep the invoking client cwd through native reload
closed.resolution: A registered client's direct zz-native reload-config now snapshots the same selected source base as source-file and carries it through the default mux.conf replay. A CLI regression runs from a cwd containing spaces and glob metacharacters, places distinct leaf files in the caller cwd and beside mux.conf, clears the earlier sourced state, and proves direct reload selects the caller-root leaf. A daemon regression proves clientless replay still uses the containing-file fallback. The change reuses the v72 ClientHello cwd and existing daemon state without a protocol change. Startup, attached session-cwd selection, deferred event hooks, and hooks raised during sentinel replay retain their separate tracked gaps.

closed.title: Keep the invoking Control client for sourced hooks
closed.resolution: source-file now resolves relative paths against the outer queue client when the running command carries a Control command target, so a hook raised by a Control-sourced command keeps the invoking client's cwd. The working-directory client is selected separately from the replay client, which leaves the hook's replay framing untouched: the 6-check differential drives a Control `source-file` of a config in a subdirectory whose after-display-message hook sources a repo-relative leaf, and both sides load the client-root leaf instead of the containing-file or daemon-home decoy while emitting the same six flags-0 %begin/%end pairs, one SOURCED_HOOK body line, no %error, and a trailing %exit.

closed.title: Bootstrap startup sources from the initial client cwd
closed.resolution: The cold launcher now captures a bounded, valid UTF-8 working directory and passes it through the private --bootstrap-client-cwd daemon argument only when it starts a new daemon. Startup replay temporarily installs that directory as its initial client base, gives it precedence over a session, registered reentry client, command context, HOME, and root fallback, then clears it at the replay boundary on both success and error. Nested relative sources retain that base, paths containing shell metacharacters remain literal, a direct daemon launch has no bootstrap base, and later runtime source-file commands use the registered client's current cwd. CLI and daemon regressions cover bounded capture, priority, nesting, literal path handling, expiration, and cleanup. The isolated startup-client-cwd differential passes exactly on both engines. The complete eight-case startup diagnostic script reaches the new control-mode.exit-pane-output difference after proving cwd selection: zz can emit a queued shell-prompt %output between the flags-0 guard and %exit, while pinned tmux discards it. No public protocol field or version changed. Event-hook cwd, sourced-hook cwd, non-UTF-8 path transport, and top-level config discovery retain their existing owners.

closed.title: Match startup source-file depth accounting
closed.resolution: One startup accounting value now spans every explicit or discovered top-level configuration. The roots do not consume slots; source commands 1 through 50 run, command 51 and later retain the declaring file and line in their cause, quiet misses consume slots, and one command with many paths consumes one slot. Runtime sequential source commands remain unbounded, while the zz-native `reload-config` whole-root replay takes one fresh startup budget of its own so reloading a file lands the same state a fresh start would. Client delivery and placement of retained startup causes remain tracked under config.startup-diagnostic-delivery.

closed.title: Preserve literal source-file tildes
closed.resolution: source-file no longer rewrites a literal leading ~/ after parsing: parser-expanded leading tildes still arrive as absolute paths, top-level literal tildes pass through cwd resolution, and registered-client nested literal tildes use the stable invoking base closed under source-file.nested-client-cwd. Startup and deferred event-hook base selection remain active. The CLI regression pins the top-level choice against a metacharacter-bearing daemon HOME.

closed.title: Scope the exact-match target prefix by slot
closed.resolution: The resolver now records which slot of cmd_find_target a token reached. A session or window slot strips the leading equals sign into an exact-match flag and maps the window alias table; a colon-less token for a pane target lands in the pane slot, so the window and session lookups that run after the pane miss search for it exactly as written, alias table included. Every measured row now matches the pin byte for byte on a throwaway server and a scratch daemon: `set-option -t =w history-limit 1234` answers `no such session: =w` and exits 1, `-t =alp` answers `no such session: =alp` instead of degrading into a session prefix search, `set-option -w -t =win0` answers `no such window: =win0`, `set-option -p -t =w` answers `no such pane: =w`, `kill-pane -t =w` and `select-pane -t =win0` answer `can't find pane:` with the equals sign kept, while `set-option -t =w:` succeeds because the colon moves the token into the session slot, and `set-window-option -t =win0` and `has-session -t =w` succeed because their own target types put it in the window and session slots. The cmd-find diagnostics keep reporting the stripped name (`has-session -t =wi` answers `can't find session: wi`, `kill-window -t =wi` answers `can't find window: wi`) while the option-scope diagnostics echo the raw `-t` argument, because the pin resolves an option target with CMD_FIND_CANFAIL and then lets options_scope_from_flags name the slot the option's own scope needs. That rewrite also fixes three adjacent messages measured the same way: `set-option -t nope`, `-t 9.9`, `-w -t :nope`, and `-p -t :nope` now answer with the pin's exact text. One residue case stays divergent and is not claimed here: the pin's `set-option -t :nope history-limit` succeeds on the retained session while zz still fails, because zz's option target derives its session from a resolved window instead of the componentwise CANFAIL state.

closed.title: Select the send-keys target client
closed.resolution: send-keys -c is a real catalog option and resolves the pin's target client. MuxEffect::TerminalView and MuxEffect::CopyModeRepeat now carry an optional target_client, and the daemon resolves it through the same find_attached_client_with_aliases path the popup and menu commands use, falling back to the invoking client when the flag is absent. The read-only guard moved with it: prepare_command_request and the bound-key preflight in execute_key_commands both ask read_only_guard_client which client cmd-send-keys.c would test, which is the -c client rather than the invoker, and a target that matches nothing leaves no client to test, matching CMD_CLIENT_CFLAG|CMD_CLIENT_CANFAIL. The bound-key half was caught at the cycle-6 gate: key_bindings_dispatch admits a send-keys binding on a read-only client because cmd_send_keys_entry carries CMD_READONLY and cmd_send_keys_exec then tests tc, so on the pin a read-only client pressing `bind-key -n z send-keys -c <writer tty> -t %0 -l K` and `bind-key -n y send-keys -c /dev/pts/nonexistent -t %0 -l N` delivers KN while zz refused both against the invoker's flag; the scenario now drives those two bindings plus an un-flagged `send-keys -t %0 -l U` from the read-only pty client and both binaries land exactly KN. Proved differentially by compat/scenarios/smoke/send-keys-client-selection.txt, which attaches two real pty clients, one read-write and one attached with -r, and runs 21 checks that both binaries answer identically: a resolved read-write client delivers at status 0; the read-only client answers `client is read-only` at status 1 and delivers nothing even though the invoker is an unattached command client; `-c /dev/pts/nonexistent-client` and `-c ''` are quiet at status 0 and still deliver, so the pane holds exactly ACD; the /dev-stripped tty spelling selects the same read-only client; and `-c <read-only> -X cursor-up` is accepted at status 0 because the guard is `tc != NULL && CLIENT_READONLY && !args_has(args, 'X')`, while the same client without -X is refused again. Unsafe -X actions selected onto a read-only client, `-X begin-selection` and `-X copy-pipe`, are refused at status 1 per clients.read-only-local-view-actions, where the pin answers 0 and posts `client is read-only` as a status message on that client because window_copy_command only checks WINDOW_COPY_CMD_FLAG_READONLY inside the mode. One divergence stays open and is recorded rather than closed: with no -c at all the pin runs cmd_find_current_client, which for an unattached command client picks the attached client with the newest activity_time, so a bare `send-keys` can be refused by a read-only peer's flag; zz keeps using the invoking client. That selection is activity-ordered and untestable without a timing race, so the scenario asserts only the -c forms.

closed.title: Complete send-keys injection and mode behavior
closed.resolution: `send-keys -K` is a client-key path, not a pane-write path. The mux emits a new `MuxEffect::SendClientKeys` carrying the `-c` client and the token list (MuxEffect is not wire, so no protocol version moved), and the daemon replays it from the post-lock tail of `execute` through `Shared::input_key` on the selected client, which is the same handler a real key press takes: the client's own key table decides whether the key fires a binding or falls through to the pane that client is looking at. `-K` is promoted from an unsupported catalog flag to a real one (supported and unsupported counters 464/39 -> 465/38, the send-keys usage override becomes `[-FHKlRX] ...` because `-M` stays unsupported), and `ExecutionContext` now carries the invoking key so the no-positional form can replay it, set from `input_key` and from the per-character text path around `execute_key_commands`. Measured on the pin on 2026-09-02 with two 80x24 pty clients on a throwaway server and asserted on both binaries in compat/scenarios/smoke/send-keys-inject.txt, 16 checks: a plain `send-keys -t %0 Z` writes Z into the pane and fires nothing, while `send-keys -c <client> -K Z` fires the client's root binding and leaves the pane untouched; `-N 3 -K Z` fires it three times; `-K -H 5a` fires the same binding because the table lookup masks `KEYC_LITERAL` off; an unbound `-K -l V` reaches the client's own pane; a `-t` naming a pane in another window is ignored entirely, because `cmd_send_keys_inject_key` never reads `wp` under `-K`; an unresolvable `-c` injects nothing and still exits 0; a binding that switches its client's table and then runs `send-keys -K` with no key replays the key that raised it into the new table; `send-keys -N 2 -K` with no key injects nothing at all, because `cmd_send_keys_exec` returns at `if (args_has(args, 'N') || args_has(args, 'R'))` inside its `count == 0` block; and the same Z resolves to the probe binding on a client switched to that table while the other client still answers root. Three facts are recorded rather than closed. `-N n -K` with no key still arms the pane's mode count on the way past, which is the count item this group already closed. The pin queues each injected key on the target client's command queue while zz calls the handler directly, so a binding that injects its own key recurses here where the pin loops on its queue; `MAX_CLIENT_KEY_INJECTION_DEPTH` stops it at 16 rather than overflowing the stack. And a `-H` byte above 0x7f has no `KeyInput` to ride, so `-K -H ff` injects nothing on zz where the pin hands `KEYC_LITERAL|0xff` to the handler; the pane-write form of the same byte is unaffected and stays proved under smoke/send-keys-control. A separate divergence turned up beside this work and belongs to the key-table subsystem, not here: after a key fires from a non-default table the pin resets the client's key table to root (`table after: root`), zz leaves the client parked in the custom table, and zz additionally stops forwarding unbound keys to the pane once a client has been switched to a table explicitly, root included. smoke/send-keys-inject therefore never asserts a table it did not just set, and never asserts a pane write after a switch. On 2026-09-05 keys.table-lifecycle corrected explicit switch-client table lifetime: one-shot dispatch resets before execution, an unbound key retries root and drops on a second miss, and -r retains the table only while repeat-time runs. smoke/keys-table-lifecycle proves these rules with attached clients.

closed.title: Reset terminal input and palette state
closed.resolution: `send-keys -R` is implemented and the catalog flag is promoted. zz composes the pin's `screen_write_reset` out of VT bytes instead of calling libghostty's `reset`, which is RIS and discards history: a bare ST abandons any half-parsed string sequence without printing a cell, an explicit SGR and charset reset restores the pen the way `input_reset_cell` does, DECSTBM drops the scroll region, and because the pinned libghostty (20c3eae0) ignores DECSTR outright (its `CSI p` arm implements only DECRQM and logs `ignoring unimplemented CSI p with intermediates` for `ESC[!p`), every flag the pin's `s->mode = MODE_CURSOR|MODE_WRAP` assignment drops gets its own sequence: DECAWM and DECTCEM come back on, and DECCKM, IRM, DECOM, LNM, DECKPAM, cursor blink, synchronized output, theme updates, the kitty keyboard flags, modifyOtherKeys, and the mouse, focus, and bracketed-paste modes go off. TBC 3 plus one HTS every eight columns reproduces `screen_reset_tabs`, a scroll-up sized to the used visible rows reproduces `grid_view_clear_history`, DECSC after the final home mirrors `input_reset_cell`'s `old_cx = old_cy = 0`, and OSC 104, 110, 111, and 112 reproduce `colour_palette_clear`. Measured against the pin on 2026-09-01 with a 20x6 pane printing twenty lines: history_size goes 15 to 20, the cursor lands at 0,0, `capture-pane -S -` still holds L01 through L20 followed by six blank rows, a custom tab stop at column 4 goes back to the default 8, and a pane whose scroll region was narrowed scrolls the full screen again afterwards.
