Four zz-terminal tests assert each of those; a fifth, `pane_reset_drops_the_modes_the_pin_clears_with_send_keys_r`, asserts the pin's mode numbers (`keypad_cursor_flag` 1 to 0 so Up encodes `ESC[A`, `insert_flag` 1 to 0 so `ab\rX` captures `Xb`, the extended-key state dropped so Escape encodes a bare ESC, and the saved cursor back at 0,0), which the differential cannot see because zz's `keypad_cursor_flag`, `insert_flag`, and `origin_flag` formats are constant zero; and `send_keys_reset_runs_before_the_requested_key_delivery` asserts the command shape the pin's exec has: `-R` alone resets and sends nothing, `-R` with strings resets and then injects exactly what a bare `send-keys` would, and `-X` returns before the `-R` block ever runs. The differential scenario `send-keys-reset` runs the whole thing against the pin and is clean on all six axes at strict geometry. One qualification the acceptance did not name: the pin's clear runs through `screen_write_clearscreen`, so it only pushes into history because `scroll-on-clear` defaults on; zz reproduces that default unconditionally because the option itself is parked in `options.pane-engine-knobs`, which is where turning it off belongs. One mode survives by design: the pin keeps `MODE_KEYS_EXTENDED` when `extended-keys` is `always`, and zz drops it unconditionally because that option lives in `options.client-terminal-negotiation`. The redraw the acceptance names is the Content snapshot the terminal worker publishes after the reset; the pin's `PANE_STYLECHANGED` and `PANE_THEMECHANGED` flags have no observable effect after its own mode reset clears `MODE_THEME_UPDATES`, so nothing models them. `-R` reaches terminal panes only: zz-only browser, picker, agent, and editor panes have no pin equivalent and are skipped. Nothing wire-reachable changed: the reset rides an internal MuxEffect and a terminal worker command, not a protocol message.

closed.title: Apply bind-key command-or-string argument parsing
closed.resolution: Protocol v84 lexical command-block positions now drive `bind-key`'s pinned command-or-string rule without another wire change. Every positional accepts a string or typed block while `-T` and `-N` remain string-only, option scanning stops at the first positional or `--`, exact typed and string tails take their distinct construction paths, and typed command-name groups are omitted from variadic chains. Typed keys expand the live mux environment and use recursive canonical printing before key validation. Daemon dispatch stops the failed source group but continues later physical groups, while a string tail remains one group. Empty blocks, the pin's typed-first variadic oddity, aliases, nested callbacks, multiline groups, exact diagnostics, Control framing, and prior-binding preservation were covered by the initial 16-check source-file and Control fixture. The later `tracker.key-binding-behavior` closure grew it to 17 checks and closed bare key-only mutation. Eager whole-file validation, parse-only `source-file -n`, same-source alias creation, and nested user-alias suppression remain with their existing parser and alias owners.

closed.title: Apply choose-buffer command-or-string argument parsing
closed.resolution: Protocol v84 lexical command-block positions now drive `choose-buffer`'s pinned command-or-string rule without another wire change. The command accepts zero or one template positional as a string or typed block, while `-F`, `-f`, `-K`, `-O`, and `-t` values remain strings. Every typed child constructs before parent type, arity, target, or effects. Command preparation constructs and serializes a typed template before the chooser opens, using ` ; ` inside a physical group and ` ;; ` between groups; a quoted template remains raw. Selection parses the resulting text against the current alias table, so typed aliases retain their earlier construction while string aliases observe later changes. The daemon closes the overlay, confirms that the selected buffer still exists, substitutes its exact name for the first `%%` and every `%1` with the pin's trailing-percent quoting, and executes in the invoking client's live context. Parse and command errors reach the attached client with an uppercase first character. An empty buffer store opens no chooser and runs no custom action; a buffer removed after opening closes the stale chooser without running its template. The focused three-step, 26-check differential reports zero TOPO, GEO, FMT, OUT, and WARN differences; both sides set `ARGS_PARSE_CHOOSERS=clean:26`. It covers typed and string alias timing, exact substitution and quoting, attached selection, uppercase parse and runtime errors, close ordering, empty-store behavior, and direct plus stored arity precedence over recognized parked flags. `-F`, `-k`, and `-y`, tagging and editor behavior, broader chooser presentation, eager whole-source construction, same-source alias mutation, generic alias recursion, and raw-TUI overlay parity retain their existing owners.

closed.title: Apply choose-tree command-or-string argument parsing
closed.resolution: Protocol v84 lexical command-block positions now drive `choose-tree`'s pinned command-or-string rule without another wire change. The command accepts zero or one template positional as a string or typed block, while `-F`, `-f`, `-K`, `-O`, and `-t` values remain strings. Every typed child constructs before parent type, arity, target, or effects. Command preparation constructs and serializes a typed template before the chooser opens, preserving ` ; ` and ` ;; ` group boundaries; a quoted template remains raw until selection. The daemon closes the overlay, substitutes the selected session as `=name:`, window as `=name:index.`, or pane as `=name:index.%id`, then parses the resulting text against the current alias table. Typed aliases retain their earlier construction, while string aliases observe later changes. The selected row supplies the replacement string without retargeting execution; the action keeps the invoking client's live session, window, and pane context. Parse and command errors reach the attached client with an uppercase first character. The focused three-step, 26-check differential reports zero TOPO, GEO, FMT, OUT, and WARN differences; both sides set `ARGS_PARSE_CHOOSERS=clean:26`. It covers typed and string timing, exact substitution, live source-context execution, attached selection, error delivery, close ordering, and direct plus stored arity precedence over recognized parked flags; mux and daemon tests cover every target spelling and physical-group serialization. `-F`, `-G`, `-h`, `-k`, and `-y`, tagging, previews, kill and swap actions, broader chooser presentation, eager whole-source construction, same-source alias mutation, generic alias recursion, and raw-TUI overlay parity retain their existing owners.

closed.title: Apply command-prompt command-or-string argument parsing
closed.resolution: Protocol v84 lexical command-block positions now drive `command-prompt`'s pinned command-or-string rule without another wire change. The command accepts zero or one template positional as a string or typed block, while `-I`, `-p`, `-t`, and `-T` values remain strings. Every lexical typed block constructs recursively before its parent command's name, callback type, or arity validation. A typed template retains that frozen constructed list through submission; a string template retains raw source and constructs after answer substitution against the then-current alias table. Recursive paths carry independent one-layer user-alias budgets, while an outer alias-produced subtree disables another user alias. Typed substitution edits structured leaf arguments without reparsing answer text, preventing quote or semicolon injection. String substitution runs against the raw template before parsing, then preflights the complete parsed result before any command executes. Both paths replace the first `%%` and every `%1`; a trailing `%` quotes `"`, `\`, `$`, `;`, and `~` in the inserted answer. Typed callbacks retain physical source groups, stopping the failed group while continuing later physical lines. String templates and free input form one group. String-template diagnostics retain the originating source path and line after substitution. Empty typed templates execute no commands. The strict three-step scenario drives a real attached client and runs 43 internal type, precedence, readback, alias, substitution, injection, group, source-file, and exact Control checks. Prompt chaining and multi-answer `%2`, format and target flags, labels, key spelling, pass order, vi editing, and freeze behavior retain their existing prompt owners. Eager whole-file source construction and broader replay placement remain with the parser and command-chain owners. Five implemented callback commands across three effective rules remain under `tracker.semantic-coverage`.

closed.title: Apply confirm-before command-or-string argument parsing
closed.resolution: Protocol v84 lexical command-block positions now drive `confirm-before`'s pinned command-or-string rule without another wire change. The single command positional accepts a string or typed block while `-c`, `-p`, and `-t` values remain strings, and option scanning stops at the first positional or `--`. Every lexical typed block is recursively constructed before its parent command's name, callback type, or arity validation. Each recursive path carries one user-alias layer independently from siblings; a subtree produced by a user alias disables further user-alias expansion, and self-recursion fails as unknown without killing the daemon. Nested `if-shell`, `run-shell`, set-option, and `confirm-before` blocks print normalized names; an empty block reads back as `{  }`, and physical internal group newlines print as ` ;; `. A typed confirm callback executes that frozen constructed list without another user-alias lookup. String children construct after target lookup and parent-format expansion as one physical group, then remain frozen with the prompt. Source-file and Control comparisons are exact, nested bind and confirm failures are preflight parse errors, and a rejected replacement preserves the prior binding. The strict three-step scenario runs 19 internal construction, parser, readback, alias, and channel checks. Reply, `-y` Enter-default, blocking, and background execution initially had daemon and GPUI unit coverage. Raw-TUI confirmation handling later closed under `clients.tui-confirm-before-overlay`, and menu descriptor consumption later closed under `clients.tui-display-menu-overlay`; popup consumption later closed under `clients.tui-display-popup-overlay`. Broader eager whole-file source construction and its replay-channel placement remain open under the existing parser and command-chain owners. Six implemented callback commands across three effective rules remain under `tracker.semantic-coverage`.

closed.title: Apply display-menu item argument parsing
closed.resolution: Protocol v84 lexical command-block positions now drive `display-menu`'s pinned item rule without another wire change. The parser walks positional data as repeated NAME, KEY, and ACTION fields. A nonempty NAME advances through a string KEY to an ACTION, which accepts a string or typed block and resets the state to NAME. An empty NAME is a separator that consumes no KEY or ACTION and leaves the parser expecting another NAME. Values for `-b`, `-c`, `-C`, `-H`, `-s`, `-S`, `-t`, `-T`, `-x`, and `-y` remain strings. Every lexical typed block constructs before the parent callback type, arity, or effects, so child construction failures precede forbidden NAME, KEY, and option-value type errors. Accepted typed actions print recursively constructed command names in stored binding readback, while quoted brace actions remain strings.
